entries.text: Section 9: Observability This section defines metrics, logs, traces, spans, alerts, alert rules, incidents, and health checks. Overview The Observability section provides comprehensive monitoring, logging, tracing, and alerting capabilities to understand system behavior and health. The Three Pillars of Observability 1. Metrics Numerical measurements over time 2. Logs Discrete events with timestamp and context 3. Traces Request flows through distributed systems Core Concepts Metric Definition: A quantitative measurement over time. Key Attributes: - metric_type: COUNTER, GAUGE, HISTOGRAM, SUMMARY - unit: Unit of measurement (seconds, bytes, requests, etc.) - labels: Metric labels for dimensionality Relationships: - metric_emitted_by_component: Component emitting this metric - monitored_by_alert_rules: AlertRule entities monitoring this metric Metric Types: COUNTER Monotonically increasing value (only goes up). - Examples: total_requests, errors_total, bytes_sent - Use Case: Cumulative counts, rates can be calculated GAUGE Value that can increase or decrease. - Examples: cpu_usage, memory_usage, queue_depth, active_connections - Use Case: Current state, resource utilization HISTOGRAM Distribution of values in buckets. - Examples: request_duration_seconds, response_size_bytes - Use Case: Percentiles, distributions - Buckets: Pre-defined ranges (0-10ms, 10-50ms, 50-100ms, etc.) SUMMARY Summary statistics (quantiles). - Examples: request_duration_seconds (with p50, p95, p99) - Use Case: Percentiles without pre-defined buckets - Trade-off: More accurate percentiles, higher overhead Metric Naming Conventions: - Use descriptive names: http_requests_total, not requests - Include unit in name: request_duration_seconds, memory_bytes - Use labels for dimensions: {method="GET", status="200"} Key Metrics to Track: - RED Metrics (Requests, Errors, Duration): - Request rate - Error rate - Duration (latency) - USE Metrics (Utilization, Saturation, Errors): - Resource utilization (CPU, memory, disk) - Saturation (queue depth, load) - Error counts - Golden Signals: - Latency - Traffic - Errors - Saturation Log Definition: A timestamped record of discrete events. Key Attributes: - log_type: APPLICATION, ACCESS, ERROR, SECURITY, AUDIT, DEBUG - log_entries: List of LogEntry records (inverse: entry_in_log) Relationships: - log_governed_by_retention: RetentionPolicy for log retention Log Types: - APPLICATION: Application-level logs (info, warnings) - ACCESS: HTTP access logs, API requests - ERROR: Errors and exceptions - SECURITY: Security-related events (auth, access control) - AUDIT: Compliance and audit trail (see Section 6) - DEBUG: Detailed debugging information Structured Logging: Use structured formats (JSON) instead of plain text: { "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:45Z", "level": "ERROR", "service": "order-service", "trace_id": "abc123", "user_id": "user_456", "message": "Payment processing failed", "error": "InsufficientFunds", "amount": 99.99 } Log Levels: - TRACE: Very detailed, typically disabled - DEBUG: Detailed information for debugging - INFO: General informational messages - WARN: Warning messages, potential issues - ERROR: Error messages, failures - FATAL: Critical errors causing shutdown LogEntry Definition: A single record within a log. Class: is_a: NamedEntity (not Log). In SAO v2.0, LogEntry was changed from a subclass of Log to a subclass of NamedEntity, with an explicit relationship back to its parent Log. Key Attributes: - timestamp: When the event occurred - level: Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) - message: Log message - context: Additional context (trace ID, user ID, etc.) - entry_in_log: The Log this entry belongs to (range: Log, inverse: contains_entries) Best Practices: 1. Correlation IDs: Include trace/request ID in all logs 2. Structured Data: Use structured logging (JSON) 3. Contextual Information: Include relevant context 4. Avoid PII: Don't log sensitive personal information 5. Appropriate Levels: Use correct log levels Trace Definition: A causal chain of operations across services. Purpose: Track requests as they flow through distributed systems. Key Attributes: - trace_id: Unique identifier for the entire trace - trace_spans: List of Span entities representing operations (inverse: belongs_to_trace) Relationships: - starts_with_span: Root Span of the trace Distributed Tracing: - Track requests across multiple services - Identify bottlenecks and latency sources - Understand service dependencies - Debug distributed systems Trace Context Propagation: - W3C Trace Context standard - Propagate trace_id and span_id in headers - Maintain parent-child relationships Span Definition: A single unit of work within a trace. Class: is_a: NamedEntity (not Trace). In SAO v2.0, Span was changed from a subclass of Trace to a subclass of NamedEntity, with an explicit relationship back to its parent Trace. Key Attributes: - span_id: Unique identifier for this span - operation_name: Name of the operation - start_time: Operation start timestamp - end_time: Operation end timestamp - status: Span status (OK, ERROR, etc.) - attributes: Key-value pairs with additional context - belongs_to_trace: The Trace this span belongs to (range: Trace, inverse: contains_spans) Relationships: - child_of_span: Parent span (for nested operations) - parent_of_spans: Child spans - root_of_trace: Trace this is the root span of Span Attributes: - HTTP method, URL, status code - Database query, table name - Error messages - Custom business context Example Trace Structure: Trace: Process Order Span 1: HTTP POST /orders (200ms) Span 2: Validate Order (10ms) Span 3: Reserve Inventory (50ms) Span 4: Database Query (30ms) Span 5: Process Payment (100ms) Span 6: External API Call to Stripe (90ms) Span 7: Create Shipment (40ms) Alert Definition: A notification triggered by metric thresholds or anomalies. Key Attributes: - severity: Alert severity (critical, warning, info) - triggered_at: When alert was triggered - acknowledged_at: When alert was acknowledged - resolved_at: When issue was resolved Relationships: - triggered_by_rule: AlertRule that triggered this alert - escalates_to_incident: Incident if escalated Alert Severity Levels: - CRITICAL: Immediate action required, service down - WARNING: Requires attention, potential issues - INFO: Informational, awareness only Alert Best Practices: 1. Actionable: Alert only on actionable conditions 2. Context: Include enough context to diagnose 3. Deduplication: Deduplicate similar alerts 4. Routing: Route to appropriate team 5. Escalation: Escalate if not acknowledged AlertRule Definition: The condition that triggers an alert. Key Attributes: - condition: Alert condition expression (e.g., "error_rate > 5%") - threshold: Threshold value - duration_seconds: Duration before alerting (avoid flapping) - notification_channels: Where to send alerts (email, Slack, PagerDuty) Relationships: - monitors_metrics: Metric entities being monitored - triggers_alerts: Alert entities triggered Common Alert Rules: - High Error Rate: error_rate > 1% for 5 minutes - High Latency: p99_latency > 1s for 3 minutes - Low Availability: availability < 99.9% for 15 minutes - Resource Exhaustion: memory_usage > 90% for 10 minutes - Disk Space: disk_usage > 85% Alert Fatigue Prevention: - Set appropriate thresholds - Use duration to avoid flapping - Deduplicate similar alerts - Regular review and tuning - Auto-resolve when condition clears Incident Definition: A tracked degradation or outage event. Key Attributes: - severity: Incident severity (P1-P5 or SEV1-SEV5) - status: Current status (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved) - started_at: Incident start time - resolved_at: Resolution time - root_cause: Root cause analysis - postmortem_url: Link to incident postmortem Relationships: - escalated_from_alerts: Alert entities that led to incident - affects_services: Service entities impacted Incident Severity Levels: - P1/SEV1: Critical - Complete outage, all users affected - P2/SEV2: High - Major functionality impaired - P3/SEV3: Medium - Partial degradation - P4/SEV4: Low - Minor issues - P5/SEV5: Minimal - Cosmetic issues Incident Response Process: 1. Detection: Alert triggers or user report 2. Triage: Assess severity and impact 3. Investigation: Identify root cause 4. Mitigation: Implement fix or workaround 5. Resolution: Verify issue resolved 6. Postmortem: Document incident and learnings HealthCheck Definition: A probe verifying service availability. Key Attributes: - check_type: LIVENESS, READINESS, DEPENDENCY, STARTUP - endpoint: Health check endpoint URL - interval_seconds: Check frequency - timeout_seconds: Check timeout - success_threshold: Successes before marking healthy - failure_threshold: Failures before marking unhealthy Health Check Types: LIVENESS Determines if service is alive (should be restarted if failing). - Check: Basic process health - Example: /health/live returns 200 if process is running READINESS Determines if service can accept traffic. - Check: Dependencies available, ready to serve - Example: /health/ready returns 200 if DB is connected DEPENDENCY Check health of dependencies. - Check: Database, cache, external APIs - Example: Verify can connect to database STARTUP Probe during service initialization. - Check: Slow-starting containers - Example: Wait for warmup before liveness checks Health Check Implementation: GET /health/live Response: 200 OK { "status": "UP", "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:45Z" } GET /health/ready Response: 200 OK { "status": "UP", "checks": { "database": "UP", "cache": "UP", "external_api": "UP" } } Observability Patterns Correlation Use correlation IDs (trace IDs) across logs, metrics, and traces Link related events together Enable end-to-end request tracking Dashboards Real-time system health visibility Service-level indicators (SLIs) Business metrics Custom views for different teams Service Level Objectives (SLOs) Define target reliability levels SLI (Service Level Indicator): Measurement (e.g., latency) SLO (Service Level Objective): Target (e.g., p99 < 200ms) SLA (Service Level Agreement): Contract (e.g., 99.9% uptime) Error Budget: Allowed failures to meet SLO Synthetic Monitoring Proactive monitoring with synthetic transactions Simulate user workflows Detect issues before users Best Practices Metrics RED/USE/Golden Signals: Track key metrics Cardinality: Avoid high-cardinality labels Retention: Balance retention with storage costs Aggregation: Pre-aggregate when possible Consistency: Use consistent naming and labels Logs Structured Logging: Use JSON or structured format Correlation IDs: Include trace IDs Log Levels: Use appropriate levels Sensitive Data: Don't log PII, credentials Sampling: Sample high-volume logs Traces Sampling: Sample traces in high-traffic systems Span Names: Use meaningful operation names Attributes: Include relevant context Propagation: Propagate trace context across services Performance: Minimize tracing overhead Alerts Actionable: Only alert on actionable conditions Severity: Use appropriate severity levels Runbooks: Link to runbooks for resolution On-Call: Route to appropriate on-call team Retrospective: Review and tune alert rules SAO v2.0 Changes In SAO v2.0, relationship attributes that were previously modeled as standalone linkML relationship classes have been inlined directly into the domain classes. For example, Incident now carries escalated_from_alerts and affects_services as direct attributes, Alert carries escalates_to_incident, and AlertRule carries triggers_alerts. Additionally, LogEntry and Span were changed from subclasses of Log and Trace respectively to subclasses of NamedEntity, with explicit back-reference attributes (entry_in_log, belongs_to_trace) linking them to their parent entities. Relationships with Other Sections Section 1 (Structural Foundation): Components emit metrics and logs Section 5 (Behavior): Events generate logs Section 6 (Data Management): Logs subject to retention policies Section 7 (Integration): Integration metrics and traces Section 8 (Deployment): Deployment health checks Example: Observability for Order Service Metrics: - order_requests_total (COUNTER) Labels: method, status - order_processing_duration_seconds (HISTOGRAM) Buckets: 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0 - active_orders (GAUGE) - payment_failures_total (COUNTER) Logs: - Application Log (JSON structured) Level: INFO Message: "Order created" Trace ID: "abc123" Order ID: "order_456" Customer ID: "cust_789" - Error Log Level: ERROR Message: "Payment processing failed" Error: "InsufficientFunds" Stack Trace: ... Traces: Trace: Create Order Span: POST /api/orders (250ms) Span: Validate order (15ms) Span: Check inventory (40ms) Span: Process payment (150ms) Span: Stripe API call (130ms) Span: Create order record (30ms) Span: Emit OrderCreated event (15ms) Alerts: - High Error Rate Condition: order_error_rate > 5% for 5 minutes Severity: CRITICAL Notification: PagerDuty, Slack #alerts Runbook: https://wiki/runbooks/order-service-errors - High Latency Condition: order_p99_latency > 2s for 3 minutes Severity: WARNING Notification: Slack #alerts Health Checks: - Liveness: GET /health/live Interval: 10s Timeout: 1s Failure Threshold: 3 - Readiness: GET /health/ready Checks: Database, Cache, Payment Gateway Interval: 5s Timeout: 2s

entries.text: Section 10: Governance and Compliance This section defines compliance requirements, controls, evidence, and risk assessments. Overview The Governance and Compliance section provides frameworks for ensuring the system meets regulatory requirements, implements appropriate controls, and manages risks. Core Concepts ComplianceRequirement Definition: A regulatory or policy obligation. Purpose: Documents requirements from compliance frameworks that the system must satisfy. Key Attributes: - framework: Compliance framework (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2, PCI_DSS, ISO27001, SOX, CCPA, FEDRAMP) - controls: List of Control entities implementing this requirement - effective_date: When requirement became effective Relationships: - applies_to_systems: System entities that must comply Compliance Frameworks: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) European Union data protection and privacy regulation. - Key Requirements: - Lawful basis for processing - Data subject rights (access, erasure, portability) - Data minimization - Privacy by design - Breach notification (72 hours) HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) US healthcare data privacy and security regulation. - Key Requirements: - Protected Health Information (PHI) safeguards - Access controls and audit trails - Encryption of PHI - Business associate agreements - Breach notification SOC 2 (Service Organization Control 2) Security, availability, and confidentiality framework. - Trust Service Criteria: - Security - Availability - Processing Integrity - Confidentiality - Privacy PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) Credit card data security standard. - Key Requirements: - Secure network and systems - Protect cardholder data - Access control measures - Network monitoring - Security policy ISO 27001 Information security management system standard. - Key Requirements: - Risk assessment - Security controls (Annex A) - Management review - Continuous improvement - Documentation SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) US financial reporting and corporate governance regulation. - Key Requirements: - Internal controls for financial reporting - Audit trails - Segregation of duties - Change management CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act) California consumer privacy regulation. - Key Requirements: - Right to know what data is collected - Right to delete personal information - Right to opt-out of data sale - Non-discrimination FedRAMP (Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program) US federal cloud security program. - Key Requirements: - Security controls (based on NIST 800-53) - Continuous monitoring - Annual assessment - Incident response Control Definition: A measure implementing a compliance requirement. Purpose: Specific security or compliance controls implemented to satisfy requirements. Key Attributes: - control_id: Identifier (e.g., SOC2-CC6.1, ISO27001-A.9.2.1) - implementation: How control is implemented - evidence: List of Evidence entities demonstrating effectiveness - frequency: Assessment frequency (daily, monthly, quarterly, annual) Relationships: - owned_by_actor: Actor responsible for this control - mitigates_risks: RiskAssessment entities mitigated Control Types: Preventive Controls Prevent security incidents from occurring. - Examples: Access controls, encryption, firewalls, input validation Detective Controls Detect security incidents after they occur. - Examples: Logging, monitoring, intrusion detection, audits Corrective Controls Correct issues after detection. - Examples: Incident response, patching, backups, recovery procedures Administrative Controls Policies, procedures, and training. - Examples: Security policies, training programs, background checks Technical Controls Technology-based controls. - Examples: Encryption, authentication, firewalls, antivirus Physical Controls Physical security measures. - Examples: Locks, badges, surveillance, environmental controls Example Controls: SOC2 CC6.1 - Logical Access: - Control: Multi-factor authentication required for all administrative access - Implementation: Enforce MFA via identity provider for admin roles - Evidence: MFA enrollment reports, access logs showing MFA verification - Frequency: Quarterly review PCI-DSS 3.4 - Encryption of Cardholder Data: - Control: Encrypt cardholder data at rest using AES-256 - Implementation: Database-level encryption for payment_methods table - Evidence: Encryption configuration, key management logs - Frequency: Annual audit GDPR Article 32 - Security of Processing: - Control: Encryption of personal data in transit - Implementation: TLS 1.3 for all API endpoints - Evidence: SSL/TLS scan reports, certificate management logs - Frequency: Monthly scans Evidence Definition: Proof that a control is operating effectively. Purpose: Demonstrates to auditors that controls are implemented and effective. Key Attributes: - evidence_type: Type of evidence (screenshot, log export, test result, policy document) - collected_at: Collection timestamp - artifact_uri: Location of evidence artifact Relationships: - verified_by_actor: Actor who verified the evidence Types of Evidence: Screenshots Visual proof of configurations or settings. - Examples: Security group rules, MFA settings, encryption enabled Log Exports Extracted log files demonstrating control operation. - Examples: Access logs, authentication logs, change logs Test Results Results from automated or manual testing. - Examples: Vulnerability scans, penetration tests, security assessments Policy Documents Written policies and procedures. - Examples: Security policy, incident response plan, acceptable use policy Attestations Signed statements from responsible parties. - Examples: Background check confirmations, training completion certificates Automated Reports Reports from security tools and systems. - Examples: SIEM reports, compliance dashboards, configuration baselines Evidence Best Practices: 1. Automated Collection: Automate evidence collection when possible 2. Timestamping: Timestamp all evidence 3. Integrity: Protect evidence from tampering 4. Retention: Retain evidence per compliance requirements 5. Accessibility: Make evidence accessible for audits RiskAssessment Definition: An evaluation of threats and vulnerabilities. Purpose: Identify, analyze, and prioritize risks to the system. Key Attributes: - assessed_at: Assessment date - risk_level: Overall risk level (Low, Medium, High, Critical) - threats: List of identified threats - vulnerabilities: List of identified vulnerabilities - residual_risk: Remaining risk after mitigations Relationships: - mitigated_by_controls: Control entities mitigating risks - assesses_system: System being assessed Risk Assessment Process: Asset Identification Identify assets to protect (data, systems, services) Threat Identification Identify potential threats Internal threats (malicious insiders, human error) External threats (hackers, malware, DDoS) Environmental threats (natural disasters, power outages) Vulnerability Identification Identify weaknesses that threats could exploit Software vulnerabilities Misconfigurations Weak access controls Social engineering susceptibility Risk Analysis Assess likelihood and impact of each risk Likelihood: Probability of occurrence (Rare, Unlikely, Possible, Likely, Almost Certain) Impact: Consequences if realized (Insignificant, Minor, Moderate, Major, Catastrophic) Risk Level: Likelihood × Impact Risk Evaluation Determine which risks require treatment Accept: Accept low risks Mitigate: Implement controls to reduce risk Transfer: Transfer risk (insurance, outsourcing) Avoid: Eliminate risk-causing activities Control Implementation Implement controls to mitigate risks Residual Risk Assessment Assess remaining risk after controls Documentation Document assessment, decisions, and controls Risk Matrix Example: Impact → Catastrophic: L, M, H, C, C Major: L, M, H, H, C Moderate: L, M, M, H, H Minor: L, L, M, M, H Insignificant:L, L, L, M, M ↑ Likelihood Rare, Unlikely, Possible, Likely, Almost Certain L = Low risk M = Medium risk H = High risk C = Critical risk Example Risk Assessment: Risk: Unauthorized access to customer PII - Threat: External attacker exploiting weak authentication - Vulnerability: Single-factor authentication for user accounts - Likelihood: Likely (attacks are common) - Impact: Major (data breach, regulatory fines, reputation damage) - Risk Level: HIGH - Controls: - Implement multi-factor authentication - Enforce strong password policy - Monitor for suspicious login attempts - Encrypt PII at rest and in transit - Residual Risk: MEDIUM (controls reduce but don't eliminate risk) Governance Framework Policy Hierarchy Policies: High-level statements (Security Policy, Privacy Policy) Standards: Specific requirements (Password Standard, Encryption Standard) Procedures: Step-by-step instructions (Incident Response Procedure) Guidelines: Recommendations and best practices Roles and Responsibilities Chief Information Security Officer (CISO): Overall security responsibility Data Protection Officer (DPO): Privacy and data protection Compliance Officer: Regulatory compliance Control Owners: Responsible for specific controls Auditors: Independent verification Governance Processes Risk Management: Ongoing risk assessment and treatment Compliance Management: Track and demonstrate compliance Audit Management: Coordinate and respond to audits Incident Management: Handle security incidents Change Management: Control changes to systems and controls Best Practices Compliance Framework Mapping: Map requirements to controls Continuous Monitoring: Monitor controls continuously Regular Audits: Conduct internal audits Evidence Collection: Automate evidence collection Gap Analysis: Identify and address gaps Control Implementation Defense in Depth: Layer multiple controls Automation: Automate controls when possible Testing: Regularly test control effectiveness Documentation: Document all controls Ownership: Assign clear ownership Risk Management Regular Assessments: Conduct risk assessments regularly Threat Intelligence: Monitor emerging threats Vulnerability Management: Scan and remediate vulnerabilities Risk Register: Maintain centralized risk register Treatment Plans: Document risk treatment decisions Audit Readiness Continuous Evidence: Collect evidence continuously Documentation: Maintain complete documentation Mock Audits: Conduct internal mock audits Remediation: Address findings promptly Collaboration: Work cooperatively with auditors SAO v2.0 Changes In SAO v2.0, relationship attributes that were previously modeled as standalone linkML relationship classes have been inlined directly into the domain classes. For example, ComplianceRequirement now carries applies_to_systems as a direct attribute, Control carries mitigates_risks, and RiskAssessment carries assesses_system. This simplifies navigation and reduces the number of intermediate relationship entities. Relationships with Other Sections Section 1 (Structural Foundation): Systems must comply with requirements Section 2 (Actors and Identity): Controls owned by actors Section 3 (Authorization): Access controls implement security requirements Section 6 (Data Management): Data classification and retention for compliance Section 9 (Observability): Audit logs provide evidence Example: GDPR Compliance ComplianceRequirement: GDPR Article 32 - Security of Processing Framework: GDPR Effective Date: 2018-05-25 Controls: Control: Encryption of Personal Data ID: GDPR-32-ENC Implementation: AES-256 encryption for PII at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit Owner: CISO Evidence: - Database encryption configuration screenshot - SSL/TLS scan report (monthly) - Key management audit log Frequency: Monthly Control: Access Control to Personal Data ID: GDPR-32-AC Implementation: RBAC with least privilege, MFA for admin access Owner: Identity Team Lead Evidence: - Role definitions and assignments - MFA enforcement report - Access review logs (quarterly) Frequency: Quarterly Control: Regular Security Testing ID: GDPR-32-TEST Implementation: Quarterly penetration testing, monthly vulnerability scans Owner: Security Team Lead Evidence: - Penetration test reports - Vulnerability scan results - Remediation tracking Frequency: Quarterly (pen test), Monthly (vuln scan) RiskAssessment: GDPR Data Breach Risk Assessed At: 2024-01-15 Risk Level: MEDIUM Threats: - External attacker targeting customer PII - Insider threat (malicious employee) - Accidental data exposure (misconfiguration) Vulnerabilities: - Public S3 buckets (historical issue) - Insufficient logging of PII access Controls: - GDPR-32-ENC (Encryption) - GDPR-32-AC (Access Control) - GDPR-32-TEST (Security Testing) - Automated S3 bucket policy enforcement - SIEM monitoring for PII access Residual Risk: LOW Risk Treatment: - Accept residual risk - Review quarterly - Cyber insurance policy covers data breach costs

entries.text: Code Structure The Code Structure layer provides a paradigm-agnostic framework for modeling software systems at the implementation level. This layer bridges the gap between architectural concepts (Components, Operations) and the actual source code that implements them, supporting both modern and legacy systems. v2.0 Note: In SAO v2.0, all single-use relationship slots have been inlined as class attributes on their owning classes. Only approximately 20 multi-domain slots remain as global relationships: defined_in_container, contained_in_unit, contains_data_elements, implements_component, implemented_by_code, annotates_element, annotated_by, affects_behavior_of, imports_symbols, and imported_via. Overview The code structure model consists of three main levels: Physical Structure - Storage and organization of code files Logical Structure - Encapsulation units, callable units, and data structures Semantic Structure - Control flow, data flow, and code semantics This design principle ensures that a single ontology can represent: - Modern object-oriented systems (Java, Python, C#) - Procedural systems (C, Pascal, Fortran) - Functional systems (Haskell, OCaml, F#) - Mainframe systems (COBOL, PL/I, Assembler) - Database systems (SQL stored procedures, triggers) Design Philosophy: Paradigm Agnosticism Rather than creating separate classes for each programming paradigm (e.g., Class, Program, Module), this ontology uses type-based polymorphism: A single class (EncapsulationUnit) represents all forms of code grouping The encapsulation_type attribute specifies the paradigm-specific type Enumerations provide comprehensive coverage across all paradigms Example Mappings # Java class my_service: a: EncapsulationUnit name: UserService encapsulation_type: class visibility: public # COBOL program batch_job: a: EncapsulationUnit name: PAYROLL encapsulation_type: batch_program # Haskell module utils: a: EncapsulationUnit name: Utils encapsulation_type: module Physical Code Structure CodeContainer Represents the physical storage of source code - files, library members, or other storage units. Key Attributes: - container_path - Path or identifier for the container - container_type - Type of container (source_file, library_member, copybook, script, etc.) - format - ~~Language or format (COBOL, Java, Python, SQL, etc.)~~ Deprecated in v2.0 — use written_in_language (range: ProgrammingLanguage) instead - written_in_language - (v2.0) ProgrammingLanguage relationship replacing format - size_bytes - Size in bytes - line_count - Number of lines - encoding - Character encoding - checksum - Content hash for version tracking - has_file_definitions - (v2.0) FileDefinition[] associated with this container - has_screen_definitions - (v2.0) ScreenDefinition[] associated with this container - has_preprocessor_directives - (v2.0) PreprocessorDirective[] associated with this container Container Types: - source_file - Standard source code file - library_member - Member of a partitioned dataset or library (mainframe) - include_file - Header or include file - script - Executable script - configuration - Configuration file - schema_definition - Database or API schema - notebook_cell - Jupyter notebook cell - inline_code - Embedded code (JavaScript in HTML, SQL in application) - jcl_member - (v2.0) JCL member - rpg_source - (v2.0) RPG source member - pli_source - (v2.0) PL/I source member - assembler_source - (v2.0) Assembler source member - cl_source - (v2.0) CL (Control Language) source member Example: user_service_file: a: CodeContainer container_path: /src/services/UserService.java container_type: source_file format: Java line_count: 450 encoding: UTF-8 StorageLocation Represents a logical or physical location for storing code containers. Key Attributes: - location_path - Path or identifier - location_type - Type (directory, library, package, namespace, module_path) Location Types: - directory - Filesystem directory - library - Partitioned dataset (mainframe) or static library - package - Language package or module - namespace - Logical namespace - module_path - Module search path Relationships: - has_parent_location - Parent storage location (hierarchical) - contains_locations - Child storage locations - contains_containers - Code containers in this location - maps_to_module - Corresponding architectural Module Example: services_directory: a: StorageLocation location_path: /src/services location_type: directory maps_to_module: user_management_module cobol_library: a: StorageLocation location_path: SYS1.COBLIB location_type: library Logical Code Structure EncapsulationUnit A logical boundary that groups related code and data. This is the cornerstone of the paradigm-agnostic design. Key Attributes: - encapsulation_type - Required. The paradigm-specific type (see EncapsulationType enum) - visibility - Visibility level (public, private, protected, internal, package) - qualified_name - Fully qualified name (e.g., com.example.UserService) - stereotype - Additional stereotype (Service, Repository, DTO, Controller, etc.) - is_abstract - Whether this is abstract/incomplete - is_final - Whether this can be extended - error_model_for_module - (v2.0) ErrorModel associated with this unit - screen_used_by_programs - (v2.0) ScreenDefinition[] used by this unit - has_outgoing_ipc_connections - (v2.0) IPCConnection[] originating from this unit - has_incoming_ipc_connections - (v2.0) IPCConnection[] targeting this unit - affected_by_directives - (v2.0) PreprocessorDirective[] affecting this unit - memory_model_for_module - (v2.0) MemoryModel associated with this unit - executed_by_job_steps - (v2.0) JobStep[] that execute this unit EncapsulationType Values (33 total): Object-Oriented: - class - Standard OOP class - interface - Interface/contract definition - abstract_class - Abstract base class - trait - Trait (Rust, Scala) or mixin - enum_class - Enumeration class - record_class - Immutable record (Java, C#) - singleton - Singleton pattern Procedural: - program - Standalone program - subprogram - Subprogram or subroutine module - unit - Pascal/Ada unit Functional: - module - Functional module (Haskell, OCaml, F#) - namespace - Namespace grouping - package - Package grouping - library - Library module Mainframe: - batch_program - Batch processing program - online_program - Online transaction program (CICS, IMS) - copybook - COBOL copybook - rpg_module - (v2.0) RPG module - rpg_service_program - (v2.0) RPG service program - pli_procedure - (v2.0) PL/I external procedure - pli_package - (v2.0) PL/I package - assembler_csect - (v2.0) Assembler control section (CSECT) Database: - stored_procedure - Database stored procedure package - function_package - Function package (Oracle) - trigger - Database trigger - view - Database view Other: - object - JavaScript/prototype-based object - component - Component definition - service - Service class - controller - Controller class - script - Script module - composite - Composite structure - other - Other types Relationships: - defined_in_container - Code container where this is defined - contains_callable_units - Callable units (methods, functions, etc.) in this unit - contains_data_structures - Data structures in this unit - contains_data_elements - Data elements (fields, variables) in this unit - extends_units - Units this extends/inherits from - implements_contracts - Contracts (interfaces) this implements - uses_definitions - Definition references (imports, includes) used - implements_component - Architectural Component this implements Example - Java Class: user_service: a: EncapsulationUnit name: UserService encapsulation_type: class visibility: public stereotype: Service qualified_name: com.example.services.UserService implements_component: user_management_component Example - COBOL Program: payroll_batch: a: EncapsulationUnit name: PAYROLL encapsulation_type: batch_program qualified_name: PAYROLL defined_in_container: payroll_source CallableUnit A named, invocable unit of code - the paradigm-agnostic representation of functions, methods, procedures, etc. Key Attributes: - callable_type - Required. The paradigm-specific type (see CallableType enum) - visibility - Visibility level - return_type - Return type (if applicable) - is_async - Whether this is asynchronous - is_pure - Whether this is a pure function (no side effects) - is_static - Whether this is static - is_virtual - Whether this is virtual/overridable - complexity_score - Cyclomatic complexity or similar metric - entry_point_type - If this is an entry point (main, constructor, handler, etc.) - has_return_type - (v2.0) TypeExpression for the return type - uses_file_definitions - (v2.0) FileDefinition[] used by this callable - has_file_operations - (v2.0) FileOperation[] performed by this callable - callable_affected_by_directives - (v2.0) PreprocessorDirective[] affecting this callable CallableType Values (53 total): Object-Oriented Methods: - method - Instance method - static_method - Static/class method - constructor - Object constructor - destructor - Object destructor - property_getter - Property getter - property_setter - Property setter - operator_overload - Operator overloading - conversion_operator - Type conversion operator - indexer - Indexer/subscript operator - abstract_method - Abstract method declaration - virtual_method - Virtual/overridable method Procedural: - function - Function (procedural or functional) - procedure - Procedure/subroutine - subroutine - Subroutine - paragraph - COBOL paragraph - section - COBOL section - rpg_subprocedure - (v2.0) RPG subprocedure - pli_entry - (v2.0) PL/I entry point - assembler_entry - (v2.0) Assembler entry point - rpg_subroutine - (v2.0) RPG subroutine Functional: - lambda - Anonymous lambda function - closure - Closure - higher_order_function - Higher-order function - curried_function - Curried function - functor - Functor Event Handling: - event_handler - Event handler - callback - Callback function - delegate - Delegate - signal_handler - Signal handler Database: - stored_procedure - Database stored procedure - stored_function - Database function - trigger_body - Trigger implementation - cursor - Database cursor Concurrency: - coroutine - Coroutine - generator - Generator function - async_function - Async function - thread_entry - Thread entry point - task - Task/future Testing: - test_case - Test case - test_fixture - Test fixture/setup - mock - Mock function Other: - macro - Preprocessor macro - template - Template/generic function - generic_method - Generic method - main_entry - Main entry point - interrupt_handler - Interrupt handler - exception_handler - Exception handler - finalizer - Finalizer/cleanup - factory_method - Factory method - extension_method - Extension method - script_function - Script function - command - Command/action - other - Other types Relationships: - contained_in_unit - Encapsulation unit containing this callable - has_parameters - Parameters of this callable - invokes_callables - Other callables invoked by this one - accesses_data_elements - Data elements accessed (read) - modifies_data_elements - Data elements modified (written) - raises_exceptions - ~~Exceptions that may be raised~~ Deprecated in v2.0 — use raises_exception_types (ExceptionType[]) instead - handles_exceptions - ~~Exceptions handled~~ Deprecated in v2.0 — use handles_exception_types (ExceptionType[]) instead - raises_exception_types - (v2.0) ExceptionType[] that may be raised - handles_exception_types - (v2.0) ExceptionType[] that are handled - overrides_callable - Callable in parent this overrides - implements_operation - Architectural Operation this implements Example - Java Method: create_user: a: CallableUnit name: createUser callable_type: method visibility: public return_type: User complexity_score: 8 contained_in_unit: user_service implements_operation: create_user_operation Example - COBOL Paragraph: calculate_totals: a: CallableUnit name: CALCULATE-TOTALS callable_type: paragraph contained_in_unit: payroll_batch DataStructure Represents organized data storage - the paradigm-agnostic representation of classes, records, structs, etc. Key Attributes: - structure_type - Required. The paradigm-specific type (see DataStructureType enum) - nesting_level - Nesting depth (for hierarchical structures like COBOL) - is_mutable - Whether data can be modified - is_serializable - Whether this can be serialized - persistence_type - How this is persisted (transient, database, file, memory, cache) - passed_via_ipc - (v2.0) IPCConnection[] through which this structure is passed DataStructureType Values (50 total): Object-Oriented: - class_data - Data members of a class - inner_class - Inner/nested class - anonymous_class - Anonymous class Procedural: - struct - C/C++ struct - record - Pascal/Ada record or COBOL record - union - C union COBOL: - group_item - COBOL group item (composite data) - copybook_structure - COBOL copybook structure - commarea - CICS communication area - rpg_data_structure - (v2.0) RPG data structure - pli_structure - (v2.0) PL/I structure - assembler_dsect - (v2.0) Assembler DSECT - cobol_file_descriptor - (v2.0) COBOL file descriptor (FD) Functional: - algebraic_data_type - ADT (Haskell, ML) - type_class - Type class - product_type - Product type (tuple-like) - sum_type - Sum/variant type Collections: - array - Fixed-size array - dynamic_array - Dynamic array - list - List structure - dictionary - Dictionary/map/hash - set - Set structure - queue - Queue - stack - Stack - tree - Tree structure - graph - Graph structure Database: - table_structure - Database table structure - view_structure - Database view structure - cursor_structure - Cursor structure - rowtype - Database row type Domain-Driven Design: - value_object - DDD value object - dto - Data Transfer Object Other: - tuple - Tuple - pair - Key-value pair - enum - Enumeration - flags - Bit flags - configuration_object - Configuration data - message - Message structure - event - Event data - command - Command data - json_schema - JSON schema structure - xml_schema - XML schema structure - protobuf_message - Protocol Buffers message - avro_record - Avro record - smart_pointer - Smart pointer wrapper - reference_wrapper - Reference wrapper Relationships: - contained_in_unit - Encapsulation unit containing this structure - contains_data_elements - Data elements in this structure - has_parent_structure - Parent structure (for nested structures) - has_child_structures - Child/nested structures - maps_to_domain_entity - Domain entity this maps to - maps_to_value_object - Value object this maps to - persisted_in_collection - Collection where this is persisted Example - Java Class Data: user_data: a: DataStructure name: UserData structure_type: class_data contained_in_unit: user_entity maps_to_domain_entity: user_entity Example - COBOL Group Item: employee_record: a: DataStructure name: EMPLOYEE-RECORD structure_type: group_item nesting_level: 1 contained_in_unit: payroll_copybook DataElement Individual data fields, variables, or constants. Key Attributes: - element_category - Category of element (field, static_field, local_variable, parameter, constant, global_variable, computed, temporary) - data_type - Data type (string, integer, User, etc.) — Deprecated for typed analysis in v2.0 — use declared_type (TypeExpression) instead - declared_type - (v2.0) TypeExpression for the declared type - visibility - Visibility level - is_constant - Whether this is a constant/immutable - is_nullable - Whether this can be null - default_value - Default value - has_ownership_annotations - (v2.0) OwnershipAnnotation[] for this element - mapped_from_screen_fields - (v2.0) ScreenField[] mapped to this element Relationships: - contained_in_unit - Encapsulation unit containing this element - contained_in_structure - Data structure containing this element - has_parent_element - Parent element (for nested fields) - has_type_definition - Type definition reference Example: user_email: a: DataElement name: email element_category: field data_type: String visibility: private is_nullable: false contained_in_structure: user_data Parameter Function/method parameter. Key Attributes: - direction - Direction (range: ParameterDirection): input, output, input_output, return - position - Position in parameter list - passing_mechanism - How passed (by_value, by_reference, by_name, by_result) Example: username_param: a: Parameter name: username direction: input data_type: String position: 1 parameter_of: create_user Semantic Code Structure CodeBlock A logical block of code (conditional, loop, try-catch, etc.). Key Attributes: - block_type - Type (sequential, conditional, loop, try_catch, transaction, critical_section, scope) Statement Individual code statement. Key Attributes: - statement_category - Category (declaration, assignment, invocation, control_transfer, io_operation, data_manipulation, transaction_control, exception_handling) - line_number - Source line number ControlFlow Control flow between code elements (calls, branches, etc.). Key Attributes: - flow_type - Type (call, async_call, branch, jump, return, throw, yield) - is_conditional - Whether flow is conditional - condition - Condition expression Relationships: - has_source_callable - Source callable - has_target_callable - Target callable - has_source_statement - Source statement - has_target_statement - Target statement DataFlow Data flow between elements. Key Attributes: - flow_type - Type (read, write, modify, define, use) Relationships: - has_source_element - Source data element - has_target_element - Target data element Mapping to Architecture The code structure model integrates with the architectural model: Component Implementation user_service_component: a: Component name: UserManagement user_service_class: a: EncapsulationUnit encapsulation_type: class implements_component: user_service_component user_repository_class: a: EncapsulationUnit encapsulation_type: class implements_component: user_service_component Operation Implementation create_user_op: a: Operation name: CreateUser create_user_method: a: CallableUnit callable_type: method implements_operation: create_user_op Domain Entity Mapping user_entity: a: DomainEntity name: User user_class: a: EncapsulationUnit encapsulation_type: class user_data_structure: a: DataStructure structure_type: class_data maps_to_domain_entity: user_entity Cross-Paradigm Examples Modern Java Microservice # File user_service_file: a: CodeContainer container_path: /src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java container_type: source_file format: Java # Class user_service: a: EncapsulationUnit name: UserService encapsulation_type: class visibility: public stereotype: Service defined_in_container: user_service_file # Method create_user: a: CallableUnit name: createUser callable_type: method visibility: public return_type: User contained_in_unit: user_service COBOL Mainframe Application # Library Member payroll_source: a: CodeContainer container_path: SYS1.COBLIB(PAYROLL) container_type: library_member format: COBOL # Program payroll_program: a: EncapsulationUnit name: PAYROLL encapsulation_type: batch_program defined_in_container: payroll_source # Paragraph calculate_pay: a: CallableUnit name: CALCULATE-PAY callable_type: paragraph contained_in_unit: payroll_program # Copybook employee_copybook: a: CodeContainer container_path: SYS1.COPYLIB(EMPLOYEE) container_type: library_member format: COBOL employee_structure: a: EncapsulationUnit name: EMPLOYEE-RECORD encapsulation_type: copybook defined_in_container: employee_copybook # Group Item employee_data: a: DataStructure name: EMPLOYEE-RECORD structure_type: group_item nesting_level: 1 contained_in_unit: employee_structure Python Script # File data_processor_file: a: CodeContainer container_path: /scripts/process_data.py container_type: script format: Python # Module data_processor: a: EncapsulationUnit name: process_data encapsulation_type: module defined_in_container: data_processor_file # Function process_records: a: CallableUnit name: process_records callable_type: function is_async: true contained_in_unit: data_processor SQL Stored Procedure # Database Object update_inventory_proc: a: EncapsulationUnit name: update_inventory encapsulation_type: stored_procedure # Procedure Body update_inventory_impl: a: CallableUnit name: update_inventory callable_type: stored_procedure contained_in_unit: update_inventory_proc Supporting Enumerations Additional Type Enumerations VisibilityType: public, private, protected, internal, package CallableCategory: normal, operator, main_entry (v2.0 — cleaned to 3 values) EntryPointType: main_program, transaction_entry, event_handler, scheduled_entry, api_endpoint DataStructureCategory: composite, collection, hierarchical, value_type, reference_type, union DataElementCategory: field, static_field, local_variable, parameter, constant, global_variable, computed, temporary ParameterDirection: input, output, input_output, return PassingMechanism: by_value, by_reference, by_name, by_result CodeBlockType: sequential, conditional, loop, try_catch, transaction, critical_section, scope StatementCategory: declaration, assignment, invocation, control_transfer, io_operation, data_manipulation, transaction_control, exception_handling ReferenceType: import_module, import_symbol, include_source, inherit, implement ControlFlowType: call, async_call, branch, jump, return, throw, yield DataFlowType: read, write, modify, define, use Usage Patterns Tracing Implementation Trace from architectural concept to implementation: # Find all code implementing a Component SELECT ?code ?type WHERE { ?code sao:implements_component :user_management_component . ?code sao:encapsulation_type ?type . } Call Graph Analysis # Find call chains SELECT ?caller ?callee WHERE { ?flow a sao:ControlFlow ; sao:flow_type "call" ; sao:source_callable ?caller ; sao:target_callable ?callee . } Cross-Reference Analysis # Find all places a function is called SELECT ?caller WHERE { ?flow a sao:ControlFlow ; sao:target_callable :create_user_method ; sao:source_callable ?caller . } Best Practices Use Qualified Names: Always provide qualified_name for encapsulation units Link to Architecture: Connect code to Components and Operations via implements_component and implements_operation Track Dependencies: Use DefinitionReference to model imports/includes Model Call Graphs: Use ControlFlow to represent invocation relationships Map Data: Connect DataStructures to DomainEntities via maps_to_domain_entity Specify Types Precisely: Use the most specific type enum value available Document Visibility: Always specify visibility for encapsulation units and callables Track Complexity: Record complexity metrics for callables to support quality analysis Integration with Other Layers Structural Foundation: CodeContainers map to Modules, EncapsulationUnits implement Components Domain Modeling: DataStructures map to DomainEntities and ValueObjects Behavior: CallableUnits implement Operations and participate in Workflows Data Management: DataStructures are persisted in Collections Integration: EncapsulationUnits may expose or consume Interfaces New Sections in v2.0 The following sections were introduced in SAO v2.0 to support advanced type modeling, error handling, file I/O, screen interaction, batch orchestration, inter-process communication, preprocessor/metaprogramming, memory/ownership models, database schema objects, and programming language metadata. Type System Modeling (Section 18) TypeExpression (is_a NamedEntity) A recursive type model capable of representing generics, unions, pointers, and function types. Key Attributes: - type_kind - TypeKind (e.g., primitive, generic, union, pointer, function_type, array) - base_type - Base type name or reference - has_type_parameters - TypeExpression[] (self-referential, multivalued) for generic parameters - type_constraints - Constraints on type parameters - is_nullable - Whether this type is nullable - nullability_model - Nullability model (e.g., optional, nullable_reference, maybe) - pointer_semantics - Pointer semantics (e.g., raw, shared, unique, weak) Relationships: - Connected to DataElement via declared_type / type_of_data_elements - Connected to Parameter via has_type / type_of_parameters - Connected to CallableUnit via has_return_type / return_type_of_callables Error Handling Model (Section 19) ErrorModel (is_a NamedEntity) Describes the error handling strategy for a module or language. Key Attributes: - strategy - ErrorHandlingStrategy (e.g., exceptions, error_codes, result_type, condition_system) - checkedness - ExceptionCheckedness (e.g., checked, unchecked, mixed) Relationships: - Connected to EncapsulationUnit via error_model_for_module - Connected to ProgrammingLanguage ExceptionType (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a specific exception or error type in the exception hierarchy. Key Attributes: - qualified_name - Fully qualified exception class name - is_checked - Whether this is a checked exception - has_parent_exception - Parent ExceptionType in the hierarchy - has_child_exceptions - Child ExceptionType[] in the hierarchy Relationships: - Connected to CallableUnit via raises_exception_types / handles_exception_types File I/O Definitions (Section 20) FileDefinition (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a declared file or dataset used by a program. Key Attributes: - organization - FileOrganization (e.g., sequential, indexed, relative, vsam_ksds, vsam_rrds) - access_mode - FileAccessMode (e.g., sequential, random, dynamic) - record_format - RecordFormat (e.g., fixed, variable, undefined) - record_length - Record length - block_size - Block size - key_fields - Key field names - file_status_field - File status variable name - external_name - External dataset or file name Relationships: - Connected to CallableUnit via uses_file_definitions - Connected to CodeContainer via has_file_definitions - Connected to DataStore FileOperation (is_a NamedEntity) Represents an individual file I/O operation within code. Key Attributes: - operation_type - FileOperationType (e.g., open, close, read, write, rewrite, delete, start) - condition_handling - Condition or error handling for this operation Relationships: - Connected to FileDefinition - Connected to CallableUnit via has_file_operations Screen / Terminal Interaction (Section 21) ScreenDefinition (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a terminal screen or display definition (e.g., BMS map, DDS display file). Key Attributes: - screen_type - ScreenType (e.g., bms_map, dds_display, mfs_format, panel) - rows - Number of rows - columns - Number of columns - external_name - External map or screen name Relationships: - Connected to ScreenField (contains fields) - Connected to EncapsulationUnit via screen_used_by_programs - Connected to CodeContainer via has_screen_definitions ScreenField (is_a NamedEntity) Represents an individual field on a screen definition. Key Attributes: - row - Row position - column - Column position - length - Field length - is_input - Whether this field accepts input - is_protected - Whether this field is protected - attribute_byte - Display attribute byte - initial_value - Initial/default value Relationships: - Connected to ScreenDefinition - Connected to DataElement via mapped_from_screen_fields Job Control / Batch Orchestration (Section 22) JobDefinition (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a batch job definition (e.g., JCL JOB statement). Key Attributes: - job_class - Job execution class - priority - Job priority - restart_point - Restart step or checkpoint - scheduling_info - Scheduling metadata Relationships: - Contains JobStep[] (ordered steps within the job) - Can depend on other JobDefinition[] (job dependencies) JobStep (is_a NamedEntity) Represents an individual step within a batch job. Key Attributes: - step_type - JobStepType (e.g., exec_program, exec_proc, utility) - program_name - Program or procedure to execute - condition_code - Condition code for step execution - region_size - Memory region size Relationships: - Connected to JobDefinition (parent job) - Connected to EncapsulationUnit via executed_by_job_steps DatasetAllocation (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a dataset or file allocation within a job step (e.g., JCL DD statement). Key Attributes: - dd_name - DD name (logical file name) - dataset_name - Physical dataset name - disposition - DatasetDisposition (e.g., new, old, shr, mod) - space_primary - Primary space allocation - space_secondary - Secondary space allocation - record_format - Record format Relationships: - Connected to JobStep - Connected to FileDefinition Inter-Process Communication (Section 23) IPCConnection (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a communication channel between processes or programs. Key Attributes: - mechanism - IPCMechanism (e.g., message_queue, socket, shared_memory, named_pipe, cics_link, cics_xctl, grpc_call, event_bus) - is_synchronous - Whether the communication is synchronous - transaction_scoped - Whether the connection is scoped to a transaction Relationships: - Connects source EncapsulationUnit (has_outgoing_ipc_connections) to target EncapsulationUnit (has_incoming_ipc_connections) - Passes DataStructure[] via passed_via_ipc Preprocessor / Metaprogramming (Section 24) PreprocessorDirective (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a preprocessor directive or metaprogramming construct. Key Attributes: - directive_type - MetaprogrammingType (e.g., conditional_compilation, macro_definition, include, pragma, template_instantiation) - condition - Condition expression (for conditional compilation) - expansion - Expanded text or result Relationships: - Connected to CodeContainer via has_preprocessor_directives - Connected to EncapsulationUnit via affected_by_directives - Connected to CallableUnit via callable_affected_by_directives Memory / Ownership Model (Section 25) MemoryModel (is_a NamedEntity) Describes the memory management model for a module or language. Key Attributes: - primary_model - OwnershipModel (e.g., gc_managed, reference_counted, manual, ownership_based, arena) - gc_type - Garbage collector type (e.g., generational, concurrent, reference_counting) - supports_unsafe - Whether unsafe/unmanaged memory access is supported Relationships: - Connected to EncapsulationUnit via memory_model_for_module - Connected to ProgrammingLanguage OwnershipAnnotation (is_a NamedEntity) Represents an ownership or lifetime annotation on a data element. Key Attributes: - ownership - OwnershipModel (e.g., owned, borrowed, shared, static) - lifetime - LifetimeScope (e.g., static, local, heap, parameter) - lifetime_name - Named lifetime identifier (e.g., 'a in Rust) Relationships: - Connected to DataElement via has_ownership_annotations Database Schema Objects (Section 27) DatabaseConstraint (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a constraint on a database table or collection. Key Attributes: - constraint_type - DatabaseConstraintType (e.g., primary_key, foreign_key, unique, check, not_null, default) - columns - Column names involved - reference_table - Referenced table (for foreign keys) - reference_columns - Referenced column names - expression - Constraint expression (for check constraints) Relationships: - Connected to Collection DatabaseIndex (is_a NamedEntity) Represents an index on a database table or collection. Key Attributes: - index_type - IndexType (e.g., btree, hash, gin, gist, fulltext) - columns - Indexed column names - is_unique - Whether this is a unique index - is_partial - Whether this is a partial/filtered index - filter_expression - Filter expression (for partial indexes) Relationships: - Connected to Collection Programming Language (Section 28) ProgrammingLanguage (is_a NamedEntity) Represents a programming language and its characteristics, replacing the string-based format attribute on CodeContainer. Key Attributes: - paradigms - ProgrammingParadigm[] (e.g., object_oriented, procedural, functional, logic, declarative) - type_discipline - Type discipline (e.g., static, dynamic, gradual, untyped) - has_preprocessor - Whether the language has a preprocessor - has_gc - Whether the language has garbage collection - year_introduced - Year the language was introduced Relationships: - Connected to CodeContainer via written_in_language (replaces format string) - Connected to ErrorModel - Connected to MemoryModel This code structure model provides complete traceability from high-level architecture down to individual lines of code, supporting analysis, documentation, and transformation across any programming paradigm.
