headings.title: Section 28: Programming Language as First-Class Entity

entries.text: Extended Modeling (Sections 18-28) This document covers the extended modeling sections introduced in SAO v2.0.0. These sections extend the ontology to represent software systems -- legacy (COBOL, RPG, Assembler, PL/I), recent legacy (C#, Java), and modern (Python, Go, Rust). v2.0 Note: Sections 18-28 are entirely new in SAO v2.0.0. They introduce first-class modeling for type systems, error handling, file I/O, screen definitions, batch orchestration, inter-process communication, preprocessor constructs, memory models, domain relationships, database schema objects, and programming languages. Several of these sections deprecate older string-based attributes in favor of typed object references. Overview The extended modeling sections address capabilities that were either implicit or absent in SAO v1.x: Type System Modeling (Section 18) - Recursive type expressions for generics, unions, pointers, and function types Error Handling Model (Section 19) - Language-level error handling paradigms File I/O Definitions (Section 20) - File-based I/O for COBOL, VSAM, and general file processing Screen/Terminal Interaction (Section 21) - Character-mode UI for CICS BMS maps, RPG display files, and TUI applications Job Control / Batch Orchestration (Section 22) - JCL, schedulers, and batch workflows Inter-Process Communication (Section 23) - CICS LINK/XCTL, shared memory, pipes, RMI, CORBA Preprocessor / Metaprogramming (Section 24) - Preprocessor directives, macros, and metaprogramming constructs Memory / Ownership Model (Section 25) - Rust ownership, garbage collection, manual memory management Domain Entity Relationships (Section 26) - Named, typed relationships between domain entities Database Schema Objects (Section 27) - Constraints and indexes for migration and impact analysis Programming Language as First-Class Entity (Section 28) - Queryable language entity replacing bare strings Section 18: Type System Modeling Provides recursive type modeling for expressing complex types across all languages. TypeExpression Definition: A recursive type expression that models generics (List<T>), unions (string | number), pointers (*int), function types (fn(int) -> bool), and other composite types. Purpose: Replaces flat data_type strings with structured, queryable type information. Enables cross-language type analysis and compatibility checking. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - type_kind (TypeKind, required): The kind of type expression - base_type (string): The base type name (e.g., List, int, String) - type_parameters (TypeExpression[]): Self-referential list for generics (e.g., the String in List<String>) - type_constraints (string[]): Constraints on the type (e.g., T: Comparable) - is_nullable (boolean): Whether the type permits null values - nullability_model (string): The nullability system (e.g., option_type, nullable_annotation, implicit) - pointer_semantics (string): Pointer behavior (e.g., raw, smart, weak, unique) Relationships: - type_of_data_elements <-> DataElement.declared_type: Data elements that have this type - type_of_parameters <-> Parameter.parameter_type: Parameters that have this type - return_type_of_callables <-> CallableUnit.return_type_expression: Callables that return this type Deprecation Note: For typed analysis, TypeExpression replaces the data_type (string) attribute on DataElement and Parameter. The string attribute is retained for backward compatibility but should not be used for new models. Example - Java Generic Type: list_of_string: a: TypeExpression name: "List<String>" type_kind: generic base_type: List type_parameters: - a: TypeExpression name: String type_kind: primitive base_type: String Example - Rust Function Type: predicate_fn: a: TypeExpression name: "fn(i32) -> bool" type_kind: function_type base_type: fn type_parameters: - a: TypeExpression name: i32 type_kind: primitive base_type: i32 is_nullable: false Example - TypeScript Union: string_or_number: a: TypeExpression name: "string | number" type_kind: union type_parameters: - a: TypeExpression type_kind: primitive base_type: string - a: TypeExpression type_kind: primitive base_type: number TypeKind Enum Value Description primitive Built-in scalar type (int, string, bool) generic Parameterized type (List, Map) union Union of types (string | number) intersection Intersection of types (A & B) alias Named type alias pointer Pointer type (*int, &str) reference Reference type (&T, ref T) array_of Array of a base type function_type Function signature as a type tuple_type Tuple of types optional_type Optional/nullable wrapper (Option, T?) constrained Type with constraints (T: Comparable) opaque Opaque/unknown type Section 19: Error Handling Model Models language-level error handling paradigms. ErrorModel Definition: Describes how a module or language handles errors. Purpose: Enables cross-language comparison of error handling strategies and identification of mixed paradigms within a codebase. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - strategy (ErrorHandlingStrategy, required): The error handling paradigm used - checkedness (ExceptionCheckedness): Whether exceptions are checked or unchecked Relationships: - modules_using_error_model <-> EncapsulationUnit.error_model_for_module: Modules that use this error model - error_model_for_languages <-> ProgrammingLanguage.default_error_model: Languages that use this as their default error model Example: java_error_model: a: ErrorModel name: JavaExceptionModel strategy: exception_based checkedness: checked rust_error_model: a: ErrorModel name: RustResultModel strategy: return_value_based checkedness: not_applicable ExceptionType Definition: A declared exception or error type with hierarchy support. Purpose: Models exception class hierarchies and connects them to the callables that raise or handle them. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - qualified_name (string): Fully qualified exception name (e.g., java.io.IOException) - is_checked (boolean): Whether this is a checked exception - parent_exception (ExceptionType, self-ref): Parent in the exception hierarchy - child_exceptions (ExceptionType[], self-ref): Children in the exception hierarchy Relationships: - raised_by_callables <-> CallableUnit.raises_exception_types: Callables that may raise this exception - handled_by_callables <-> CallableUnit.handles_exception_types: Callables that handle this exception Deprecation Note: ExceptionType replaces the raises_exceptions (string[]) and handles_exceptions (string[]) attributes on CallableUnit. Example: io_exception: a: ExceptionType name: IOException qualified_name: java.io.IOException is_checked: true parent_exception: java_exception file_not_found: a: ExceptionType name: FileNotFoundException qualified_name: java.io.FileNotFoundException is_checked: true parent_exception: io_exception ErrorHandlingStrategy Enum Value Description exception_based Try/catch exception handling (Java, Python, C#) return_value_based Result/Either return types (Rust, Go) condition_based Condition system (Common Lisp) error_code_based Numeric error codes (C, COBOL) panic_recover Panic and recover mechanism (Go) monadic Monadic error handling (Haskell) ExceptionCheckedness Enum Value Description checked Compiler-enforced handling (Java checked exceptions) unchecked Runtime-only, not enforced (Python, C#, Java unchecked) not_applicable Language does not use exception-based error handling Section 20: File I/O Definitions Models file-based I/O for COBOL, mainframe VSAM, and general file processing systems. FileDefinition Definition: A file defined for I/O operations, corresponding to a COBOL SELECT clause, a C fopen target, or similar constructs. Purpose: Captures the physical and logical characteristics of files used by programs, enabling impact analysis when file structures change. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - organization (FileOrganization): Physical organization of the file - access_mode (FileAccessMode): How the file is accessed - record_format (RecordFormat): Record format - record_length (int): Record length in bytes - block_size (int): Block size in bytes - key_fields (string[]): Key field names for indexed files - file_status_field (string): Status field for error detection - external_name (string): External/DD name or system filename Relationships: - used_by_callables <-> CallableUnit: Callables that perform I/O on this file - file_defined_in_container <-> CodeContainer: Container where this file is defined - persisted_in_store <-> DataStore: Data store backing this file - file_operations <-> FileOperation: Operations performed on this file - mapped_from_dataset_allocations <-> DatasetAllocation: JCL dataset allocations that map to this file Example - COBOL File: customer_master: a: FileDefinition name: CUSTOMER-MASTER organization: vsam_ksds access_mode: random_access record_format: fixed record_length: 200 key_fields: [CUSTOMER-ID] file_status_field: WS-FILE-STATUS external_name: CUSTMAST file_defined_in_container: customer_program_source Example - C File: log_file: a: FileDefinition name: application_log organization: sequential access_mode: sequential_access record_format: stream external_name: /var/log/app.log FileOperation Definition: An individual I/O operation performed on a file. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - operation_type (FileOperationType, required): The type of I/O operation - condition_handling (string): Error handling approach for this operation Relationships: - operates_on_file <-> FileDefinition: The file being operated on - performed_in_callable <-> CallableUnit: The callable performing the operation Example: read_customer: a: FileOperation name: READ-CUSTOMER-RECORD operation_type: read condition_handling: "AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE" operates_on_file: customer_master performed_in_callable: process_customers_paragraph FileOrganization Enum Value Description sequential Sequential file indexed Indexed file (ISAM) relative Relative record file vsam_ksds VSAM Key-Sequenced Data Set vsam_esds VSAM Entry-Sequenced Data Set vsam_rrds VSAM Relative Record Data Set partitioned_dataset Partitioned Data Set (PDS/PDSE) generation_data_group Generation data group (GDG) line_sequential Line-sequential text file heap Heap/unstructured file FileAccessMode Enum Value Description sequential_access Records accessed in order random_access Records accessed by key or position dynamic_access Both sequential and random access RecordFormat Enum Value Description fixed Fixed-length records variable Variable-length records undefined Undefined record format spanned Spanned records (across blocks) stream Stream-oriented (no record boundaries) FileOperationType Enum Value Description read Read a record write Write a new record rewrite Update an existing record delete Delete a record start Position for sequential access open Open the file close Close the file sort Sort the file merge Merge files Section 21: Screen/Terminal Interaction Models character-mode UI definitions for CICS BMS maps, RPG display files, and TUI applications. ScreenDefinition Definition: A screen or terminal map definition. Purpose: Captures the layout and structure of character-mode user interfaces, enabling UI-to-program traceability and modernization analysis. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - screen_type (ScreenType, required): The type of screen definition - rows (int): Number of screen rows - columns (int): Number of screen columns - external_name (string): External map or display file name Relationships: - contains_screen_fields <-> ScreenField: Fields defined on this screen - program_uses_screens <-> EncapsulationUnit: Programs that use this screen - screen_defined_in_container <-> CodeContainer: Container where this screen is defined Example - CICS BMS Map: customer_inquiry_map: a: ScreenDefinition name: CUSTINQ screen_type: bms_map rows: 24 columns: 80 external_name: CUSTMAP ScreenField Definition: An individual field on a screen definition. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - row (int): Row position on screen - column (int): Column position on screen - length (int): Field length in characters - is_input (boolean): Whether the user can type into this field - is_protected (boolean): Whether the field is protected from modification - attribute_byte (string): Display attribute (e.g., bright, dark, reverse) - initial_value (string): Default display value Relationships: - field_on_screen <-> ScreenDefinition: The screen this field belongs to - maps_to_data_element <-> DataElement: Data element mapped to this field Example: customer_name_field: a: ScreenField name: CUST-NAME row: 5 column: 20 length: 30 is_input: false is_protected: true attribute_byte: bright field_on_screen: customer_inquiry_map maps_to_data_element: customer_name_element ScreenType Enum Value Description bms_map CICS Basic Mapping Support map rpg_display_file RPG display file (AS/400) character_terminal Generic character terminal screen tui Text User Interface (ncurses, etc.) form_based Form-based terminal interaction Section 22: Job Control / Batch Orchestration Models batch job definitions for JCL, schedulers, and batch workflows. JobDefinition Definition: A batch job definition, such as a JCL job or scheduler entry. Purpose: Captures the structure and dependencies of batch workflows, enabling scheduling analysis and restart planning. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - job_class (string): Job class or queue assignment - priority (int): Execution priority - restart_point (string): Step to restart from on failure - scheduling_info (string): Scheduling metadata (cron, calendar, etc.) Relationships: - contains_job_steps <-> JobStep: Steps within this job - depends_on_jobs (self-ref): Jobs that must complete before this one - depended_on_by_jobs (self-ref): Jobs that depend on this one Example: daily_payroll_job: a: JobDefinition name: PAYROLL job_class: A priority: 10 restart_point: STEP030 scheduling_info: "Daily 06:00 EST, business days only" depends_on_jobs: [hr_extract_job] JobStep Definition: A single step within a batch job. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - step_type (JobStepType, required): The type of step - program_name (string): Name of the program to execute - condition_code (string): Condition code expression for step execution - region_size (string): Memory region allocation Relationships: - step_in_job <-> JobDefinition: The job containing this step - step_executes_program <-> EncapsulationUnit: The program executed by this step - allocates_datasets <-> DatasetAllocation: Datasets allocated for this step Example: payroll_calc_step: a: JobStep name: STEP010 step_type: exec_program program_name: PAYCALC condition_code: "COND=(4,LT)" region_size: 4M step_in_job: daily_payroll_job step_executes_program: payroll_calc_program DatasetAllocation Definition: A dataset allocation within a job step (JCL DD statement or equivalent). Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - dd_name (string): DD name (logical file reference) - dataset_name (string): Physical dataset name - disposition (DatasetDisposition): Dataset disposition - space_primary (string): Primary space allocation - space_secondary (string): Secondary space allocation - record_format (RecordFormat): Record format (shared enum with Section 20) Relationships: - allocated_in_step <-> JobStep: The step where this allocation occurs - maps_to_file_definition <-> FileDefinition: The file definition this allocation maps to Example: customer_file_alloc: a: DatasetAllocation name: CUSTDD dd_name: CUSTMAST dataset_name: PROD.CUSTOMER.MASTER disposition: old_dataset record_format: fixed allocated_in_step: payroll_calc_step maps_to_file_definition: customer_master JobStepType Enum Value Description exec_program Execute a program exec_proc Execute a cataloged or in-stream procedure utility Execute a system utility sort Execute a sort operation file_transfer File transfer step conditional Conditional execution step DatasetDisposition Enum Value Description new_dataset Create a new dataset old_dataset Exclusive access to existing dataset shared Shared access to existing dataset modify Modify an existing dataset catalog Catalog the dataset after use delete_disp Delete the dataset after use pass Pass the dataset to the next step Section 23: Inter-Process Communication Models IPC mechanisms including CICS LINK/XCTL, shared memory, pipes, RMI, CORBA, and more. IPCConnection Definition: A connection between two programs via an inter-process communication mechanism. Purpose: Captures how programs communicate at runtime, enabling dependency analysis across process boundaries. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - mechanism (IPCMechanism, required): The IPC mechanism used - is_synchronous (boolean): Whether the communication is synchronous - transaction_scoped (boolean): Whether the communication participates in a transaction Relationships: - ipc_source_program / outgoing_ipc_connections <-> EncapsulationUnit: The program initiating the communication - ipc_target_program / incoming_ipc_connections <-> EncapsulationUnit: The program receiving the communication - ipc_passes_data / passed_via_ipc <-> DataStructure: Data structures passed between programs Example - CICS Program Link: cics_customer_lookup: a: IPCConnection name: CUSTLOOKUP-LINK mechanism: cics_link is_synchronous: true transaction_scoped: true ipc_source_program: order_entry_program ipc_target_program: customer_lookup_program ipc_passes_data: customer_commarea Example - Unix Pipe: log_pipeline: a: IPCConnection name: log-filter-pipe mechanism: pipe is_synchronous: true transaction_scoped: false ipc_source_program: log_generator ipc_target_program: log_filter IPCMechanism Enum Value Description cics_link CICS LINK (call with return) cics_xctl CICS XCTL (transfer control, no return) ims_schedule IMS message scheduling shared_memory Shared memory segment pipe Unix pipe rmi Java Remote Method Invocation corba CORBA IIOP database_mediated Communication via shared database message_queue Message queue (MQ Series, etc.) socket TCP/UDP socket named_pipe Named pipe / FIFO signal Unix signal semaphore Semaphore-based synchronization dcom Distributed COM rest_call REST API call between processes grpc_call gRPC inter-process call event_bus Event bus communication Section 24: Preprocessor / Metaprogramming Models preprocessor directives, macros, and metaprogramming constructs. PreprocessorDirective Definition: A preprocessor directive or metaprogramming construct that modifies code before or during compilation. Purpose: Captures conditional compilation, macro expansion, and code generation constructs that affect program behavior and structure. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - directive_type (MetaprogrammingType, required): The type of metaprogramming construct - condition (string): Conditional expression (e.g., #ifdef DEBUG) - expansion (string): The expanded or generated code Relationships: - directive_defined_in_container <-> CodeContainer: Container where this directive is defined - directive_affects_encapsulation_units <-> EncapsulationUnit: Encapsulation units affected by this directive - directive_affects_callables <-> CallableUnit: Callables affected by this directive Example - C Preprocessor: debug_guard: a: PreprocessorDirective name: DEBUG_LOGGING directive_type: c_preprocessor condition: "#ifdef DEBUG" expansion: "printf(\"Debug: %s\\n\", msg);" directive_defined_in_container: logger_header Example - COBOL COPY REPLACING: employee_copy: a: PreprocessorDirective name: EMPLOYEE-COPY directive_type: cobol_copy_replacing condition: "COPY EMPLOYEE REPLACING ==:PREFIX:== BY ==EMP-==" directive_defined_in_container: payroll_source MetaprogrammingType Enum Value Description c_preprocessor C/C++ preprocessor (#define, #ifdef) rust_macro_declarative Rust declarative macros (macro_rules!) rust_macro_procedural Rust procedural macros (derive, attribute) cobol_copy_replacing COBOL COPY ... REPLACING template_metaprogramming C++ template metaprogramming python_metaclass Python metaclass lisp_macro Lisp macro java_annotation_processor Java annotation processor code_generator External code generator Section 25: Memory / Ownership Model Models memory management and ownership semantics. MemoryModel Definition: Describes the memory management strategy for a module or language. Purpose: Enables analysis of memory safety, ownership transfer, and resource management patterns across codebases. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - primary_model (OwnershipModel, required): The primary memory management approach - gc_type (string): Garbage collector type (e.g., generational, reference_counting, mark_sweep) - supports_unsafe (boolean): Whether the language/module allows unsafe memory operations Relationships: - modules_using_memory_model <-> EncapsulationUnit: Modules that use this memory model - memory_model_for_languages <-> ProgrammingLanguage: Languages that use this as their default memory model Example: rust_ownership: a: MemoryModel name: RustOwnershipModel primary_model: owned supports_unsafe: true java_gc: a: MemoryModel name: JavaGCModel primary_model: garbage_collected gc_type: generational supports_unsafe: false OwnershipAnnotation Definition: An ownership or lifetime annotation on a specific data element. Purpose: Captures fine-grained ownership and lifetime information, particularly for Rust and C++ codebases. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - ownership (OwnershipModel, required): The ownership model for this element - lifetime (LifetimeScope): The lifetime scope - lifetime_name (string): Named lifetime identifier (e.g., 'a in Rust) Relationships: - annotates_data_element <-> DataElement: The data element this annotation applies to Example: borrowed_ref_annotation: a: OwnershipAnnotation name: borrowed_config_ref ownership: borrowed_shared lifetime: named_lifetime lifetime_name: "'a" annotates_data_element: config_reference OwnershipModel Enum Value Description owned Exclusively owned (Rust owned value) borrowed_shared Shared immutable borrow (&T in Rust) borrowed_mutable Exclusive mutable borrow (&mut T in Rust) moved Value has been moved (ownership transferred) copied Value is copied (Copy trait in Rust) reference_counted Reference-counted (Rc, Arc in Rust; shared_ptr in C++) garbage_collected Managed by garbage collector manual Manual allocation/deallocation (C malloc/free) stack_allocated Stack-allocated with automatic cleanup LifetimeScope Enum Value Description static_lifetime Lives for the entire program duration ('static) function_scope Lives for the duration of a function call block_scope Lives for the duration of a block named_lifetime Has a named lifetime parameter ('a, 'b) heap_lifetime Lives on the heap until explicitly freed Section 26: Domain Entity Relationships Provides named, typed relationships between domain entities. Wires the previously orphaned Cardinality enum into the domain model. DomainRelationship Definition: A named, typed relationship between two domain entities (e.g., "Order has many OrderLines", "User belongs to Organization"). Purpose: Explicitly models ER-style relationships with cardinality, navigability, and composition semantics. This section wires the Cardinality enum -- previously defined but unused -- into the domain model. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - cardinality (Cardinality, required): The multiplicity of the relationship - is_navigable (boolean): Whether the relationship is traversable from source to target - is_bidirectional (boolean): Whether the relationship can be navigated in both directions - is_composition (boolean): Whether this represents UML composition (strong ownership) vs aggregation - foreign_key_field (string): The implementing field in the data layer - join_entity (string): For many-to-many relationships, the join table or entity Relationships: - source_entity / outgoing_relationships <-> DomainEntity: The entity that owns or originates the relationship - target_entity / incoming_relationships <-> DomainEntity: The entity referenced by the relationship Uses Existing Cardinality Enum: Value Description one_to_one One-to-one relationship one_to_many One-to-many relationship many_to_one Many-to-one relationship many_to_many Many-to-many relationship Example: order_has_line_items: a: DomainRelationship name: OrderHasLineItems source_entity: order_entity target_entity: order_line_item_entity cardinality: one_to_many is_composition: true is_navigable: true is_bidirectional: true foreign_key_field: order_id student_enrolled_in_courses: a: DomainRelationship name: StudentEnrolledInCourses source_entity: student_entity target_entity: course_entity cardinality: many_to_many is_composition: false is_navigable: true is_bidirectional: true join_entity: Enrollment Section 27: Database Schema Objects Models schema-level constraints and indexes for migration, performance, and impact analysis. DatabaseConstraint Definition: A constraint on a database collection (table). Purpose: Captures primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints, and check constraints for schema analysis, migration planning, and impact assessment. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - constraint_type (DatabaseConstraintType, required): The type of constraint - columns (string[]): Columns involved in the constraint - reference_table (string): Referenced table (for foreign keys) - reference_columns (string[]): Referenced columns (for foreign keys) - expression (string): Constraint expression (for check constraints) Relationships: - constraint_on_collection <-> Collection.has_constraints: The collection this constraint belongs to Deprecation Note: DatabaseConstraint and DatabaseIndex together deprecate the indexes (string[]) attribute on Collection for index information. Example: order_pk: a: DatabaseConstraint name: pk_orders constraint_type: primary_key columns: [order_id] constraint_on_collection: orders_table order_customer_fk: a: DatabaseConstraint name: fk_orders_customer constraint_type: foreign_key columns: [customer_id] reference_table: customers reference_columns: [customer_id] constraint_on_collection: orders_table DatabaseIndex Definition: An index on a database collection (table). Purpose: Captures index definitions for performance analysis and schema management. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - index_type (IndexType, required): The type of index - columns (string[]): Columns included in the index - is_unique (boolean): Whether the index enforces uniqueness - is_partial (boolean): Whether the index is partial/filtered - filter_expression (string): Filter expression for partial indexes Relationships: - index_on_collection <-> Collection.has_indexes: The collection this index belongs to Example: customer_email_idx: a: DatabaseIndex name: idx_customers_email index_type: btree columns: [email] is_unique: true is_partial: false index_on_collection: customers_table order_search_idx: a: DatabaseIndex name: idx_orders_fulltext index_type: fulltext columns: [description, notes] is_unique: false is_partial: false index_on_collection: orders_table DatabaseConstraintType Enum Value Description primary_key Primary key constraint foreign_key Foreign key constraint unique Unique constraint check Check constraint (arbitrary expression) not_null Not-null constraint IndexType Enum Value Description btree B-tree index (default for most databases) hash Hash index gin GIN (Generalized Inverted Index, PostgreSQL) fulltext Full-text search index Section 28: Programming Language as First-Class Entity Replaces bare string fields with a queryable language entity. ProgrammingLanguage Definition: A programming language modeled as a first-class entity. Purpose: Enables structured cross-language analysis. Query "show me all Rust modules" without resorting to string matching on format or language fields. Key Attributes: - Inherits from NamedEntity - paradigms (ProgrammingParadigm[]): Programming paradigms supported - type_discipline (string): Type system discipline (e.g., static_strong, dynamic_weak) - has_preprocessor (boolean): Whether the language has a preprocessor - has_gc (boolean): Whether the language has garbage collection - year_introduced (int): Year the language was first released Relationships: - language_used_by_containers <-> CodeContainer.written_in_language: Code containers written in this language - default_error_model <-> ErrorModel: The default error handling model for this language - default_memory_model <-> MemoryModel: The default memory management model for this language Deprecation Note: ProgrammingLanguage replaces the format (string) attribute on CodeContainer and the language (string) attribute on Component. Example: rust_language: a: ProgrammingLanguage name: Rust paradigms: [procedural, functional, multi_paradigm] type_discipline: static_strong has_preprocessor: false has_gc: false year_introduced: 2010 default_error_model: rust_error_model default_memory_model: rust_ownership cobol_language: a: ProgrammingLanguage name: COBOL paradigms: [procedural] type_discipline: static_strong has_preprocessor: true has_gc: false year_introduced: 1959 java_language: a: ProgrammingLanguage name: Java paradigms: [object_oriented, multi_paradigm] type_discipline: static_strong has_preprocessor: false has_gc: true year_introduced: 1995 default_error_model: java_error_model default_memory_model: java_gc ProgrammingParadigm Enum Value Description object_oriented Object-oriented programming procedural Procedural programming functional Functional programming logic Logic programming (Prolog) concatenative Concatenative programming (Forth, Factor) data_driven Data-driven programming multi_paradigm Supports multiple paradigms Cross-Section Relationships The following diagram summarizes how the new sections connect to existing SAO classes and to each other. (ProgrammingLanguage) Section 25 (MemoryModel) has_default_memory_model Section 20 (FileOperation) Section 20 (FileDefinition) operates_on_file Deprecation Summary The following table lists all attributes deprecated by Sections 18-28, along with their replacements. Deprecated Attribute On Class Replaced By New Type Section data_type (string) DataElement declared_type TypeExpression 18 data_type (string) Parameter has_type TypeExpression 18 raises_exceptions (string[]) CallableUnit raises_exception_types ExceptionType[] 19 handles_exceptions (string[]) CallableUnit handles_exception_types ExceptionType[] 19 indexes (string[]) Collection has_indexes DatabaseIndex[] 27 format (string) CodeContainer written_in_language ProgrammingLanguage 28 language (string) Component written_in_language (via CodeContainer) ProgrammingLanguage 28 All deprecated attributes remain in the schema for backward compatibility. New models should use the replacement attributes exclusively. Usage Patterns Cross-Language Type Analysis # Find all data elements with generic types SELECT ?element ?base_type WHERE { ?type a sao:TypeExpression ; sao:type_kind "generic" ; sao:base_type ?base_type . ?element sao:declared_type ?type . } Batch Job Impact Analysis # Find all programs executed by a job and the files they use SELECT ?job ?step ?program ?file WHERE { ?job a sao:JobDefinition ; sao:contains_job_steps ?step . ?step sao:step_executes_program ?program . ?program sao:uses_file_definitions ?file . } IPC Dependency Graph # Find all inter-process communication paths SELECT ?source ?mechanism ?target WHERE { ?ipc a sao:IPCConnection ; sao:mechanism ?mechanism ; sao:ipc_source_program ?source ; sao:ipc_target_program ?target . } Language-Scoped Queries # Find all Rust modules and their memory models SELECT ?module ?memory_model WHERE { :rust_language sao:language_used_by_containers ?container . ?module sao:defined_in_container ?container . ?module sao:memory_model_for_module ?memory_model . } Best Practices Use TypeExpression for new models: Do not rely on data_type strings when structured type information is needed. Model error handling explicitly: Attach an ErrorModel to each EncapsulationUnit to enable cross-module error strategy analysis. Connect files to jobs: Always link FileDefinition to DatasetAllocation via maps_to_file_definition for mainframe systems. Use ProgrammingLanguage over strings: Replace bare format and language strings with ProgrammingLanguage entity references. Capture IPC dependencies: Model all inter-process communication paths, even database-mediated ones, to get a complete dependency picture. Annotate ownership in Rust/C++: Use OwnershipAnnotation to track borrow relationships and lifetime constraints on data elements. Define screen-to-data mappings: Link ScreenField to DataElement to trace user input through the program. Model constraints and indexes as objects: Use DatabaseConstraint and DatabaseIndex instead of string arrays to enable schema comparison and migration analysis.

entries.text: Changelog [3.0.0] - Unreleased candidate Breaking relationship changes Introduce generic version_of, entry_in, uses, constrains, and contains_unit_members relationships with class-specific SHACL pairings. Separate subscriber/interface and file/callable participant roles using explicit predicates. Retire nine replaced predicates with explicit SHACL rejection; add no compatibility aliases. Add typed unit-data membership and subproperty entailments without treating data structures as encapsulation units. Tentatively bump RDF/project metadata to 3.0.0 while retaining the unchanged LinkML 2.1.0 baseline. See migration guidance. Earlier migration milestones Add an optional editable OWL supplement for 208 inverse pairs and document seven unresolved inverse groups without changing their vocabulary definitions. Promote Turtle vocabulary and initial SHACL shapes to editable source, with Turtle-only assembly and validation. Retain the legacy LinkML baseline. All notable changes to the Systems Abstraction Ontology (SAO) are documented here. The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning. Earlier release preparation Rename SAO to Systems Abstraction Ontology to make its scope explicit across libraries, services, batch programs, and applications. Update the LinkML schema name and project metadata to systems-abstraction-ontology; the SAO acronym, term namespace, and model definitions are unchanged. Split the LinkML schema into topic modules under legacy/sao/schema/, preserving legacy/sao/sao.yml as the entry point and keeping definitions, constraints, and term IRIs unchanged. Module schema IDs now identify definition provenance. Enrich LinkML attribute, shared-slot, and enum value descriptions from the existing documentation, and add class-purpose comments without changing the model. Replace the placeholder schema ID and term prefix with https://ontologies.corestory.ai/sao/, using the shared CoreStory ontology host. Update all module schema IDs to the same URI space. Consumers using ontology.example.org or https://sao.corestory.ai/ must update schema references and term IRIs. Prepare the repository for Apache License 2.0 distribution: replace the proprietary license, add attribution, and align project metadata. Refresh the README for schema version 2.1.0 and add validated instance examples. Add contribution guidance and CI checks for schema and example validation. [2.1.0] - 2026-04-18 This release standardizes the naming convention for relationship attributes. Every plain-noun relationship attribute has been renamed to a verb-prefixed form so the ontology reads uniformly across all layers. Rename rule contains_* when the inverse is part_of_* or contained_in_* (composition). has_* otherwise (association). Removed Four v2.0-migration-leftover attributes that duplicated newer relationships: Class Removed attribute Use instead UserInterface screens contains_screens (renamed from ui_screens) AuditLog entries contains_entries (renamed from audit_log_entries) Log entries contains_entries (renamed from log_entries) Trace spans contains_spans (renamed from trace_spans) Changed — forward attribute renames Simple-collection attributes (renamed to has_* or contains_*): Class Old name New name Actor actor_subscriptions has_subscriptions Aggregate value_objects has_value_objects AuditLog has_ownership_annotations DataPipeline steps has_steps DataStore collections has_collections Dataset schema has_schema Dependency target has_target Endpoint operations has_operations FileDefinition file_operations has_file_operations IaCDefinition resources has_resources Identity credentials has_credentials Integration messages has_messages Lifecycle states has_states Lifecycle transitions has_transitions Log log_entries contains_entries MLModel input_schema has_input_schema MLModel metrics has_metrics MLModel output_schema has_output_schema Module dependencies has_dependencies PackageDependency known_vulnerabilities has_known_vulnerabilities Parameter parameter_type has_type Permission constraints has_constraints Policy rules has_rules ProgrammingLanguage default_error_model has_default_error_model ProgrammingLanguage default_memory_model has_default_memory_model Release artifacts has_artifacts Schema schema_versions has_versions Service health_checks has_health_checks StateStore state_shape has_state_shape Tenant organizations has_organizations Tenant settings has_settings TestCase assertions has_assertions Trace trace_spans contains_spans TypeExpression type_parameters has_type_parameters UIComponent props has_props UserInterface ui_screens contains_screens ValueObject attributes has_attributes Workflow steps has_steps Tree/role/directional attributes (renamed to has_* for uniformity): Class Old name New name CodeBlock parent_block has_parent_block CodeBlock child_blocks has_child_blocks ControlFlow source_callable has_source_callable ControlFlow target_callable has_target_callable ControlFlow source_statement has_source_statement ControlFlow target_statement has_target_statement DataElement parent_element has_parent_element DataElement child_elements has_child_elements DataFlow source_element has_source_element DataFlow target_element has_target_element DataFlow through_callable has_through_callable DataFlow through_statement has_through_statement DataStructure parent_structure has_parent_structure DataStructure child_structures has_child_structures DomainEntity incoming_relationships has_incoming_relationships DomainEntity outgoing_relationships has_outgoing_relationships DomainRelationship source_entity has_source_entity DomainRelationship target_entity has_target_entity EncapsulationUnit incoming_ipc_connections has_incoming_ipc_connections EncapsulationUnit outgoing_ipc_connections has_outgoing_ipc_connections ExceptionType parent_exception has_parent_exception ExceptionType child_exceptions has_child_exceptions IaCModule child_resources has_child_resources IPCConnection ipc_source_program has_source_program IPCConnection ipc_target_program has_target_program Organization parent has_parent Organization children has_children Route parent_route has_parent_route Route child_routes has_child_routes StorageLocation parent_location has_parent_location UIComponent parent_ui_component has_parent_ui_component UIComponent child_ui_components has_child_ui_components Added New inverse relationships on target classes for a subset of the renamed attributes that previously lacked an inverse (e.g., ValueObject.belongs_to_aggregate, Credential.credential_for_identity, Configuration.setting_for_tenant, Organization.organization_in_tenant). The remaining forward-only relationships retain single-direction traversal semantics as before; a follow-up pass may add inverses across the board if bidirectional traversal is needed. DataPipeline.pipeline_trains_model (the inverse of MLModel.model_trained_by_pipeline). The inverse was previously declared on BuildPipeline by mistake, leaving the MLModel → DataPipeline side dangling. Moved to the correct class. Fixed BuildPipeline.pipeline_trains_model removed; ML model training is a DataPipeline concern, not a CI/CD concern. The attribute now lives on DataPipeline. Migration guide Consumers of the ontology should update queries and tooling as follows: Replace every old attribute name with its new name per the tables above. Any code that relied on the removed duplicate attributes (UserInterface.screens, AuditLog.entries, Log.entries, Trace.spans) must switch to the canonical contains_* replacement. Documentation The authoritative reference for v2.1 is legacy/sao/sao.yml itself. The docs/ tree has been updated for the most-distinctive renames (e.g., ui_screens → contains_screens, default_error_model → has_default_error_model) but some ambiguous names that also appear as prose in the docs (e.g., "entries," "steps," "rules") may still reference the old attribute names in explanatory text. A full documentation sweep is tracked as a follow-up. [2.0.0] See git history for v2.0 changes; prior to this release the repository did not maintain a changelog. Key v2.0 work: inlining single-use relationship slots as class attributes, code-structure layer expansion, and introduction of the bidirectional-relationship pattern that v2.1 generalizes.

entries.text: Contributing to SAO Follow the shared repository contribution guide. Run commands from the repository root. Edit vocabulary under ontologies/sao/vocabulary/, constraints under ontologies/sao/shapes/, and reviewed inverse axioms under ontologies/sao/axioms/. Update manifests when adding files. Rebuild and commit the dist/sao.*ttl distributions with source edits. The inverse audit and 3.0.0 migration notes explain relationship compatibility. Do not reinterpret class-local inverses as global OWL axioms without reviewing all uses. Add valid and invalid examples for changed constraints. The historical LinkML baseline and its check commands are documented under legacy/sao/. It is not the source for current Turtle authoring. Use bold for class names in prose and monospace for exact property names, enum values and dotted paths. Keep synthetic examples and preserved Apache attribution.

entries.text: Systems Abstraction Ontology (SAO) A comprehensive, language-agnostic ontology for modeling software systems — from individual lines of code to business capabilities, from COBOL copybooks to Kubernetes deployments. SAO describes software systems—their structure, behavior, domain concepts, and operating context—including libraries, services, batch programs, and applications. Version: 3.0.0 candidate (unreleased) Author: Charath Ranganathan License: Apache License 2.0 Editable sources: RDFS vocabulary and SHACL shapes in Turtle Distributions: sao.ttl, sao.shacl.ttl, and optional sao.owl.ttl inverse axioms Legacy baseline: LinkML 2.1.0 retained during migration 147 classes · 102 enums · 217 inverse pairs in the 3.0.0 candidate See the 3.0.0 relationship migration for breaking predicate changes. Key Features Comprehensive Coverage: Models all aspects of software systems DDD-Aligned: Built on Domain-Driven Design principles (Aggregates, Bounded Contexts, Ubiquitous Language) Cloud-Native: Supports microservices, containers, serverless, and cloud deployment Compliance-Ready: Includes models for GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, and more Legacy-Ready: First-class support for COBOL, RPG, PL/I, Assembler, JCL, CICS, IMS alongside modern languages Interoperable: Based on LinkML standard with RDF/RDFS, SKOS, and Dublin Core alignment Extensible: Designed for subclassing, mixins, custom enumerations, and additional relationships This ontology is part of the CoreStory Ontologies repository. Run all commands below from the repository root. Documentation The guide reflects the retained LinkML baseline; use the migration notes for current relationship names. Start here: The SAO Guide — a layered walkthrough of all 147 classes organized by abstraction level, from code structure to business intent. Section deep dives Doc Topic Key classes 01 Enumerations All enum types 102 enums with 804 permissible values 02 Structural Foundation Architecture System, BoundedContext, Module, Component, Service, Interface 03 Actors and Identity Identity Actor, Identity, Credential, Tenant, Organization 04 Authorization and Policy Access control Role, Permission, Policy, Scope, Constraint 05 Domain Modeling DDD Aggregate, DomainEntity, ValueObject, Attribute, Lifecycle 06 Behavior and Workflow Behavior Action, Operation, Workflow, Rule, Event, Transaction 07 Data Management Persistence DataStore, Collection, Schema, DataClassification, RetentionPolicy 08 Integration External systems ExternalSystem, Integration, Contract, Adapter, CircuitBreaker 09 Deployment and Operations Runtime Environment, Deployment, Configuration, Infrastructure, Release 10 Observability Monitoring Metric, Log, Trace, Alert, Incident, HealthCheck 11 Governance and Compliance Compliance ComplianceRequirement, Control, Evidence, RiskAssessment 12 Code Structure Code modeling CodeContainer, EncapsulationUnit, CallableUnit, DataStructure 13 Extended Modeling Sections 18–28 TypeExpression, ErrorModel, FileDefinition, JobDefinition, IPC, etc. Other resources C4 Model Mapping — SAO classes mapped to C4 architecture layers (Layer 1, Layer 2, Layer 3, Layer 4) Whitepaper (not included in this public snapshot) — "Beyond Grep and Vector Search: The Case for Ontology-driven Extraction of Software Requirements" Getting Started Read the SAO Guide for a conceptual overview Define your System and BoundedContexts Identify Modules and Components Map domain Aggregates and Entities Document Integrations, Authorization, and Compliance metadata Turtle source workflow Edit topic files in ontologies/sao/vocabulary/ and class-specific shapes in ontologies/sao/shapes/. The manifests under ontologies/sao/manifests/ define the distributions. The normal build reads Turtle directly and does not invoke LinkML: uv sync --locked uv run python scripts/build_rdf.py uv run python scripts/build_rdf.py --check uv run python scripts/validate_rdf.py uv run python scripts/validate_axioms.py uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests The RDF example is synthetic. To validate another Turtle data graph, pass its path to scripts/validate_rdf.py. The initial shapes are open and do not yet provide full equivalence with the legacy schema. See the migration status. Legacy baseline validation Install uv, then run these commands from the repository root. uv sync installs Python 3.13 if needed and, with --group legacy, the historical LinkML toolchain pinned in uv.lock. uv sync --locked --group legacy uv run --group legacy linkml-lint --validate-only legacy/sao/sao.yml uv run --group legacy python scripts/migration/sao/check_schema.py uv run --group legacy gen-json-schema legacy/sao/sao.yml > /tmp/sao.schema.json uv run --group legacy linkml-validate --exit-on-first-failure -s legacy/sao/sao.yml -C System examples/sao/system.yaml uv run --group legacy linkml-validate --exit-on-first-failure -s legacy/sao/sao.yml -C Aggregate examples/sao/aggregate.yaml uv run --group legacy linkml-validate --exit-on-first-failure -s legacy/sao/sao.yml -C Integration examples/sao/integration.yaml This repository contains an ontology and documentation; it does not include a codebase extractor or a deployed application. The extraction playbook describes how to populate the ontology. Multi-class snippets in the guides are conceptual illustrations; validate an individual instance with an explicit -C target class as shown above. For RDFS consumers, use dist/sao.ttl, or load the vocabulary files listed in ontologies/sao/manifests/vocabulary.json into one graph. Use dist/sao.shacl.ttl for the initial validation profile. For optional inverse reasoning, load the vocabulary plus dist/sao.owl.ttl; see the inverse audit and the proposed redesign. See semantics and limits. Other LinkML generators include gen-pydantic, gen-typescript, and gen-graphql. Legacy LinkML layout legacy/sao/sao.yml is the entry point for the retained LinkML baseline. It imports the topic modules in schema/; pass it to legacy LinkML validators and generators. Each definition has one home. Enums used in one topic live with that topic; shared enums, types, base classes, and global slots live in schema/common.yaml. Cross-topic references are resolved through the entry point, so the topic files are not standalone schemas. The split preserves the public sao term namespace. Each module has its own schema ID under https://ontologies.corestory.ai/sao/schema/, used by LinkML for definition provenance; these IDs do not change class or property IRIs. Generate the full Markdown reference, including imported definitions, with: uv run --group legacy gen-doc --render-imports --directory /tmp/sao-reference legacy/sao/sao.yml --render-imports also includes the standard LinkML types. Without this flag, the documentation generator omits definitions in the topic modules. Examples The YAML files under examples/ are legacy instances checked against the LinkML baseline; the RDF example is checked against the initial SHACL profile. Reference relationships use entity IDs; relationships declared with inlined_as_list: true embed objects. See the examples for both representations. Simple E-Commerce System id: ecommerce-platform name: E-Commerce Platform contains_bounded_contexts: - id: catalog-context name: Catalog Context - id: order-context name: Order Context - id: customer-context name: Customer Context - id: payment-context name: Payment Context Order Aggregate id: order-aggregate name: Order has_root_entity: order aggregates_entities: - id: order name: Order - id: order-line-item name: Order Line Item has_value_objects: - money - address Integration with External Service id: stripe-integration name: Stripe Integration integration_type: bidirectional protocol: https integrates_with_system: stripe-payment-gateway uses_adapter: stripe-adapter protected_by_breaker: payment-circuit-breaker integration_governed_by_contract: stripe-api-contract Schema namespace The schema ID and sao term prefix are both https://ontologies.corestory.ai/sao/. For example, the System class IRI is https://ontologies.corestory.ai/sao/System. Applications using the earlier ontology.example.org or https://sao.corestory.ai/ namespaces should migrate their schema references and term IRIs. The documentation site will be rendered to the site branch and published through CoreStory's CDN. Technical Details Source format: Turtle, with RDFS vocabulary, SHACL constraints and optional OWL axioms Semantic Web: RDF/RDFS compatible, SKOS concept schemes, Dublin Core metadata, Schema.org alignment Composition: Explicit manifests assemble independently versioned ontology layers Extensibility: Subclass existing classes, add mixins, define custom enumerations, or add new relationship slots Version History Version 3.0.0 (Candidate, unreleased) Generic inverse relationships with class-specific SHACL pairing Role-specific subscription and file-operation predicates Replaced predicates rejected by validation; see migration guidance Version 2.1.0 (Legacy baseline) Relationship attributes standardized to verb-prefixed names Duplicate relationship attributes removed and ML training inverse corrected See CHANGELOG.md for the complete migration guide Version 2.0.0 Structural refactor: ~340 single-use global slots inlined as class attributes 18 new classes spanning type system, error handling, file I/O, screen definitions, job control, IPC, preprocessor, memory model, domain relationships, database schema, and programming language 17 new enums for type kinds, error strategies, file organization, screen types, job steps, IPC mechanisms, ownership models, and more 8 existing enums extended with legacy platform values (RPG, PL/I, Assembler, VSAM, JCL) Programming Language as first-class entity replacing bare string fields Version 1.0.0 Initial comprehensive ontology release with 12 major sections Paradigm-agnostic code structure modeling supporting modern and legacy systems Roadmap v2.1: Enhanced event sourcing patterns v2.2: Service mesh and API gateway extensions Contributing See CONTRIBUTING.md for setup, validation, and submission guidance. Areas of interest: additional compliance framework mappings, domain-specific extensions, example implementations, documentation improvements, validation rules, and code generators. entries.text: Layer 1: System Context Representation This document defines the SAO v2.0 classes that correspond to C4 Level 1 (System Context) -- the outermost zoom level, where the system is viewed as a black box. Layer 1 answers the big-picture questions: what is this system, who uses it (actors), what sits outside it (external systems), and how is it governed (compliance and risk). Where Layer 2 answers "what containers and services make up the system?", Layer 1 answers "what is the system, who interacts with it, and what rules constrain it?" Scope Layer 1 covers: The system itself -- the top-level named entity representing the software product, platform, or application Actors and identity -- human users, automated agents, their verified identities, credentials, and organizational membership Multi-tenancy -- tenant boundaries for systems that serve multiple isolated customer populations External systems -- third-party services, partner systems, legacy systems, and SaaS applications outside the system boundary Compliance and governance -- regulatory obligations, controls implementing those obligations, evidence of control effectiveness, and risk assessments Layer 1 is paradigm-agnostic. These concepts apply equally to a legacy mainframe CICS system, a monolithic Java EE application, and a modern cloud-native microservices platform. Every software system has actors who use it, external systems it depends on, and governance constraints it must satisfy. The differences in how these concepts are realized emerge at Layer 2 (containers) and below. Summary # Class Definition Group SAO Section 1 System Top-level container representing a software product, platform, or application System 1 2 Actor (abstract) Any entity that can initiate actions -- base class for HumanActor and SystemActor Actors & Identity 2 3 HumanActor A human user of the system Actors & Identity 2 4 SystemActor A system or automated actor Actors & Identity 2 5 Identity A verified representation of an actor Actors & Identity 2 6 Credential Authentication material proving an identity claim Actors & Identity 2 7 Organization A logical grouping of users and resources within a tenant Actors & Identity 2 8 Tenant An organizational boundary for multi-tenant systems Multi-tenancy 2 9 ExternalSystem A system outside this system's boundary External Systems 7 10 ComplianceRequirement A regulatory or policy obligation Compliance & Governance 10 11 Control A measure implementing a compliance requirement Compliance & Governance 10 12 Evidence Proof that a control is operating effectively Compliance & Governance 10 13 RiskAssessment An evaluation of threats and vulnerabilities Compliance & Governance 10 Total: 13 classes (including 2 subtypes: HumanActor and SystemActor that inherit from the abstract Actor). Connections to Adjacent Layers Downward links to Layer 2 (Container) These relationships connect Layer 1 concepts to the internal structure of the system: Layer 1 class Attribute Layer 2 class Description System contains_bounded_contexts BoundedContext Bounded contexts within this system System has_integrations Integration Integration connections owned by this system System exposes_interfaces Interface Interfaces the system exposes to the outside world Identity belongs_to_tenant Tenant Tenant an identity belongs to (Tenant links further down) Tenant settings Configuration Tenant-specific configuration values ExternalSystem integrated_via Integration Integrations connecting to this external system Cross-layer links to Layer 3 (Component) These relationships connect Layer 1 concepts to component-level and behavioral abstractions: Layer 1 class Attribute Layer 3 class Description System enforces_policies Policy Authorization policies enforced at the system level Actor performs_actions Action Actions initiated by this actor Identity has_roles Role Roles assigned to this identity Actor has_subscriptions Subscription Event subscriptions registered by this actor System (1 class) 1. System Top-level container representing a software product, platform, or application. This is the root node of the entire SAO model -- everything else is contained within or connected to a System. Mixins: Versionable (adds version, effective_from, effective_to, is_current) Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) version SemanticVersion No Semantic version (from Versionable) effective_from Timestamp No Version start date (from Versionable) effective_to Timestamp No Version end date (from Versionable) is_current boolean No Whether this is the current version (from Versionable) Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description contains_bounded_contexts BoundedContext Yes contained_in_system Bounded contexts within this system (Layer 2) has_integrations Integration Yes belongs_to_system Integration connections (Layer 2) enforces_policies Policy Yes enforced_by_system Authorization policies enforced (Layer 3) must_comply_with ComplianceRequirement Yes applies_to_systems Compliance obligations assessed_by RiskAssessment Yes assesses_system Risk assessments performed exposes_interfaces Interface Yes exposed_by_system Interfaces exposed to external consumers (Layer 2) Actors & Identity (6 classes) 2. Actor (abstract) Any entity that can initiate actions. This is the abstract base class for HumanActor and SystemActor -- it is never instantiated directly. Actors have identities, perform actions, own controls, and subscribe to events. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) category ActorCategory No human or system Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description has_identities Identity Yes represents_actor Verified identities for this actor performs_actions Action Yes performed_by_actor Actions initiated (Layer 3) audit_actions_performed AuditEntry Yes audit_performed_by_actor Audit trail of actions has_subscriptions Subscription Yes subscribed_by_actor Event subscriptions (Layer 3) owns_controls Control Yes owned_by_actor Compliance controls owned verifies_evidence Evidence Yes verified_by_actor Evidence verified by this actor ActorCategory Enum: Value Description human A human user system An automated system or agent 3. HumanActor A human user of the system. Inherits all attributes and relationships from Actor. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description actor_type HumanActorType No Specific type of human actor email string No Email address Relationships: Inherits all relationships from Actor. HumanActorType Enum: Value Description end_user Regular end user administrator System administrator operator Operations staff developer Software developer auditor Compliance or security auditor 4. SystemActor A system or automated actor. Inherits all attributes and relationships from Actor. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description actor_type SystemActorType No Specific type of system actor service_account string No Service account identifier Relationships: Inherits all relationships from Actor. SystemActorType Enum: Value Description internal_service An internal service within the system external_system An external system acting as a client scheduled_process A cron job or scheduled task ai_agent An AI/ML agent or bot message_trigger A message-driven trigger 5. Identity A verified representation of an actor. An actor may have multiple identities (e.g., one per tenant, one per authentication provider). Identities hold credentials, are assigned roles, and belong to tenants and organizations. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) identity_type string No Freeform identity type label Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description credentials Credential Yes -- Authentication credentials (inline) has_roles Role Yes assigned_to_identities Roles assigned to this identity (Layer 3) belongs_to_tenant Tenant No contains_identities Tenant this identity belongs to member_of_organizations Organization Yes has_identity_members Organizations this identity is a member of represents_actor Actor No has_identities Actor this identity represents 6. Credential Authentication material proving an identity claim. Credentials are inlined within Identity (not standalone top-level entities). Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) credential_type CredentialType No Type of credential expires_at Timestamp No Expiration timestamp is_active boolean No Whether the credential is currently active Relationships: No outgoing relationships. Credentials are inlined within Identity via credentials. CredentialType Enum: Value Description password Password-based authentication token Token-based authentication (JWT, bearer token) certificate Digital certificate or X.509 certificate api_key API key biometric Biometric authentication mfa Multi-factor authentication oauth OAuth 2.0 authentication flow 7. Organization A logical grouping of users and resources within a tenant. Organizations can form hierarchies via parent/child relationships. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description parent Organization No -- Parent organization in the hierarchy children Organization Yes -- Child organizations has_identity_members Identity Yes member_of_organizations Identities belonging to this organization Multi-tenancy (1 class) 8. Tenant An organizational boundary for multi-tenant systems. Tenants contain organizations, identities, and tenant-specific configuration. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description organizations Organization Yes -- Organizations within this tenant (inline) settings Configuration Yes -- Tenant-specific configuration (Layer 2) contains_identities Identity Yes belongs_to_tenant Identities scoped to this tenant External Systems (1 class) 9. ExternalSystem A system outside this system's boundary. External systems are integrated via Integration objects and classified by type. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) system_type ExternalSystemType No Category of external system owner string No Team or organization that owns the external system sla string No Service level agreement description documentation_url URI No Link to external system documentation Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description integrated_via Integration Yes integrates_with_system Integrations connecting to this system (Layer 2) ExternalSystemType Enum: Value Description third_party_service Third-party service (Stripe, Twilio, etc.) partner_system Partner or affiliate system legacy_system Legacy system being integrated saas_application SaaS application Compliance & Governance (4 classes) 10. ComplianceRequirement A regulatory or policy obligation that the system must satisfy. Requirements reference a compliance framework, contain controls, and apply to one or more systems. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) framework ComplianceFramework No Compliance framework this requirement belongs to effective_date Timestamp No Date the requirement takes effect Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description controls Control Yes -- Controls implementing this requirement (inline) applies_to_systems System Yes must_comply_with Systems subject to this requirement ComplianceFramework Enum: Value Description gdpr General Data Protection Regulation (EU) hipaa Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act soc2 SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria pci_dss Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard iso27001 ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management sox Sarbanes-Oxley Act ccpa California Consumer Privacy Act fedramp Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program 11. Control A measure implementing a compliance requirement. Controls are owned by actors, produce evidence, and mitigate risks. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) control_id string No External control identifier (e.g., "SOC2-CC6.1") implementation string No Description of how the control is implemented frequency string No How often the control is executed (e.g., "daily", "continuous") Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description evidence Evidence Yes -- Evidence proving this control works (inline) owned_by_actor Actor No owns_controls Actor responsible for this control mitigates_risks RiskAssessment Yes mitigated_by_controls Risk assessments this control mitigates 12. Evidence Proof that a control is operating effectively. Evidence is collected at a point in time, references an artifact, and may be verified by an actor. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) evidence_type string No Freeform type of evidence (e.g., "log export", "screenshot", "report") collected_at Timestamp No When the evidence was collected artifact_uri URI No URI to the evidence artifact Relationships: Relationship Range Multi Inverse Description verified_by_actor Actor No verifies_evidence Actor who verified this evidence 13. RiskAssessment An evaluation of threats and vulnerabilities affecting the system. Risk assessments are linked to the system they evaluate and the controls that mitigate identified risks. Attributes: Attribute Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier (from NamedEntity) name string Yes Human-readable name (from NamedEntity) description string No Free-text description (from NamedEntity) tags string[] No Freeform tags (from NamedEntity) metadata Metadata No Created/updated timestamps and version (from NamedEntity, inline) assessed_at Timestamp No When the assessment was performed risk_level string No Overall risk level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "critical") threats string[] No Identified threats vulnerabilities string[] No Identified vulnerabilities entries.text: Layer 2: Container-Level Representation This document defines the SAO v2.0 classes that correspond to C4 Level 2 (Container) -- the deployable services, data stores, interfaces, pipelines, and operational infrastructure that compose a system. This layer sits between the system context (Layer 1) and the component internals (Layer 3). Where Layer 1 answers "what systems exist and how do they interact?", Layer 2 answers "what are the running parts of this system -- its services, databases, message brokers, build pipelines, and how are they deployed, monitored, and integrated?" Scope Layer 2 covers: Structural decomposition -- bounded contexts, modules, services, dependencies Interfaces and endpoints -- user interfaces, APIs, event interfaces, screens, routes Data management -- data stores, collections, records, classifications, retention, lineage, audit, database schema objects Integration -- external system connections, messages, contracts, adapters, circuit breakers Deployment and runtime -- environments, deployments, deployment units, configuration, infrastructure, releases Observability -- metrics, logs, traces, spans, alerts, alert rules, incidents, health checks Build and CI/CD -- pipelines, pipeline stages, build artifacts, artifact registries Dependency management -- package managers, package dependencies, known vulnerabilities Infrastructure as code -- IaC definitions, modules, resources ML and data pipelines -- data pipelines, steps, datasets, ML models, model metrics, feature stores Testing -- test suites, coverage, assertions Frontend supporting -- state stores, UI properties, concurrency patterns Like Layer 3, Layer 2 is paradigm-agnostic. A mainframe CICS system and a cloud-native microservice architecture both have services, data stores, deployments, and integrations. The differences emerge in how these are implemented (Layers 3 and 4), not in what they are (Layer 2). NamedEntity base attributes. Every class in this document extends NamedEntity, which provides id (string, required), name (string, required), description (string), tags (string[]), and metadata (Metadata, inline). These are not repeated in individual class tables. Summary # Class Definition Group SAO Section 1 BoundedContext A semantic boundary within which a domain model applies consistently (DDD) Structural 1 2 Module A deployable, cohesive unit of functionality within a bounded context Structural 1 3 Service An independently deployable runtime unit Structural 1 4 Interface (abstract) A contract-defined boundary through which interaction occurs Structural 1 5 Dependency (inline) A lightweight dependency reference between components or services Structural 1 6 UserInterface A user-facing interface (web, mobile, desktop, CLI) Interfaces & Endpoints 1 7 ProgrammaticInterface A machine-to-machine interface (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, SDK, SOAP) Interfaces & Endpoints 1 8 EventInterface An event-driven interface (webhook, message queue, event stream, pub/sub) Interfaces & Endpoints 1 9 Screen A single screen or view in a user interface Interfaces & Endpoints 1 10 Endpoint A specific addressable entry point on a service Interfaces & Endpoints 1 11 Route A navigation route or URL path in a frontend application Interfaces & Endpoints 12 12 DataStore A persistence mechanism (relational DB, document DB, cache, message broker, etc.) Data Management 6 13 Collection A logical grouping of records (table, collection, bucket) Data Management 6 14 Record A single persisted instance of data Data Management 6 15 DataClassification A sensitivity or handling category for data Data Management 6 16 RetentionPolicy Rules governing data lifecycle and deletion Data Management 6 17 DataLineage The origin, transformation history, and movement of data Data Management 6 18 AuditLog A tamper-evident record of system activities Data Management 6 19 AuditEntry A single record within an audit log Data Management 6 20 DatabaseConstraint (inline) A constraint on a database table/collection Data Management 27 21 DatabaseIndex (inline) An index on a database table/collection Data Management 27 22 Integration A configured connection to an external system Integration 7 23 Message (inline) A unit of data exchanged in integration Integration 7 24 Contract A formal specification of integration behavior Integration 7 25 ContractVersion (inline) A specific iteration of a contract Integration 7 26 Adapter A component that translates between system and external protocols (extends Component from L3) Integration 7 27 CircuitBreaker A resilience pattern preventing cascade failures Integration 7 28 Environment A runtime context with specific configuration Deployment & Runtime 8 29 Deployment An instance of a service running in an environment Deployment & Runtime 8 30 DeploymentUnit The packaged artifact being deployed Deployment & Runtime 8 31 Configuration Runtime parameters for a deployment Deployment & Runtime 8 32 Infrastructure The underlying compute, storage, and network resources Deployment & Runtime 8 33 Release A versioned, deployable package of changes Deployment & Runtime 8 34 Metric A quantitative measurement over time Observability 9 35 Log A timestamped record of discrete events Observability 9 36 LogEntry (inline) A single record within a log Observability 9 37 Trace A causal chain of operations across services Observability 9 38 Span (inline) A single unit of work within a trace Observability 9 39 Alert A notification triggered by metric thresholds or anomalies Observability 9 40 AlertRule The condition that triggers an alert (extends Rule from L3) Observability 9 41 Incident A tracked degradation or outage event Observability 9 42 HealthCheck (inline) A probe verifying service availability Observability 9 43 BuildPipeline A CI/CD pipeline automating build, test, and deployment Build & CI/CD 13 44 PipelineStage (inline) A discrete stage within a CI/CD pipeline Build & CI/CD 13 45 BuildArtifact An artifact produced by a build pipeline Build & CI/CD 13 46 ArtifactRegistry A registry or repository for storing build artifacts Build & CI/CD 13 47 PackageManager A package/dependency management tool Dependency Management 14 48 PackageDependency A declared dependency on an external package or library Dependency Management 14 49 KnownVulnerability (inline) A known security vulnerability in a dependency Dependency Management 14 50 IaCDefinition An infrastructure-as-code definition for declarative resource provisioning Infrastructure as Code 17 51 IaCModule A reusable module of IaC definitions Infrastructure as Code 17 52 IaCResource (inline) A single infrastructure resource defined in code Infrastructure as Code 17 53 DataPipeline A data processing pipeline for ETL, feature engineering, or model training ML & Data Pipelines 16 54 DataPipelineStep (inline) A discrete step within a data pipeline ML & Data Pipelines 16 55 Dataset A dataset used for training, evaluation, or inference ML & Data Pipelines 16 56 MLModel A machine learning model defined, trained, or served by the system ML & Data Pipelines 16 57 MLModelMetric (inline) A performance metric for an ML model ML & Data Pipelines 16 58 FeatureStore A centralized store for computed ML features ML & Data Pipelines 16 59 TestSuite A collection of related test cases Testing 11 60 TestCoverage Code coverage metrics for a component or module Testing 11 61 TestAssertion (inline) An individual assertion within a test case Testing 11 62 StateStore A frontend state management store or container Frontend Supporting 12 63 UIProperty (inline) A property (prop) passed to a UI component Frontend Supporting 12 64 ConcurrencyPattern A high-level concurrency pattern used in the system Frontend Supporting 15 Total: 64 classes (including 3 Interface subtypes, 1 Component subtype, and 1 Rule subtype that inherit from parents). entries.text: Layer 3: Component-Level Representation This document defines the SAO v2.0 classes that correspond to C4 Level 3 (Component) -- the logical building blocks inside a deployable unit, their responsibilities, and relationships. This layer sits between the code (Layer 4) and the container/service boundary (Layer 2). Where Layer 4 answers "what does the source code look like?", Layer 3 answers "what are the logical parts of this application, what do they do, and how do they interact?" Scope Layer 3 covers: Component architecture -- logical building blocks, operations they expose, capabilities and features they provide Domain model -- aggregates, entities, value objects, their attributes, relationships, and lifecycle Behavior and workflow -- actions, rules, events, workflows, and transactions Authorization and policy -- roles, permissions, policies, scopes, and constraints Supporting structures -- schemas, tests, annotations, imports, concurrency, and UI components Unlike Layer 4, which splits into Modern and Legacy profiles based on programming paradigm, Layer 3 is largely paradigm-agnostic. A COBOL batch system and a Java microservice both have components, domain entities, business rules, and authorization models. The differences emerge in how these concepts are implemented (Layer 4), not in what they are (Layer 3). The one exception is UIComponent, which specifically models modern component-tree UI frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) -- with concepts like props, lazy loading, server rendering, route binding, state store management, and parent/child component hierarchies. Legacy terminal screens (CICS BMS maps, RPG display files, MFS formats) are a fundamentally different model -- fixed-grid character maps with positional fields compiled from source members -- and are fully captured at Layer 4 via ScreenDefinition/ScreenField. This creates a deliberate asymmetry: modern UI has representation at both Layer 3 (UIComponent as a logical building block) and Layer 4 (EncapsulationUnit for the source file), while legacy UI lives entirely at Layer 4 (ScreenDefinition as a compiled source artifact). Summary # Class Definition Group SAO Section 1 Component A logical building block within a module or service, grouping related operations Component Architecture 2 2 Operation A named, invocable unit of behavior exposed via a component's interface Component Architecture 6 3 Capability A business capability the system provides, realized by features and requiring permissions Component Architecture 2
