entries.text: Layer 4: Code-Level Representation This document defines the SAO v2.0 classes that correspond to C4 Level 4 (Code) -- a faithful, close-to-code representation of a software codebase as written: source files, their internal structure, and the relationships between code elements. It does not cover architectural abstractions (Components, BoundedContexts), runtime behavior (Deployments, Environments), or operational concerns (Observability, Compliance). The document covers 21 primary classes and 8 supporting classes (29 total). Two profiles are defined: Modern (OOP, functional, and multi-paradigm languages) and Legacy (COBOL, RPG, PL/I, Assembler, and other procedural/mainframe languages). The profiles share a common core and diverge where the programming models differ. Summary # Class Definition Modern Legacy SAO Section 1 CodeContainer A physical container of source code -- a file, library member, or other storage unit Yes Yes 12 2 StorageLocation A logical or physical location for storing code containers (directory, PDS library, package) Yes Yes 12 3 EncapsulationUnit A logical boundary grouping related code and data (class, module, program, copybook) Yes Yes 12 4 CallableUnit A named, invocable unit of code (method, function, paragraph, procedure, lambda) Yes Yes 12 5 DataStructure A composite data type grouping related data elements (struct, record, group item, DTO) Yes Yes 12 6 DataElement An individual data field, variable, or constant Yes Yes 12 7 Parameter An input/output parameter for a callable unit Yes Yes 12 8 ControlFlow Control flow between code elements -- calls, branches, jumps Yes Yes 12 9 DataFlow Data flow between code elements -- reads, writes, assignments Yes Yes 12 10 TypeExpression A recursive type model for complex types (generics, unions, pointers, function types) Yes -- 18 11 ExceptionType A declared exception or error type with hierarchy support Yes -- 19 12 Operation A named, invocable unit of behavior exposed via a component's interface (API endpoint) Yes -- 6 13 FileDefinition A file defined for I/O in a program (COBOL SELECT/FD, VSAM dataset) -- Yes 20 14 FileOperation An individual I/O operation on a file (READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE) -- Yes 20 15 ScreenDefinition A terminal screen or map definition (BMS map, RPG display file, MFS format) -- Yes 21 16 ScreenField An individual field on a terminal screen with row/column position -- Yes 21 17 JobDefinition A batch job definition (JCL JOB, scheduler entry) -- Yes 22 18 JobStep A single step within a batch job (JCL EXEC statement) -- Yes 22 19 DatasetAllocation A dataset allocation within a job step (JCL DD statement) -- Yes 22 20 IPCConnection A communication link between two programs or processes (CICS LINK, shared memory, pipes) -- Yes 23 21 PreprocessorDirective A preprocessor directive or metaprogramming construct (COPY REPLACING, #ifdef, macros) -- Yes 24 Supporting classes 22 CodeBlock A logical grouping of statements within a callable unit (conditional, loop, try-catch) Yes Yes 12 23 Statement A single executable instruction or declaration with line number Yes Yes 12 24 ProgrammingLanguage A programming language with paradigms, type discipline, and runtime characteristics Yes Yes 28 25 ErrorModel Describes how a module or language handles errors (exceptions, error codes, monadic, etc.) Yes Yes 19 26 MemoryModel Describes how a language or module manages memory (GC, manual, ownership) Yes Yes 25 27 OwnershipAnnotation An ownership or lifetime annotation on a data element (Rust borrows, C++ smart pointers) Yes -- 25 28 PlatformExtension Abstract base for platform-specific extensions Yes Yes 12 29 ExecutionEnvironmentDirective Platform-specific execution directives (Docker Compose, K8s manifests, Makefiles) Yes Yes 12 Primary classes: Modern 12, Legacy 18, Shared core 9. Supporting classes: 8 (shared across both profiles). entries.text: SAO Extraction Playbook: Overview This document series is a step-by-step playbook for decomposing any software codebase into SAO-conformant YAML. It covers modern cloud-native applications, legacy mainframe systems, and everything in between. How to use this series Audience. These documents are written for both software engineers performing manual extraction and LLM agents (e.g., Claude Code) performing automated extraction. The term "extraction agent" refers to whoever or whatever is performing the work. Reading path. Start here, then follow the phases in order. Each phase document is self-contained: it states its inputs, outputs, steps, and the SAO classes it populates. Once you are familiar with the overall flow, you can use individual phase documents as standalone references. Notation conventions. This series follows the formatting conventions established in the SAO documentation: Bold for class and entity names in prose (e.g., ControlFlow, DataStore, Actor) Monospace for enum values, attribute names, and literal identifiers (e.g., web_ui, rest_api, contained_in_unit) Dotted.path references in monospace (e.g., Component.implemented_by_code) RFC 2119 keywords. Throughout this series: MUST — required for a valid SAO instance SHOULD — strongly recommended; omission requires justification MAY — optional enrichment that adds value but is not required Prerequisites and inputs Before starting extraction, gather the following: Required inputs Input Purpose Full source tree Repository access (all branches relevant to the extraction scope) Build manifests pom.xml, package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, Makefile, JCL procs, etc. Dependency lock files package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock, etc. Strongly recommended inputs Input Purpose Deployment manifests Dockerfiles, Kubernetes YAML, docker-compose, serverless configs, JCL API schemas OpenAPI, GraphQL, gRPC .proto, WSDL Database schemas DDL scripts, migration files, ORM model definitions Documentation READMEs, wikis, ADRs, API docs, runbooks CI/CD configs GitHub Actions, Jenkinsfile, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines IaC definitions Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi Optional inputs (if available) Input Purpose Runtime telemetry Logs, traces, APM data Config files application.yml, .env, feature flag configs Test suites Test files, coverage reports Identification checklist Before extraction begins, identify and record: Programming language(s) present in the repository Build system (Maven, Gradle, npm, Cargo, Make, etc.) Package manager and dependency resolution mechanism Deployment model (containers, VMs, mainframe LPAR, serverless, bare metal) External dependencies visible from configuration (databases, message brokers, third-party APIs) Architectural style if apparent (monolith, microservices, modular monolith, mainframe batch/online) Tools needed Tool category Purpose Phase Language-appropriate AST parser Code structure extraction Phase 2 LinkML validator (linkml-validate) Schema validation Phase 9 (Validation) LLM with large context window Semantic inference Phases 4-5 YAML serializer Output generation All phases Extraction philosophy Bottom-up, then top-down Extract the mechanical layers first, then infer the semantic layers from them. Code structure (Layer 3) is deterministic — a parser can extract it with near-perfect accuracy. Architecture (Layer 4) is heuristic — it can be inferred from code organization with high confidence. Domain model (Layer 5) and business intent (Layer 6) are inferential — they require semantic reasoning and human validation. This matches the SAO guide's core insight: Layers 3 and 4 are largely structural (you can derive them from code organization and dependency graphs), while layers 5 and 6 require semantic understanding (recognizing business meaning in code patterns). Confidence gradient Each extraction phase operates at a different confidence level: Confidence Meaning Phases Deterministic Extracted directly from AST; no interpretation needed Phase 1, Phase 2 Heuristic Inferred from structural patterns with high confidence Phase 3 Inferential Requires semantic reasoning; may need correction Phases 4-5 Manual Requires human domain expert validation Parts of Phases 5-6 When populating SAO instances, the extraction agent SHOULD be aware of which confidence level applies and flag inferential results for human review. Incremental extraction You do not need to extract everything at once. Start with a single bounded context or module, complete it through all phases, then expand. This approach: Validates your extraction process on a manageable scope Produces usable output quickly Reveals gaps in your tooling or understanding early Idempotency Re-running a phase with the same inputs SHOULD produce the same outputs. Phases should be designed as deterministic transformations wherever possible, with non-deterministic steps (LLM inference) clearly marked. Phase dependency map The eight extraction phases execute in a defined order. Each phase consumes the outputs of prior phases. Phase 1: Inventory ─────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ v │ Phase 2: Code Structure (Layer 3) ──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ v │ │ Phase 3: Architecture (Layers 2/4) ─────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ │ ├───> Phase 4: Domain Model (Layer 5) │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ v │ │ │ ├───> Phase 5: Business Intent (Layer 6) │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ├───> Phase 6: Cross-Cutting ◄───────────┘ │ │ │ (parallel with 3-5) │ │ v │ │ Phase 7: Bridge Stitching ◄──────────────────────┘ │ │ (requires all prior) │ v │ Phase 8: System Context (Layer 1) ◄──────────────────┘ │ (capstone) v Validation (doc 09) Phase summary table Phase Doc SAO layers Primary technique Automation Key outputs 1. entries.text: Phase 1: Inventory and Language Identification Input: Raw repository (source tree, build manifests, lock files) Output: StorageLocation hierarchy, skeletal CodeContainer instances, ProgrammingLanguage instances, PackageManager, PackageDependency 1. Overview Phase 1 is the first extraction phase and the most mechanical. It walks the repository file tree and produces a complete inventory of where code lives, what languages are used, and what external packages the project depends on. Every subsequent phase builds on this inventory. This phase is fully automatable and deterministic: given the same repository, it MUST produce the same output. No semantic reasoning is required -- only file-system traversal, extension mapping, and manifest parsing. Why it comes first: every later phase needs to know which files exist, where they are, and what language they are written in. The StorageLocation hierarchy anchors the physical structure; CodeContainer instances become the targets that Phase 2 populates with parsed code elements. 2. Step 1: Build the StorageLocation hierarchy Walk the repository file tree top-down. For each directory (or platform-equivalent namespace/package), create a StorageLocation instance. Required attributes Attribute Type Description name string Directory or namespace name (e.g., src, controllers, com.example.orders) location_path string (required) Relative path from the repository root (e.g., src/main/java/com/example) location_type StorageLocationType One of the permissible values below location_type permissible values directory -- standard filesystem directory library -- partitioned dataset or library (mainframe PDS) package -- language-level package (e.g., Java package, Python package with __init__.py) namespace -- language-level namespace (e.g., C# namespace, C++ namespace) module_path -- Go module path or similar module-level path The extraction agent MUST choose the most specific applicable value. For a Java project, src/main/java/com/example/orders SHOULD be typed as package; its parent src/main/java SHOULD be typed as directory. Establishing the hierarchy Set has_parent_location on each child to reference its parent StorageLocation. Set contains_locations on each parent to list its children. The root StorageLocation (the repository root) has no has_parent_location. Module mapping The attribute maps_to_module links a StorageLocation to a Module instance. In Phase 1, this SHOULD be left empty unless the mapping is unambiguous (e.g., a Go module root, a Python package with a clear __init__.py). Module identification is the responsibility of Phase 3. Directories to skip The extraction agent SHOULD skip directories that do not contain meaningful source code: Version control directories (.git, .svn, .hg) Dependency directories (node_modules, vendor, .venv, target, build, dist) IDE directories (.idea, .vscode -- unless extracting IDE configuration is in scope) 3. Step 2: Create CodeContainer instances For each source file in the repository, create a CodeContainer instance. Non-source files (binary assets, images, fonts) SHOULD be excluded unless they are relevant to the application's structure (e.g., compiled protobuf files). Required and recommended attributes Attribute Type Required Description name string inherited File name without path (e.g., UserService.java) container_path string yes Full relative path from repository root (e.g., src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java) container_type CodeContainerType recommended Mapped from file extension (see table below) line_count integer recommended Total lines in the file size_bytes integer optional File size in bytes encoding string optional Character encoding (e.g., utf-8, ebcdic) container_type permissible values source_file -- standard source code file library_member -- member of a partitioned dataset or library (mainframe) include_file -- shared definitions file (C/C++ header, COBOL copybook) script -- standalone script (shell, Python script, etc.) configuration -- configuration file (application.yml, .env, etc.) schema_definition -- schema file (OpenAPI, GraphQL, Protobuf, DDL) notebook_cell -- Jupyter notebook or similar inline_code -- inline code embedded in another artifact jcl_member -- JCL member in a PDS rpg_source -- RPG source member pli_source -- PL/I source member assembler_source -- assembler source member cl_source -- IBM CL (Control Language) source Extension-to-type mapping heuristic The extraction agent SHOULD use file extensions to assign container_type. The following table covers common cases: Extensions container_type .java, .py, .rs, .go, .ts, .js, .c, .cpp, .cs, .rb, .kt, .swift, .scala source_file .h, .hpp, .hxx include_file .cpy, .cbl, .cob source_file (COBOL) or include_file (copybook) .sh, .bash, .ps1, .bat, .cmd script .yml, .yaml, .json, .toml, .ini, .cfg, .properties, .env configuration .proto, .graphql, .gql, .xsd, .wsdl, .avsc schema_definition .ipynb notebook_cell .jcl jcl_member .rpg, .rpgle rpg_source .pli pli_source .asm, .s assembler_source .clp, .clle cl_source When a file extension is ambiguous (e.g., .json could be configuration or schema), the extraction agent SHOULD default to configuration and let later phases reclassify. Linking to StorageLocation Each CodeContainer MUST set contained_in_storage_location to reference the StorageLocation for the directory that contains it. The inverse attribute contains_containers on the StorageLocation MUST also be populated. Linking to language The attribute written_in_language links a CodeContainer to a ProgrammingLanguage instance. Populate this after Step 3 creates the language instances. 4. Step 3: Identify programming languages Scan the CodeContainer instances created in Step 2. For each distinct programming language found, create a single ProgrammingLanguage instance. Attributes Attribute Type Description name string Language name (e.g., Java, Python, Rust, COBOL) paradigms ProgrammingParadigm (multivalued) Paradigms the language supports type_discipline string Type system characterization (e.g., static_strong, dynamic_strong) has_preprocessor boolean Whether the language has a preprocessor (e.g., true for C/C++) has_gc boolean Whether the language has garbage collection year_introduced integer Year the language was first released (optional) paradigms permissible values object_oriented procedural functional logic concatenative data_driven multi_paradigm Common language profiles Language paradigms type_discipline has_gc has_preprocessor Java object_oriented, multi_paradigm static_strong true false Python object_oriented, procedural, functional, multi_paradigm dynamic_strong true false TypeScript object_oriented, functional, multi_paradigm static_strong true false C procedural static_weak false true C++ object_oriented, procedural, functional, multi_paradigm static_strong false true Rust functional, procedural, multi_paradigm static_strong false true Go procedural, multi_paradigm static_strong true false COBOL procedural static_strong false true Linking containers to languages After creating all ProgrammingLanguage instances, iterate over every CodeContainer and set written_in_language to the appropriate language based on file extension. The inverse attribute language_used_by_containers on the ProgrammingLanguage instance lists all containers using that language. Configuration files, schema definitions, and other non-source containers MAY have written_in_language left empty, or MAY reference a markup/data language if one has been created (e.g., a YAML language instance). 5. Step 4: Parse dependency manifests Identify build and dependency manifest files in the repository. For each package manager detected, create a PackageManager instance; for each declared dependency, create a PackageDependency instance. Identifying manifests Manifest file manager_type package.json npm requirements.txt, setup.py, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml (with pip/setuptools) pip pom.xml maven build.gradle, build.gradle.kts gradle Cargo.toml cargo *.csproj, *.sln (with NuGet references) nuget go.mod go_modules Gemfile bundler composer.json composer conanfile.txt, conanfile.py conan PackageManager attributes Attribute Type Description name string Descriptive name (e.g., npm, Maven Central) manager_type PackageManagerType (required) One of: npm, pip, maven, gradle, nuget, cargo, go_modules, bundler, composer, conan, none manifest_file string Path to the manifest file (e.g., package.json) lock_file string Path to the lock file (e.g., package-lock.json) registry_url URI Package registry URL (e.g., https://registry.npmjs.org) PackageDependency attributes Attribute Type Description name string Instance name for the dependency package_name string (required) Package identifier (e.g., express, spring-boot-starter-web) version_constraint string Declared version range (e.g., ^4.18.0, >=3.0,<4.0) resolved_version string Actual resolved version from lock file (e.g., 4.18.2) scope DependencyScope One of the values below is_direct boolean true for direct dependencies, false for transitive license string SPDX license identifier if known (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0) scope permissible values production -- required at runtime development -- development-only tooling test -- test-only dependencies build -- build-time only optional -- optional/feature-gated provided -- expected to be provided by the runtime environment Scope mapping from ecosystems Ecosystem Production Development Test npm dependencies devDependencies (convention-based) Maven compile scope -- test scope Gradle implementation -- testImplementation pip main requirements requirements-dev.txt requirements-test.txt Cargo [dependencies] -- [dev-dependencies] Linking dependencies PackageDependency links to a Module via dependency_of_module, and PackageManager links to a Module via manages_dependencies_for_module. In Phase 1, if a Module has not yet been created (modules are identified in Phase 3), the extraction agent SHOULD defer these links and record the association for later stitching. For transitive dependencies (from lock files), set is_direct to false and use has_transitive_dependencies / transitive_dependency_of to establish the dependency graph between PackageDependency instances. In Phase 1, the extraction agent SHOULD focus on direct dependencies. Transitive dependencies MAY be extracted from lock files if available, but full transitive graph construction is optional. 6. YAML output example The following example shows Phase 1 output for a small Node.js project with three directories, four source files, one language, and three dependencies. # Phase 1 output: Inventory # Project: my-api storage_locations: - name: my-api location_path: "." location_type: directory contains_locations: - src-dir - src-routes-dir contains_containers: - package-json - id: src-dir name: src location_path: src location_type: directory parent_location: my-api contains_locations: - src-routes-dir contains_containers: - app-ts - db-ts - id: src-routes-dir name: routes location_path: src/routes location_type: directory parent_location: src-dir contains_containers: - users-ts code_containers: - name: package.json container_path: package.json container_type: configuration line_count: 28 contained_in_storage_location: my-api - id: app-ts name: app.ts container_path: src/app.ts container_type: source_file line_count: 45 contained_in_storage_location: src-dir written_in_language: typescript-lang - id: db-ts name: db.ts container_path: src/db.ts container_type: source_file line_count: 22 contained_in_storage_location: src-dir written_in_language: typescript-lang - id: users-ts name: users.ts container_path: src/routes/users.ts container_type: source_file line_count: 67 contained_in_storage_location: src-routes-dir written_in_language: typescript-lang programming_languages: - id: typescript-lang name: TypeScript paradigms: - object_oriented - functional - multi_paradigm type_discipline: static_strong has_gc: true has_preprocessor: false language_used_by_containers: - app-ts - db-ts - users-ts package_managers: - name: npm manager_type: npm manifest_file: package.json lock_file: package-lock.json registry_url: https://registry.npmjs.org package_dependencies: - name: express-dep package_name: express version_constraint: "^4.18.0" resolved_version: "4.18.2" scope: production is_direct: true license: MIT - name: pg-dep package_name: pg version_constraint: "^8.11.0" resolved_version: "8.11.3" scope: production is_direct: true license: MIT - name: typescript-dep package_name: typescript version_constraint: "^5.2.0" resolved_version: "5.3.3" scope: development is_direct: true license: Apache-2.0 7. Checklist After Phase 1 completes, verify the following: [ ] Every source-relevant directory has a StorageLocation instance [ ] The StorageLocation hierarchy (via has_parent_location / contains_locations) matches the actual directory structure [ ] Every source file has a CodeContainer instance with container_path and container_type set [ ] Every CodeContainer is linked to its parent StorageLocation via contained_in_storage_location [ ] Every source-code CodeContainer has written_in_language set to a ProgrammingLanguage instance [ ] At least one ProgrammingLanguage instance exists with paradigms and type_discipline populated [ ] All build/dependency manifest files have been identified [ ] A PackageManager instance exists for each package manager detected [ ] All direct dependencies are captured as PackageDependency instances with package_name, version_constraint, and scope [ ] No files from excluded directories (node_modules, .git, vendor, etc.) are included When all items pass, proceed to Phase 2: Code Structure.

headings.title: Sub-phase 2c: Data Structures and Data Elements

entries.text: Phase 2: Code Structure (Layer 3) This phase populates SAO Layer 3 --- the direct structural representation of source code. It is the largest and most critical extraction phase: every subsequent phase depends on the code structure graph built here. Confidence level: Deterministic. No inference is needed; this phase captures what the code literally says. AST parsing is the primary technique, achieving ~90% automation. Input: Phase 1 outputs --- StorageLocation, CodeContainer, ProgrammingLanguage instances. Output: EncapsulationUnit, CallableUnit, DataStructure, DataElement, Parameter, TypeExpression, ControlFlow, DataFlow, DefinitionReference, CodeBlock, Statement, Annotation, plus platform-specific extension classes. Containment hierarchy Phase 2 builds the structural spine of the SAO model. Every element produced here lives within this containment hierarchy: StorageLocation └── CodeContainer └── EncapsulationUnit ├── CallableUnit │ ├── Parameter │ ├── CodeBlock │ │ └── Statement │ ├── ControlFlow (edges) │ └── DataFlow (edges) ├── DataStructure │ └── DataElement │ └── TypeExpression ├── DataElement (unit-level fields) └── DefinitionReference The extraction agent MUST process sub-phases in order (2a through 2h) because later sub-phases reference entities created in earlier ones. Sub-phase 2a: Encapsulation Units Parse each CodeContainer using a language-appropriate AST parser and create an EncapsulationUnit for every class, module, program, package, trait, or interface found. Required attributes Attribute Range Rule encapsulation_type EncapsulationType MUST set. See enum values below. qualified_name string MUST set to the fully qualified name (e.g., com.example.UserService). visibility VisibilityType SHOULD set when the language has visibility modifiers. is_abstract boolean SHOULD set for abstract classes, interfaces, and traits. is_final boolean SHOULD set when the language supports sealed/final. is_reusable boolean MAY set if the unit is designed for reuse (libraries, shared modules). stereotype string MAY set to indicate a pattern role (e.g., Service, Repository, Controller, DTO). line_start / line_end integer SHOULD set for source-level traceability. EncapsulationType enum (33 values) Object-oriented: - class - interface - abstract_class - trait - enum_class - record_class - singleton Procedural: - program - subprogram - unit Functional / organizational: - module - namespace - package - library Component / pattern: - object - component - service - controller - script - composite - other Database: - stored_procedure - function_package - trigger - view Mainframe: - batch_program - online_program - copybook - rpg_module - rpg_service_program - pli_procedure - pli_package - assembler_csect Required relationships Relationship Target Rule defined_in_container CodeContainer MUST link every unit to its source container. extends_units EncapsulationUnit MUST set for inheritance (e.g., Java extends, Python base classes). implements_contracts Contract MUST set for interface implementation (e.g., Java implements, Rust impl Trait). contains_callable_units CallableUnit Populated in sub-phase 2b. contains_data_structures DataStructure Populated in sub-phase 2c. contains_data_elements DataElement For unit-level fields not inside a DataStructure. uses_definitions DefinitionReference Populated in sub-phase 2d. VisibilityType enum public private protected internal package Procedure For each CodeContainer, invoke the AST parser for the container's language (determined via written_in_language). Walk the top-level AST nodes. For each class/module/program/trait/interface/enum/record declaration, create an EncapsulationUnit. For nested types (inner classes, companion objects), create a separate EncapsulationUnit and record the nesting relationship via a second defined_in_container link to the same CodeContainer. Resolve inheritance: set extends_units to the parent EncapsulationUnit by matching qualified names. If the parent is in an external dependency, create a stub EncapsulationUnit with a qualified_name only. Resolve interface implementation: set implements_contracts to the corresponding Contract instance. If no Contract exists yet, create one. Example # Java class with inheritance and interface implementation order_service: a: EncapsulationUnit name: OrderService encapsulation_type: class visibility: public qualified_name: com.example.orders.OrderService is_abstract: false is_final: false stereotype: Service line_start: 15 line_end: 280 defined_in_container: order_service_file extends_units: - base_service implements_contracts: - order_operations_contract # COBOL batch program payroll_calc: a: EncapsulationUnit name: PAYROLL-CALC encapsulation_type: batch_program qualified_name: PAYROLL-CALC defined_in_container: payroll_calc_source Sub-phase 2b: Callable Units For each EncapsulationUnit, extract every method, function, paragraph, procedure, or other invocable construct. Required attributes Attribute Range Rule callable_type CallableType MUST set. See enum values below. visibility VisibilityType SHOULD set when the language has visibility modifiers. return_type string SHOULD set (use the source-level type name as-is). has_return_type TypeExpression MAY set for structured type modeling (see sub-phase 2c). is_async boolean MUST set to true for async/await functions. is_static boolean MUST set to true for static/class methods. is_pure boolean MAY set if determinable (no side effects). is_virtual boolean SHOULD set for virtual/overridable methods. is_override boolean SHOULD set for methods that override a parent. is_recursive boolean MAY set if the callable calls itself. is_inline boolean MAY set for inline functions. complexity_score integer SHOULD compute cyclomatic complexity. entry_point_type EntryPointType MUST set for program entry points. documentation string MAY extract from docstrings/Javadoc. line_start / line_end integer SHOULD set for source-level traceability. CallableType enum (53 values) Object-oriented methods: - method - static_method - constructor - destructor - property_getter - property_setter - operator_overload - conversion_operator - indexer - abstract_method - virtual_method Procedural: - function - procedure - subroutine - paragraph - section - rpg_subprocedure - pli_entry - assembler_entry - rpg_subroutine Functional: - lambda - closure - higher_order_function - curried_function - functor Event handling: - event_handler - callback - delegate - signal_handler Database: - stored_procedure - stored_function - trigger_body - cursor Concurrency: - coroutine - generator - async_function - thread_entry - task Testing: - test_case - test_fixture - mock Other: - macro - template - generic_method - main_entry - interrupt_handler - exception_handler - finalizer - factory_method - extension_method - script_function - command - other EntryPointType enum main_program transaction_entry event_handler scheduled_entry api_endpoint CallableCategory enum The callable_category attribute classifies a callable's behavioral role: normal operator main_entry Required relationships Relationship Target Rule contained_in_unit EncapsulationUnit MUST link every callable to its containing unit. has_parameters Parameter Populated below. overrides_callable CallableUnit MUST set when a method overrides a parent method. invokes_callables CallableUnit Populated in sub-phase 2e. accesses_data_elements DataElement Populated in sub-phase 2f. modifies_data_elements DataElement Populated in sub-phase 2f. Parameters For each parameter of a CallableUnit, create a Parameter instance. Parameter inherits from DataElement and adds: Attribute Range Rule direction ParameterDirection SHOULD set. Values: input, output, input_output, return. position integer MUST set (0-based or 1-based, be consistent). passing_mechanism PassingMechanism SHOULD set. Values: by_value, by_reference, by_name, by_result. has_type TypeExpression MAY set for structured type modeling. data_type string SHOULD set (inherited from DataElement; use source-level type name). is_nullable boolean SHOULD set when determinable. default_value string SHOULD set when a default is declared. Link each Parameter back via parameter_of to its CallableUnit. Procedure For each EncapsulationUnit, walk the AST children that are callable declarations. Create a CallableUnit for each, setting callable_type based on the AST node kind. For each parameter in the callable's signature, create a Parameter and link via has_parameters / parameter_of. Compute complexity_score if the AST parser supports control-flow analysis. For main functions, __init__ methods, or COBOL PROCEDURE DIVISION, set entry_point_type. Example # Java method with parameters create_order: a: CallableUnit name: createOrder callable_type: method visibility: public return_type: Order is_async: false is_static: false complexity_score: 12 line_start: 45 line_end: 92 contained_in_unit: order_service has_parameters: - create_order_request_param - create_order_user_param create_order_request_param: a: Parameter name: request data_type: CreateOrderRequest direction: input position: 1 passing_mechanism: by_value is_nullable: false parameter_of: create_order create_order_user_param: a: Parameter name: currentUser data_type: User direction: input position: 2 passing_mechanism: by_value is_nullable: false parameter_of: create_order # COBOL paragraph calc_totals: a: CallableUnit name: CALCULATE-TOTALS callable_type: paragraph contained_in_unit: payroll_calc Sub-phase 2c: Data Structures and Data Elements Extract struct/record/group declarations and their fields from each EncapsulationUnit. DataStructure attributes Attribute Range Rule structure_type DataStructureType MUST set. See enum values below. structure_category DataStructureCategory SHOULD set. visibility VisibilityType SHOULD set. is_mutable boolean SHOULD set. is_serializable boolean MAY set. is_nested boolean MUST set to true for nested/inner structures. nesting_level integer MUST set for COBOL group items (01, 05, 10, etc.). is_packed boolean MAY set for packed structs. alignment integer MAY set for explicit alignment. size_bytes integer MAY set when determinable. persistence_type PersistenceType MAY set (e.g., transient, database, file, memory, cache). line_start / line_end integer SHOULD set. DataStructureType enum (50 values) Object-oriented: - class_data - inner_class - anonymous_class Procedural: - struct - record - union COBOL / Mainframe: - group_item - copybook_structure - commarea - linkage_section - rpg_data_structure - pli_structure - assembler_dsect - cobol_file_descriptor Functional: - algebraic_data_type - type_class - product_type - sum_type Collections: - array - dynamic_array - list - dictionary - set - queue - stack - tree - graph Database: - table_structure - view_structure - cursor_structure - rowtype DDD: - value_object - dto Other: - tuple - pair - enum - flags - configuration_object - message - event - command - json_schema - xml_schema - protobuf_message - avro_record - smart_pointer - reference_wrapper - opaque_type - variant - other DataStructureCategory enum composite collection hierarchical value_type reference_type union DataStructure relationships Relationship Target Rule contained_in_unit EncapsulationUnit MUST link to the containing unit. structure_contains_elements DataElement Populated below. has_parent_structure DataStructure MUST set for nested structures. has_child_structures DataStructure Inverse of has_parent_structure. DataElement attributes For each field, variable, or constant within a DataStructure (or directly within an EncapsulationUnit), create a DataElement. Attribute Range Rule data_type string MUST set (source-level type name). element_category DataElementCategory SHOULD set. visibility VisibilityType SHOULD set. is_constant boolean MUST set to true for constants/finals. is_nullable boolean SHOULD set when determinable. default_value string SHOULD set when a default is declared. size_specification string SHOULD set for COBOL PIC clauses or array dimensions. storage_class StorageClass MAY set. Values: automatic, static, heap, register, thread_local, external. classification DataClassificationType MAY set for data governance. line_number integer SHOULD set. DataElementCategory enum field static_field local_variable parameter constant global_variable computed temporary DataElement relationships Relationship Target Rule contained_in_structure DataStructure MUST link when element belongs to a structure. contained_in_unit EncapsulationUnit MUST link when element is at the unit level. has_parent_element DataElement MUST set for COBOL hierarchical data items. has_child_elements DataElement Inverse of has_parent_element. declared_type TypeExpression MAY set for structured type modeling. TypeExpression For complex types (generics, unions, optional wrappers, function types), create a TypeExpression. Attribute Range Rule type_kind TypeKind MUST set. base_type string MUST set (e.g., List, int, String). has_type_parameters TypeExpression[] MUST set for generic types (recursive). type_constraints string[] MAY set (e.g., T: Comparable). is_nullable boolean SHOULD set. nullability_model string MAY set (e.g., option_type, nullable_annotation). pointer_semantics string MAY set for pointer types (e.g., raw, smart, weak). TypeKind enum primitive generic union intersection alias pointer reference array_of function_type tuple_type optional_type constrained opaque Procedure For each EncapsulationUnit, walk its AST children for struct/record/class-data/enum declarations. Create a DataStructure for each, choosing structure_type based on the language construct. For each field within the structure, create a DataElement and link via structure_contains_elements / contained_in_structure. For fields at the unit level (e.g., Java class fields not inside an inner struct), link directly via contains_data_elements on the EncapsulationUnit. For complex types, create a TypeExpression and link via declared_type on the DataElement. For COBOL group items, preserve the level-number hierarchy using has_parent_element / has_child_elements. Example # Java DTO with fields and a generic type order_data: a: DataStructure name: Order structure_type: class_data structure_category: composite visibility: public is_mutable: true contained_in_unit: order_entity structure_contains_elements: - order_id_field - order_items_field - order_total_field order_id_field: a: DataElement name: id data_type: Long element_category: field visibility: private is_constant: false is_nullable: false contained_in_structure: order_data order_items_field: a: DataElement name: items data_type: "List<OrderItem>" element_category: field visibility: private is_constant: false is_nullable: false contained_in_structure: order_data declared_type: list_of_order_item list_of_order_item: a: TypeExpression name: "List<OrderItem>" type_kind: generic base_type: List type_parameters: - a: TypeExpression name: OrderItem type_kind: primitive base_type: OrderItem order_total_field: a: DataElement name: total data_type: BigDecimal element_category: field visibility: private is_constant: false is_nullable: false default_value: "0.00" contained_in_structure: order_data # COBOL group item with hierarchy employee_record: a: DataStructure name: EMPLOYEE-RECORD structure_type: group_item nesting_level: 1 contained_in_unit: payroll_calc emp_name: a: DataElement name: EMP-NAME data_type: "PIC X(30)" element_category: field size_specification: "PIC X(30)" contained_in_structure: employee_record parent_element: null emp_salary: a: DataElement name: EMP-SALARY data_type: "PIC 9(7)V99" element_category: field size_specification: "PIC 9(7)V99" contained_in_structure: employee_record Sub-phase 2d: Definition References Create a DefinitionReference for each import, include, COPY, using, or require statement. Attributes Attribute Range Rule reference_type ReferenceType MUST set. reference_path string MUST set (the import path or module name as written in source). alias string SHOULD set when an alias is used (e.g., Python import x as y). is_wildcard boolean MUST set to true for wildcard imports (e.g., import java.util.*). scope string MAY set to indicate the scope of the import. ReferenceType enum import_module import_symbol include_source inherit implement Relationships Relationship Target Rule referencing_container CodeContainer MUST link to the source file performing the import. referenced_container CodeContainer SHOULD link to the target file being imported (when resolvable). imports_symbols EncapsulationUnit / CallableUnit / DataStructure SHOULD set to the specific entities imported. Procedure Walk each CodeContainer's AST for import/include/COPY/using/require statements. Create a DefinitionReference for each statement. Resolve referenced_container by matching the import path to known CodeContainer instances from Phase 1. If the import targets a specific symbol, set imports_symbols to the corresponding EncapsulationUnit, CallableUnit, or DataStructure. Link the DefinitionReference to the containing EncapsulationUnit via EncapsulationUnit.uses_definitions. Example # Python import import_order_model: a: DefinitionReference name: "from models.order import Order" reference_type: import_symbol reference_path: models.order is_wildcard: false referencing_container: order_service_file referenced_container: order_model_file imports_symbols: - order_entity # COBOL COPY statement copy_employee_record: a: DefinitionReference name: "COPY EMPREC" reference_type: include_source reference_path: EMPREC is_wildcard: false referencing_container: payroll_calc_source referenced_container: emprec_copybook # Java wildcard import import_java_util: a: DefinitionReference name: "import java.util.*" reference_type: import_module reference_path: java.util is_wildcard: true referencing_container: order_service_file Sub-phase 2e: Call Graph (ControlFlow) For each CallableUnit, identify what it calls and build the call graph using ControlFlow edges. Attributes Attribute Range Rule flow_type ControlFlowType MUST set. is_conditional boolean SHOULD set to true if the call is inside a conditional branch. condition string MAY set to the guard expression (e.g., if user != null). ControlFlowType enum call async_call branch jump return throw yield Relationships Relationship Target Rule has_source_callable CallableUnit MUST set (the caller). has_target_callable CallableUnit MUST set (the callee). has_source_statement Statement MAY set for statement-level precision. has_target_statement Statement MAY set for statement-level precision. Bidirectional call links In addition to ControlFlow edge entities, the extraction agent MUST also populate: CallableUnit.invokes_callables --- the list of callables this one calls CallableUnit.invoked_by_callables --- the inverse (auto-populated if using LinkML inverse) These provide direct navigation without querying ControlFlow entities. Procedure For each CallableUnit, walk its AST body for call expressions, method invocations, and PERFORM statements. Resolve each call target to a known CallableUnit by matching name and scope. Create a ControlFlow edge with flow_type: call (or async_call for awaited calls). Also append the target to invokes_callables on the source CallableUnit. For unresolvable calls (external libraries, dynamic dispatch), create a stub CallableUnit with the name and mark it as external. Example # Direct method call call_create_to_validate: a: ControlFlow name: createOrder_calls_validateOrder flow_type: call is_conditional: false source_callable: create_order target_callable: validate_order # Conditional async call call_notify_async: a: ControlFlow name: createOrder_calls_notifyAsync flow_type: async_call is_conditional: true condition: "order.requiresNotification()" source_callable: create_order target_callable: send_notification # Update the source callable's invocation list create_order: a: CallableUnit # ... (other attributes from sub-phase 2b) invokes_callables: - validate_order - calculate_total - save_order - send_notification Sub-phase 2f: Data Flow For each CallableUnit, identify which DataElements it reads, writes, or transforms, and create DataFlow edges. Attributes Attribute Range Rule flow_type DataFlowType MUST set. DataFlowType enum read write modify define use Relationships Relationship Target Rule has_source_element DataElement MUST set (the data being read from or defined). has_target_element DataElement MUST set (the data being written to or consumed). has_through_callable CallableUnit SHOULD set (the callable performing the flow). has_through_statement Statement MAY set for statement-level precision. Bidirectional data links The extraction agent MUST also populate: CallableUnit.accesses_data_elements --- data elements the callable reads CallableUnit.modifies_data_elements --- data elements the callable writes Procedure For each CallableUnit, perform a lightweight data-flow analysis on its AST body. Identify variable reads (right-hand side of assignments, arguments to calls) and writes (left-hand side of assignments, output parameters). Create a DataFlow edge for each read/write/modify relationship. Populate accesses_data_elements and modifies_data_elements on the CallableUnit. Note: Full data-flow analysis (reaching definitions, def-use chains) is valuable but not required. At minimum, capture direct field reads and writes. Example # Reading a field read_order_total: a: DataFlow name: createOrder_reads_total flow_type: read source_element: order_total_field target_element: invoice_amount_field through_callable: create_order # Writing a field write_order_status: a: DataFlow name: createOrder_writes_status flow_type: write source_element: status_pending_constant target_element: order_status_field through_callable: create_order # Update the callable create_order: a: CallableUnit # ... (other attributes) accesses_data_elements: - order_total_field - customer_id_field modifies_data_elements: - order_status_field - order_created_at_field Sub-phase 2g: Annotations Extract decorators, attributes, annotations, and pragmas attached to code elements. Attributes Attribute Range Rule annotation_syntax string SHOULD set (the raw syntax, e.g., @Override, #[derive(Debug)]). parameters string[] SHOULD set for annotation parameters/arguments. Relationships Annotation uses two global (multi-domain) slots: Slot Target Rule annotates_element EncapsulationUnit / CallableUnit / DataStructure / DataElement MUST link to the annotated entity. affects_behavior_of EncapsulationUnit / CallableUnit MAY set when the annotation changes runtime behavior. The inverse slot on target entities is annotated_by. Procedure For each EncapsulationUnit, CallableUnit, DataStructure, or DataElement, check the AST for attached annotations/decorators. Create an Annotation for each, capturing the name and parameters. Link via annotates_element to the annotated entity. Mark behavior-affecting annotations (e.g., @Transactional, @Cached, @Async) via affects_behavior_of. Example # Java annotation override_annotation: a: Annotation name: Override annotation_syntax: "@Override" annotates_element: create_order # Python decorator with parameters route_annotation: a: Annotation name: route annotation_syntax: '@app.route("/orders", methods=["POST"])' parameters: - '"/orders"' - 'methods=["POST"]' annotates_element: create_order_handler affects_behavior_of: create_order_handler # Rust derive macro derive_debug: a: Annotation name: derive annotation_syntax: "#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]" parameters: - Debug - Clone - Serialize annotates_element: order_struct Sub-phase 2h: Platform-Specific Extensions This sub-phase is conditional. The extraction agent MUST determine which extensions apply based on the ProgrammingLanguage instances from Phase 1, then extract only the relevant ones. Decision tree What language/platform? │ ├── COBOL, PL/I, RPG, Assembler (Mainframe) │ ├── Extract FileDefinition, FileOperation │ ├── Extract ScreenDefinition, ScreenField │ ├── Extract JobDefinition, JobStep, DatasetAllocation │ └── Extract IPCConnection │ ├── C / C++ │ ├── Extract PreprocessorDirective │ ├── Extract MemoryModel │ └── Extract OwnershipAnnotation (smart pointers) │ ├── Rust │ ├── Extract MemoryModel │ └── Extract OwnershipAnnotation (ownership/lifetimes) │ ├── Any language with macro/metaprogramming │ └── Extract PreprocessorDirective │ └── All languages ├── Extract ErrorModel (per-module error handling strategy) └── Extract ExceptionType (exception hierarchies) Mainframe extensions FileDefinition and FileOperation Extract for every COBOL SELECT clause, PL/I DECLARE FILE, or equivalent file declaration. Attribute Description organization File organization: sequential, indexed, relative, vsam_ksds, vsam_esds, vsam_rrds, partitioned_dataset, generation_data_group, line_sequential, heap access_mode Access pattern: sequential_access, random_access, dynamic_access record_format Record format: fixed, variable, undefined, spanned, stream record_length Record length in bytes key_fields Key field names for indexed files file_status_field Variable receiving I/O status codes external_name DD name or physical file name Link file_defined_in_container to the CodeContainer and used_by_callables to the CallableUnits that perform I/O on the file. For each I/O verb (READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, OPEN, CLOSE), create a FileOperation linked to the FileDefinition via operates_on_file and to the CallableUnit via performed_in_callable. customer_file: a: FileDefinition name: CUSTOMER-MASTER organization: vsam_ksds access_mode: random_access record_format: fixed record_length: 200 key_fields: [CUSTOMER-ID] file_status_field: WS-FILE-STATUS external_name: CUSTMAST file_defined_in_container: customer_pgm_source read_customer_op: a: FileOperation name: READ-CUSTOMER operation_type: read operates_on_file: customer_file performed_in_callable: process_customer_paragraph ScreenDefinition and ScreenField Extract for CICS BMS map definitions, RPG display files, and similar character-mode UIs. Attribute Description screen_type Type of screen (e.g., bms_map, display_file) rows / columns Screen dimensions external_name External map or display file name For each field on the screen, create a ScreenField with row, column, length, is_input, is_protected, and maps_to_data_element linking to the corresponding DataElement. Link the ScreenDefinition to its EncapsulationUnit via program_uses_screens. inquiry_screen: a: ScreenDefinition name: CUSTINQ screen_type: bms_map rows: 24 columns: 80 external_name: CUSTMAP program_uses_screens: - customer_inquiry_program cust_name_field: a: ScreenField name: CUST-NAME row: 5 column: 20 length: 30 is_input: false is_protected: true field_on_screen: inquiry_screen maps_to_data_element: ws_customer_name JobDefinition, JobStep, DatasetAllocation Extract from JCL members, scheduler definitions, or cron configurations. JobDefinition: one per JOB card. Set job_class, priority, scheduling_info. JobStep: one per EXEC statement. Set step_type, program_name, link step_executes_program to the EncapsulationUnit. DatasetAllocation: one per DD statement. Set dd_name, dataset_name, disposition, record_format. Link maps_to_file_definition to the corresponding FileDefinition. payroll_job: a: JobDefinition name: PAYROLLJ job_class: A priority: 10 contains_job_steps: - payroll_step1 payroll_step1: a: JobStep name: CALC step_type: exec_pgm program_name: PAYROLL-CALC step_in_job: payroll_job step_executes_program: payroll_calc allocates_datasets: - emp_file_alloc emp_file_alloc: a: DatasetAllocation name: EMPFILE-DD dd_name: EMPFILE dataset_name: PROD.EMPLOYEE.MASTER disposition: shr allocated_in_step: payroll_step1 maps_to_file_definition: employee_master_file IPCConnection Extract for CICS LINK/XCTL, MQ calls, shared memory references, or any inter-program communication. Attribute Description mechanism IPC mechanism (e.g., cics_link, cics_xctl, mq_put, mq_get, shared_memory, pipe, rmi, corba) is_synchronous Whether the call is synchronous transaction_scoped Whether the IPC participates in a transaction boundary Link has_source_program and has_target_program to EncapsulationUnit instances. Link ipc_passes_data to the DataStructure being exchanged (typically a COMMAREA or message structure). link_to_validation: a: IPCConnection name: CUSTPGM-LINK-VALPGM mechanism: cics_link is_synchronous: true transaction_scoped: true ipc_source_program: customer_inquiry_program ipc_target_program: validation_program ipc_passes_data: - customer_commarea C/C++ and Rust extensions PreprocessorDirective Extract for #include, #define, #ifdef, #pragma, and similar constructs. Also applies to languages with compile-time metaprogramming (Rust macro_rules!, Lisp macros, etc.). Attribute Description directive_type Metaprogramming type (from MetaprogrammingType enum) condition Conditional compilation expression (e.g., #ifdef DEBUG) expansion Expanded text or transformation result Link directive_defined_in_container to the CodeContainer and directive_affects_encapsulation_units / directive_affects_callables to the affected entities. debug_guard: a: PreprocessorDirective name: DEBUG_IFDEF directive_type: conditional_compilation condition: "defined(DEBUG)" directive_defined_in_container: main_c_file directive_affects_callables: - debug_log_function MemoryModel and OwnershipAnnotation Extract one MemoryModel per language or module to describe the memory management strategy. Attribute Description primary_model Ownership model (e.g., manual, garbage_collected, reference_counted, ownership_borrowing) gc_type GC algorithm if applicable (e.g., generational, mark_sweep) supports_unsafe Whether unsafe/manual access is permitted For Rust and C++ smart pointers, create OwnershipAnnotation instances on individual DataElements: Attribute Description ownership Ownership model for this element lifetime Lifetime scope (e.g., static_lifetime, function_scope, block_scope, named) lifetime_name Named lifetime identifier (e.g., 'a in Rust) rust_memory: a: MemoryModel name: RustOwnership primary_model: ownership_borrowing supports_unsafe: true modules_using_memory_model: - order_service_module buffer_ownership: a: OwnershipAnnotation name: buffer_ref ownership: ownership_borrowing lifetime: named lifetime_name: "'a" annotates_data_element: buffer_data_element Error handling extensions (all languages) ErrorModel Create one ErrorModel per error handling paradigm observed in the codebase. Attribute Description strategy Error handling paradigm: exception_based, return_value_based, condition_based, error_code_based, panic_recover, monadic checkedness Exception checkedness: checked, unchecked, not_applicable Link modules_using_error_model to the EncapsulationUnit instances that use this paradigm. ExceptionType Create an ExceptionType for each declared exception or error type in the codebase. Attribute Description qualified_name Fully qualified exception name is_checked Whether this is a checked exception has_parent_exception Parent in the exception hierarchy Link raised_by_callables and handled_by_callables to the relevant CallableUnit instances. java_errors: a: ErrorModel name: JavaExceptions strategy: exception_based checkedness: checked modules_using_error_model: - order_service order_not_found: a: ExceptionType name: OrderNotFoundException qualified_name: com.example.orders.OrderNotFoundException is_checked: false parent_exception: runtime_exception raised_by_callables: - find_order_by_id handled_by_callables: - create_order Phase 2 Checklist Before proceeding to Phase 3, verify the following: Check How to verify Every CodeContainer has been parsed Count of parsed containers equals count from Phase 1. Every class/module/program has an EncapsulationUnit No top-level AST declarations lack a corresponding unit. Every method/function/paragraph has a CallableUnit No callable AST nodes lack a corresponding unit. Every field/variable has a DataElement Spot-check representative classes for completeness. Every parameter has a Parameter Compare parameter counts against source signatures. Import/include relationships are captured as DefinitionReferences Count of references matches import statement count per container. Call graph (ControlFlow) is built Every CallableUnit with call expressions has invokes_callables populated. Data flow edges are captured At minimum, direct field reads/writes are recorded. Annotations are extracted Spot-check decorated/annotated elements for Annotation instances. Platform-specific extensions are populated where applicable Mainframe: file definitions, screens, JCL. C/C++/Rust: memory model. All: error model. encapsulation_type is set on every EncapsulationUnit No unit has a null or missing type. callable_type is set on every CallableUnit No callable has a null or missing type. structure_type is set on every DataStructure No structure has a null or missing type. data_type is set on every DataElement No element has a null or missing type. Common pitfalls Missing nested types. Inner classes, companion objects, and anonymous classes are easily skipped. Ensure the AST walker recurses into nested type declarations. Unresolved call targets. Dynamic dispatch, reflection, and dependency injection make call graph construction incomplete. Create stub CallableUnit instances for unresolvable targets and annotate them. COBOL hierarchy. COBOL data items use level numbers (01, 05, 10, etc.) to express hierarchy. Map these to has_parent_element / has_child_elements rather than flattening. Generic types. Do not flatten List<Map<String, Order>> to a string. Use nested TypeExpression instances. Visibility defaults. Languages have different default visibilities (Java: package, Python: public, C++: private for class members). Apply the correct default when no modifier is present. Next phase Phase 3: Architecture (Layers 2/4) --- infers System, BoundedContext, Module, Component, Service, and Interface from the code structure graph built here.
