Step 7: Identify External Systems and Integrations

entries.text: Phase 3: Architecture and Integration (Layers 2 & 4) This phase bridges the physical code structure extracted in Phases 1-2 to logical architectural concepts. It maps directories to Modules, groups them into BoundedContexts, identifies Components and Services, extracts Interfaces and Endpoints, and documents ExternalSystem connections. Automation level: 60-70%. Module and service identification can be largely automated from build manifests and deployment configs. Bounded context identification requires judgment and is the most subjective step in the entire extraction process. Input: Phase 1 outputs (StorageLocation, CodeContainer, ProgrammingLanguage) + Phase 2 outputs (EncapsulationUnit, CallableUnit, DataStructure, DefinitionReference) + build manifests + deployment configs + documentation Output: System, BoundedContext, Module, Component, Service, Interface (and subtypes UserInterface, ProgrammaticInterface, EventInterface), Endpoint, Screen, Subscription, ExternalSystem, Integration, Contract, Adapter, CircuitBreaker, Dependency, Capability, Feature Overview Phase 3 establishes the architectural skeleton of the application. Where Phase 2 asks "what code exists?", Phase 3 asks "how is that code organized into deployable, meaningful units?" Two critical bridges are established in this phase: Code-to-Module bridge: Module.mapped_from_directory links to a StorageLocation, and StorageLocation.maps_to_module provides the inverse. This connects the physical file tree to the logical module structure. Code-to-Component bridge: Component.implemented_by_code links to EncapsulationUnit (or CodeContainer) instances, and the inverse EncapsulationUnit.implements_component links back. This connects individual code units to their architectural role. These bridges are what make SAO a true cross-layer ontology rather than a collection of disconnected models. Step 1: Create the System instance Every extraction produces exactly one System instance. This is the root container from which all other architectural entities are reachable. The extraction agent MUST create the System before proceeding to any other step in this phase. Set the following attributes: name -- the application or product name description -- a concise summary of what the system does version -- the version being extracted (inherited from the Versionable mixin) systems: - name: order-platform description: >- E-commerce order management platform handling order placement, payment processing, and fulfillment tracking. version: 2.4.1 All subsequent entities in this phase will be linked back to this System instance via relationship attributes such as contains_bounded_contexts, has_integrations, and exposes_interfaces. Step 2: Map StorageLocations to Modules Create one Module for each cohesive, deployable unit of code. The goal is to transform the flat directory tree from Phase 1 into a logical module structure. Heuristic: what constitutes a Module? A Module is a cohesive, deployable unit of code. Use these signals to identify module boundaries: A top-level package or directory with its own build manifest (pom.xml, package.json, build.gradle, Cargo.toml) A separate build target within a monorepo A directory that represents a distinct functional area and could be deployed independently In mainframe systems, a partition of programs grouped by function (e.g., all batch programs for a subsystem) Required attributes name -- the module name, typically matching the directory or package name mapped_from_directory -- MUST reference the corresponding StorageLocation from Phase 1 Establishing the bridge The extraction agent MUST set both sides of the code-to-module bridge: Module.mapped_from_directory pointing to the StorageLocation StorageLocation.maps_to_module pointing back to the Module Module dependencies Use the DefinitionReference instances from Phase 2 to infer inter-module dependencies. When code in Module A imports or references code in Module B, set depends_on_module on Module A to include Module B. Optional enrichment is_optional -- whether the module is an optional plugin or extension required_features -- feature flags needed to enable the module architectural_patterns -- applicable patterns (e.g., layered, hexagonal, cqrs) dependencies -- inline Dependency instances with dependency_type (runtime, build, optional, dev) modules: - name: order-service mapped_from_directory: storage-locations/src-orders depends_on_module: - payment-module - inventory-module architectural_patterns: - hexagonal dependencies: - name: spring-boot-starter-web dependency_type: runtime - name: junit-jupiter dependency_type: dev - name: payment-module mapped_from_directory: storage-locations/src-payments is_optional: false On the StorageLocation side, set the inverse: storage_locations: - name: src-orders location_path: src/main/java/com/example/orders maps_to_module: order-service Step 3: Group Modules into BoundedContexts Create BoundedContext instances representing the DDD semantic boundaries within the system. This is the most subjective step in the extraction process -- the extraction agent SHOULD flag bounded context assignments for human review. Decision tree for identifying bounded context boundaries Use these signals, ordered from strongest to weakest: Separate databases -- if two modules use different databases or schemas, they are almost certainly in separate contexts Separate deployment units -- independently deployed services map to separate contexts Separate teams -- if different teams own different modules, those modules likely belong to different contexts Clear domain-oriented package names -- directories like orders/, inventory/, users/, payments/ are strong candidates for separate contexts Distinct ubiquitous language -- if the same term (e.g., "account") means different things in different parts of the code, those parts belong to different contexts When boundaries are unclear (e.g., a monolith with no clear domain separation), start with a single BoundedContext and refine later as domain understanding deepens. Required attributes name -- the context name, typically a domain concept (e.g., "Order Management", "Inventory") contained_in_system -- MUST reference the System instance contains_modules -- MUST list the Module instances in this context Recommended attributes ubiquitous_language -- list of key domain terms used within this context context_map_relationship -- the DDD relationship pattern as a free-text string (e.g., "Customer-Supplier", "Partnership", "Shared Kernel", "Conformist", "Anti-Corruption Layer") upstream_from / downstream_from -- other BoundedContext instances this context depends on or is depended on by architectural_patterns -- applicable patterns (e.g., cqrs, event_sourcing, domain_model) System-level link The extraction agent MUST also set System.contains_bounded_contexts to reference all created BoundedContext instances. systems: - name: order-platform contains_bounded_contexts: - order-management-context - inventory-context - payment-context bounded_contexts: - name: order-management-context contained_in_system: order-platform contains_modules: - order-service ubiquitous_language: - order - line item - fulfillment - shipment context_map_relationship: "Upstream to Inventory (Customer-Supplier)" downstream_from: - payment-context architectural_patterns: - domain_model - cqrs - name: payment-context contained_in_system: order-platform contains_modules: - payment-module ubiquitous_language: - payment - refund - transaction - settlement upstream_from: - order-management-context Step 4: Identify Components within Modules Create Component instances representing the logical building blocks within each module. Components group related EncapsulationUnit instances by their architectural role. Heuristic: what constitutes a Component? Group EncapsulationUnits by stereotype or architectural role: Controller/Handler layer -- classes annotated with @Controller, @RestController, or similar Service layer -- classes annotated with @Service or named *Service Repository/DAO layer -- classes annotated with @Repository or implementing data access DTO/Model layer -- data transfer objects, request/response models Domain layer -- domain entities, value objects, aggregates Configuration layer -- configuration classes, factories, dependency injection setup Required attributes name -- the component name (e.g., "OrderController", "PaymentService", "OrderRepository") component_type -- a free-text string describing the component's role (e.g., "controller", "service", "repository", "adapter") contained_in_module -- MUST reference the parent Module Establishing the bridge The extraction agent MUST set both sides of the code-to-component bridge: Component.implemented_by_code -- list of EncapsulationUnit (or CodeContainer) instances that implement this component EncapsulationUnit.implements_component -- pointing back to the Component Module-level link Set Module.contains_components to reference all components within the module. modules: - name: order-service contains_components: - order-controller - order-service-component - order-repository - order-dto-layer components: - name: order-controller component_type: controller contained_in_module: order-service implemented_by_code: - OrderController # EncapsulationUnit - OrderExceptionHandler # EncapsulationUnit - name: order-service-component component_type: service contained_in_module: order-service implemented_by_code: - OrderService - OrderValidationService - OrderNotificationService - name: order-repository component_type: repository contained_in_module: order-service implemented_by_code: - OrderRepository - OrderItemRepository On the EncapsulationUnit side, set the inverse: encapsulation_units: - name: OrderController encapsulation_type: class implements_component: order-controller Step 5: Extract Services Create Service instances from deployment manifests. A Service represents an independently deployable runtime unit. Where to find services Scan for deployment artifacts: Dockerfiles and docker-compose.yml -- each service definition is a Service Kubernetes manifests -- each Deployment, StatefulSet, or CronJob is a Service Serverless configs (serverless.yml, SAM templates, functions/) -- each function is a Service JCL procedures -- each batch job or CICS transaction is a Service Procfiles, systemd units, Windows Services -- each process definition is a Service Required attributes name -- the service name, matching the deployment artifact name service_type -- one of: microservice, monolith, function, job, daemon, cics_transaction, ims_transaction, batch_program, stored_proc_service runs_module -- MUST reference the Module this service runs Recommended attributes depends_on_service -- other Service instances this service depends on exposes_endpoints -- Endpoint instances exposed by this service (see Step 6) Module-level inverse Set Module.runs_as_services on the corresponding module. services: - name: order-api service_type: microservice runs_module: order-service depends_on_service: - payment-api - inventory-api - name: order-processor service_type: job runs_module: order-service description: Nightly batch job for order reconciliation - name: payment-api service_type: microservice runs_module: payment-module On the Module side: modules: - name: order-service runs_as_services: - order-api - order-processor Step 6: Extract Interfaces and Endpoints Interface is an abstract class with three concrete subtypes. The extraction agent MUST determine which subtype to use based on the nature of the interface. UserInterface Use for any human-facing interface. Set category to user_interface. Required attributes: name -- the interface name category -- user_interface ui_type -- one of: web_ui, mobile_ui, desktop_ui, cli UserInterface MAY contain Screen instances with route and offers_operations attributes. user_interfaces: - name: order-management-ui category: user_interface ui_type: web_ui exposed_by_system: order-platform screens: - name: order-list-screen route: /orders - name: order-detail-screen route: /orders/:id - name: create-order-screen route: /orders/new ProgrammaticInterface Use for machine-to-machine interfaces. Set category to programmatic_interface. Required attributes: name -- the interface name category -- programmatic_interface api_type -- one of: rest_api, graphql_api, grpc_api, sdk, soap_api ProgrammaticInterface MAY contain Endpoint instances. Each Endpoint SHOULD specify path, method, and protocol. programmatic_interfaces: - name: order-rest-api category: programmatic_interface api_type: rest_api base_url: https://api.example.com/v2 exposed_by_system: order-platform has_endpoints: - name: list-orders path: /orders method: GET protocol: https - name: create-order path: /orders method: POST protocol: https - name: get-order path: /orders/{id} method: GET protocol: https - name: cancel-order path: /orders/{id}/cancel method: POST protocol: https Endpoint instances MAY also be linked to a Service via exposed_by_service / Service.exposes_endpoints. EventInterface Use for event-driven interfaces. Set category to event_interface. Required attributes: name -- the interface name category -- event_interface event_type -- one of: webhook, message_queue, event_stream, pub_sub EventInterface MAY specify topics and contain Subscription instances. event_interfaces: - name: order-events category: event_interface event_type: pub_sub topics: - order.created - order.fulfilled - order.cancelled exposed_by_system: order-platform has_subscriptions: - name: inventory-order-subscription filter: "order.created" delivery_mode: at_least_once Linking interfaces Interfaces MAY be linked at the System level via System.exposes_interfaces, or they MAY be linked to specific services via the Endpoint relationship. The extraction agent SHOULD use System.exposes_interfaces for the primary linkage and add service-level endpoint links for additional precision. Step 7: Identify External Systems and Integrations Create an ExternalSystem for each system outside the extraction boundary that this system interacts with. Identifying external systems Scan these sources: Configuration files -- database connection strings, API base URLs, message broker addresses Environment variables -- DATABASE_URL, REDIS_HOST, STRIPE_API_KEY Infrastructure-as-Code -- Terraform resources, CloudFormation stacks Import statements -- SDK imports for third-party services (e.g., import stripe, import boto3) Docker Compose -- linked services (PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ) Required ExternalSystem attributes name -- the external system name system_type -- one of: third_party_service, partner_system, legacy_system, saas_application Optional ExternalSystem attributes owner -- the team or vendor that owns the external system sla -- service level agreement documentation_url -- link to API docs Creating Integrations For each connection between the system and an external system, create an Integration instance. Required Integration attributes: name -- a descriptive name for the integration integration_type -- one of: inbound, outbound, bidirectional integrates_with_system -- reference to the ExternalSystem belongs_to_system -- reference to the System Recommended Integration attributes: protocol -- one of: http, https, websocket, grpc, amqp, mqtt, kafka, sftp, tcp, udp, corba, dcom, rmi, named_pipe, shared_memory integration_governed_by_contract -- a Contract if one exists uses_adapter -- an Adapter if protocol translation is needed protected_by_breaker -- a CircuitBreaker if resilience patterns are in place Optional supporting entities Contract -- create when a formal API specification exists: contract_type -- one of: openapi, asyncapi, json_schema, protobuf, avro, graphql_schema, wsdl definition -- the contract definition or path to the spec file Adapter (extends Component) -- create when protocol translation occurs: source_protocol and target_protocol -- the protocols being translated between transformation -- description of the data transformation CircuitBreaker -- create when resilience patterns are detected (e.g., Hystrix, Resilience4j, Polly): failure_threshold -- number of failures before opening reset_timeout_seconds -- time before attempting half-open half_open_requests -- requests allowed in half-open state System-level link Set System.has_integrations to reference all Integration instances. external_systems: - name: stripe-payments system_type: third_party_service owner: Stripe Inc. documentation_url: https://stripe.com/docs/api - name: order-database system_type: legacy_system owner: Platform Team - name: notification-broker system_type: third_party_service owner: Platform Team integrations: - name: stripe-payment-integration integration_type: outbound protocol: https integrates_with_system: stripe-payments belongs_to_system: order-platform integration_governed_by_contract: stripe-api-contract uses_adapter: stripe-adapter protected_by_breaker: stripe-circuit-breaker - name: order-db-integration integration_type: bidirectional protocol: tcp integrates_with_system: order-database belongs_to_system: order-platform contracts: - name: stripe-api-contract contract_type: openapi definition: "specs/stripe-api-v3.yaml" adapters: - name: stripe-adapter component_type: adapter source_protocol: https target_protocol: https transformation: "Maps internal PaymentRequest to Stripe charge API format" circuit_breakers: - name: stripe-circuit-breaker failure_threshold: 5 reset_timeout_seconds: 30 half_open_requests: 3 Capabilities and Features If the extraction scope warrants it, the extraction agent MAY create Capability and Feature instances at this stage. Capability represents a discrete business or technical ability the system provides. Link via provided_by_modules to the Module instances that deliver it, and via enables_features to the Feature instances it supports. Feature represents a user-facing manifestation of one or more capabilities. Set category to one of: core, optional, experimental, deprecated. These entities are often better populated in Phase 5 (Business Intent) when domain understanding is richer. Creating placeholders here and refining later is acceptable. capabilities: - name: order-placement provided_by_modules: - order-service enables_features: - place-order-feature features: - name: place-order-feature category: core enabled_by_capabilities: - order-placement Phase 3 Checklist Before proceeding to Phase 4, verify the following: [ ] A single System instance exists with name, description, and version [ ] Every top-level package or directory identified in Phase 1 maps to a Module via mapped_from_directory / maps_to_module [ ] Every Module is assigned to a BoundedContext via contained_in_context / contains_modules [ ] Components are identified within each module and linked to EncapsulationUnit instances via implemented_by_code / implements_component [ ] Services are identified from deployment manifests and linked to modules via runs_module / runs_as_services [ ] Interfaces are extracted and categorized by subtype (UserInterface, ProgrammaticInterface, EventInterface) [ ] Endpoints are documented for programmatic interfaces with path, method, and protocol [ ] ExternalSystem instances exist for every external dependency [ ] Integration instances connect the system to each external system with integration_type and protocol [ ] Module dependencies (depends_on_module) are captured from Phase 2 import analysis [ ] All inverse relationships are set (both sides of every bridge) [ ] Bounded context assignments are flagged for human review
entries.title: Phase 3: Architecture and Integration (Layers 2 & 4)

entries.description: Input: Phase 2 outputs (DataStructure, DataElement) + Phase 3 outputs (BoundedContext, Module) Output: Aggregate, DomainEntity, ValueObject, Attribute, DomainRelationship, Lifecycle, State, Transition, DataStore, Collection, Schema,…

headings.title: 3. Step 2: Create DomainEntities and map Attributes
7. Step 6: Extract Lifecycles and State Machines

entries.text: Phase 4: Domain Model (Layer 5) Input: Phase 2 outputs (DataStructure, DataElement) + Phase 3 outputs (BoundedContext, Module) Output: Aggregate, DomainEntity, ValueObject, Attribute, DomainRelationship, Lifecycle, State, Transition, DataStore, Collection, Schema, SchemaVersion, DataClassification, RetentionPolicy, DatabaseConstraint, DatabaseIndex 1. Overview Phase 4 is where extraction moves from deterministic parsing to inferential reasoning. Prior phases catalogued files (Phase 1), parsed code structures (Phase 2), and identified architectural boundaries (Phase 3). This phase recognizes business meaning in those code structures using Domain-Driven Design patterns. The key insight: a COBOL group item named CUST-MSTR-REC with a primary key field and CRUD operations is not just a DataStructure -- it is a Customer domain entity. A Java class with @Entity, a primary key, and repository methods is an Order aggregate root. This phase surfaces those facts. Automation level: 40--50%. Deterministic heuristics (presence of @Entity, primary key fields, ORM annotations) handle part of the classification, but an LLM or human analyst MUST confirm business names, aggregate boundaries, and lifecycle semantics. Critical bridge Phase 4 establishes the central bridge between code and domain: DomainEntity.mapped_from_structure links to the DataStructure(s) from Phase 2 DataStructure.maps_to_domain_entity is the inverse Attribute.mapped_from_element links to the DataElement(s) from Phase 2 DataElement.maps_to_attribute is the inverse These bidirectional links MUST be established for every DomainEntity and Attribute created in this phase. 2. Step 1: Classify DataStructures Iterate over every DataStructure produced in Phase 2 and apply the following decision tree. Decision tree For each DataStructure: │ ├─ Has unique identifier + CRUD operations + persisted? │ └─ → Create a DomainEntity │ ├─ No unique identifier + immutable + used as property of another structure? │ └─ → Create a ValueObject │ ├─ DTO, transport object, configuration, utility type? │ └─ → Leave as DataStructure only (no domain mapping) │ └─ Ambiguous → Flag for human review Signals by language Signal Language Implies @Entity, @Table Java/JPA DomainEntity @Embeddable Java/JPA ValueObject class Meta: db_table Python/Django DomainEntity 01 ... RECORD with PK and FD COBOL DomainEntity 01 ... GROUP (no PK, used inline) COBOL ValueObject CREATE TABLE with PRIMARY KEY SQL DDL DomainEntity frozen<> UDT Cassandra CQL ValueObject 3. Step 2: Create DomainEntities and map Attributes For each DataStructure classified as a domain entity, create a DomainEntity instance. Required attributes Attribute Type Notes name string Clean business name -- e.g., "Customer", not "CUST-MSTR-REC" mapped_from_structure DataStructure (multivalued) MUST link to the originating structure(s) attributes Attribute list (inlined) One per meaningful field classifications DataClassificationType list If the entity holds sensitive data Creating Attributes For each meaningful field (skip framework noise like serialization IDs), create an Attribute: Attribute Type Notes name string Clean business name for the field category AttributeCategory One of: required, optional, computed, derived, transient data_type string (required) Data type: string, integer, boolean, date, timestamp, decimal, etc. is_identifier boolean true for primary key / unique identifier fields is_indexed boolean true if the field is indexed default_value string Default value if discoverable classification DataClassificationType One of: public, internal, confidential, restricted, pii, phi, pci mapped_from_element DataElement (multivalued) MUST link to the originating element(s) Establishing bridges The extraction agent MUST set both sides of every bridge: DomainEntity.mapped_from_structure → the DataStructure DataStructure.maps_to_domain_entity → the DomainEntity Attribute.mapped_from_element → the DataElement DataElement.maps_to_attribute → the Attribute YAML example DomainEntity: - name: Customer mapped_from_structure: CUST-MSTR-REC classifications: - pii attributes: - name: customer_id data_type: string category: required is_identifier: true mapped_from_element: CUST-ID - name: name data_type: string category: required classification: pii mapped_from_element: CUST-NAME - name: email data_type: string category: required classification: pii mapped_from_element: CUST-EMAIL - name: loyalty_points data_type: integer category: computed mapped_from_element: CUST-LOYALTY-PTS - name: created_at data_type: timestamp category: required mapped_from_element: CUST-CREATE-DT 4. Step 3: Create ValueObjects For each DataStructure classified as a value object, create a ValueObject instance. Required attributes Attribute Type Notes name string Clean business name (e.g., "Money", "Address") attributes Attribute list (inlined) Component fields mapped_from_structure_vo DataStructure (multivalued) MUST link to the originating structure(s) The inverse DataStructure.maps_to_value_object MUST also be set. Common value object patterns Money: amount + currency Address: street, city, state, postal_code, country DateRange: start_date, end_date Coordinates: latitude, longitude PhoneNumber: country_code, area_code, number YAML example ValueObject: - name: Money mapped_from_structure_vo: AMOUNT-FIELDS attributes: - name: amount data_type: decimal category: required mapped_from_element: AMT-VALUE - name: currency data_type: string category: required default_value: "USD" mapped_from_element: AMT-CURRENCY - name: Address mapped_from_structure_vo: CUST-ADDR-GRP attributes: - name: street data_type: string category: required classification: pii mapped_from_element: CUST-ADDR-STREET - name: city data_type: string category: required mapped_from_element: CUST-ADDR-CITY # ... state, postal_code, country follow the same pattern 5. Step 4: Group into Aggregates Create Aggregate instances that define transactional consistency boundaries around related entities and value objects. Heuristics for identifying aggregate boundaries The extraction agent SHOULD use the following signals: Co-loaded entities -- entities that are always fetched and saved together (e.g., Order and OrderLineItem loaded in the same repository method) Shared transaction boundary -- entities modified within the same @Transactional method, the same CICS SYNCPOINT, or the same database transaction Root-controls-access -- a root entity that mediates all access to its children (e.g., Order.addLineItem() rather than direct OrderLineItem creation) Cascade delete -- if deleting entity A always deletes entity B, they belong in the same aggregate Bounded context alignment -- aggregates SHOULD NOT cross BoundedContext boundaries Required attributes Attribute Type Notes name string Aggregate name (typically same as root entity) has_root_entity DomainEntity (required) The root entity -- MUST be set aggregates_entities DomainEntity list Non-root entities in the aggregate has_value_objects ValueObject list (inlined) Value objects within the aggregate enforced_by_invariant_rules Rule list Invariant rules (if known at this point) persisted_in_stores DataStore list Where the aggregate is persisted contained_in_bounded_context BoundedContext Parent bounded context from Phase 3 Linking to BoundedContext Set Aggregate.contained_in_bounded_context to the BoundedContext identified in Phase 3. The inverse BoundedContext.contains_aggregates MUST also be set. YAML example Aggregate: - name: Order has_root_entity: Order aggregates_entities: - OrderLineItem value_objects: - Money # defined in Step 3 enforced_by_invariant_rules: - OrderMustHaveAtLeastOneItem - TotalMustEqualSumOfLineItems persisted_in_stores: - OrderDatabase contained_in_bounded_context: OrderManagement 6. Step 5: Extract DomainRelationships Create a DomainRelationship for each association between domain entities. Required attributes Attribute Type Notes name string Descriptive name (e.g., "OrderHasLineItems") has_source_entity DomainEntity The entity that owns or originates the relationship has_target_entity DomainEntity The entity that is referenced cardinality Cardinality (required) One of: one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one, many_to_many is_navigable boolean Whether the relationship can be traversed source → target is_bidirectional boolean Whether it can be navigated in both directions is_composition boolean true if the target's lifecycle depends on the source foreign_key_field string The field implementing this relationship in the data layer join_entity string For many_to_many, the join table or entity name Sources for discovering relationships Source Language / Platform Example ORM annotations Java (@ManyToOne, @OneToMany) @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order") ORM declarations Python/Django (ForeignKey, ManyToManyField) ForeignKey(Customer, on_delete=CASCADE) FK constraints SQL DDL FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id) Record references COBOL CUST-ID field in ORDER-REC referencing CUST-MSTR-REC ActiveRecord Ruby on Rails (belongs_to, has_many) has_many :order_line_items Composition vs. association Set is_composition to true when: The child entity cannot exist without the parent (e.g., OrderLineItem cannot exist without Order) Cascade delete is configured (on_delete=CASCADE, CascadeType.ALL) The child has no independent access path (no standalone repository) YAML example DomainRelationship: - name: OrderHasLineItems source_entity: Order target_entity: OrderLineItem cardinality: one_to_many is_composition: true is_navigable: true is_bidirectional: true foreign_key_field: order_id - name: OrderBelongsToCustomer source_entity: Order target_entity: Customer cardinality: many_to_one is_composition: false is_navigable: true is_bidirectional: true foreign_key_field: customer_id - name: StudentEnrolledInCourses source_entity: Student target_entity: Course cardinality: many_to_many is_composition: false is_navigable: true is_bidirectional: true join_entity: Enrollment 7. Step 6: Extract Lifecycles and State Machines Look for evidence of state management in the codebase and create lifecycle definitions. Signals for state machines Status/state fields with constrained values (enums, finite string sets) State transition methods (e.g., order.submit(), order.cancel()) Workflow definitions (state machine DSLs, workflow engines) Guard conditions (e.g., if order.status == 'CONFIRMED' then allow ship) COBOL paragraph names following transition patterns (e.g., 1000-PROCESS-NEW-ORDER, 2000-CONFIRM-ORDER) Creating instances Create a Lifecycle with name, states (inlined State list), transitions (inlined Transition list), starts_with_state (initial State), and governs_entities (the DomainEntity instances that follow this lifecycle). For each State, set name, is_initial, is_terminal, and optionally allows_actions_in_state. For each Transition, set name, transitions_from_state (required), transitions_to_state (required), and optionally triggered_by_events, guarded_by_rules, and executes_actions_on_transition. Link DomainEntity.governed_by_lifecycle → Lifecycle for each entity that has state behavior. YAML example Lifecycle: - name: OrderLifecycle governs_entities: - Order starts_with_state: Draft states: - name: Draft is_initial: true is_terminal: false allows_actions_in_state: - AddLineItem - RemoveLineItem - name: Submitted is_initial: false is_terminal: false - name: Confirmed is_initial: false is_terminal: false - name: Shipped is_initial: false is_terminal: false - name: Delivered is_initial: false is_terminal: true - name: Cancelled is_initial: false is_terminal: true transitions: - name: SubmitOrder transitions_from_state: Draft transitions_to_state: Submitted triggered_by_events: - OrderSubmitted guarded_by_rules: - OrderMustHaveAtLeastOneItem - name: ConfirmOrder transitions_from_state: Submitted transitions_to_state: Confirmed guarded_by_rules: - PaymentMustBeAuthorized - name: ShipOrder transitions_from_state: Confirmed transitions_to_state: Shipped executes_actions_on_transition: - CreateShipment - NotifyCustomer - name: DeliverOrder transitions_from_state: Shipped transitions_to_state: Delivered - name: CancelOrder transitions_from_state: Submitted # also valid from Confirmed transitions_to_state: Cancelled executes_actions_on_transition: - RefundPayment 8. Step 7: Identify DataStores and Collections Create persistence infrastructure instances that capture where aggregates are stored. Creating DataStore instances Attribute Type Notes name string E.g., "OrderDatabase", "CustomerVSAM" store_type DataStoreType See permissible values below connection_string string Connection URI if discoverable collections Collection list (inlined) Tables, collections, or buckets store_type permissible values relational_db, document_db, key_value_store, graph_db, time_series_db, object_storage, search_index, cache, message_broker, data_lake, vsam, flat_file, isam, dead_letter_queue Creating Collection instances Attribute Type Notes name string Table/collection/bucket name collection_structured_by_schema Schema Schema that defines the structure persists_structures DataStructure list Link to Phase 2 DataStructures stored here has_constraints DatabaseConstraint list (inlined) PK, FK, unique, check constraints has_indexes DatabaseIndex list (inlined) Index definitions governed_by_retention_policy RetentionPolicy Data retention rules Creating Schema and SchemaVersion If DDL files or migration scripts exist, create a Schema with schema_type (one of: table_schema, document_schema, event_schema, api_schema, message_schema) and definition (the DDL or schema content). Add SchemaVersion instances to has_versions for each migration, setting version, migration_script, and is_backward_compatible. Creating DatabaseConstraint and DatabaseIndex instances For each Collection, create DatabaseConstraint instances with constraint_type (required, one of: primary_key, foreign_key, unique, check, not_null), columns, and -- for foreign keys -- reference_table and reference_columns. For check constraints, set expression. Create DatabaseIndex instances with index_type (required, one of: btree, hash, gin, fulltext), columns, and optionally is_unique, is_partial, and filter_expression. DataClassification and RetentionPolicy If data sensitivity or retention requirements are discoverable (from comments, annotations, compliance documentation): Create DataClassification with classification_type (one of: public, internal, confidential, restricted, pii, phi, pci), handling_requirements, and encryption_required. Create RetentionPolicy with retention_days, archive_after_days, and deletion_strategy. Linking aggregates to stores Set Aggregate.persisted_in_stores → DataStore and the inverse DataStore.persists_aggregates. Set DataStore.collections → Collection list (inlined). Set Collection.persists_structures → DataStructure and the inverse DataStructure.persisted_in_collection. YAML example DataStore: - name: OrderDatabase store_type: relational_db persists_aggregates: - Order collections: - name: orders collection_structured_by_schema: OrderTableSchema persists_structures: - ORDER-REC has_constraints: - name: pk_orders constraint_type: primary_key columns: [order_id] - name: fk_orders_customer constraint_type: foreign_key columns: [customer_id] reference_table: customers reference_columns: [customer_id] - name: chk_order_total constraint_type: check expression: "total_amount >= 0" has_indexes: - name: idx_orders_customer index_type: btree columns: [customer_id] - name: idx_orders_status index_type: btree columns: [status] governed_by_retention_policy: OrderRetention - name: order_line_items persists_structures: [ORDER-LINE-REC] has_constraints: - name: pk_order_lines constraint_type: primary_key columns: [line_item_id] Schema: - name: OrderTableSchema schema_type: table_schema definition: "CREATE TABLE orders (order_id UUID PRIMARY KEY, ...);" schema_versions: - name: OrderTable_v1 version: "1.0.0" is_backward_compatible: true - name: OrderTable_v2 version: "2.0.0" migration_script: "ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN discount_code VARCHAR(20);" is_backward_compatible: true DataClassification: - name: CustomerPII classification_type: pii handling_requirements: ["Must be encrypted at rest", "Access requires audit logging"] encryption_required: true RetentionPolicy: - name: OrderRetention retention_days: 2555 archive_after_days: 365 deletion_strategy: "anonymize" 9. Phase 4 Checklist Before proceeding to Phase 5, verify the following: [ ] Every persistent DataStructure from Phase 2 has been evaluated against the decision tree (Section 2) [ ] DomainEntity instances have clean business names and mapped_from_structure bridges [ ] Attribute instances have mapped_from_element bridges back to DataElement [ ] ValueObject instances have mapped_from_structure_vo bridges [ ] Aggregate instances have has_root_entity set (required) and are assigned to a BoundedContext via contained_in_bounded_context [ ] DomainRelationship instances capture entity associations with correct cardinality, is_composition, and foreign_key_field [ ] Lifecycle, State, and Transition instances are created where state patterns exist in the code [ ] DataStore and Collection instances identify all persistence mechanisms [ ] DatabaseConstraint and DatabaseIndex instances capture schema-level metadata where DDL or migrations are available [ ] DataClassification and RetentionPolicy instances are created where data sensitivity or retention requirements are discoverable [ ] All bidirectional inverse links are set on both sides of every relationship
