headings.title: 4. Step 3: Classify Actions as Queries or Commands

entries.text: Phase 5: Business Intent Input: All prior phase outputs (Phases 1--4) + documentation + domain knowledge Output: HumanActor, SystemActor, Operation, Query, Command, Rule, DomainEvent, IntegrationEvent, Subscription, Workflow, Step, Transaction, Capability, Feature, Message 1. Overview Phase 5 is the highest-abstraction layer in the SAO extraction process. Where earlier phases answer "what is the code?" and "how is it structured?", this phase answers "what does the system do, and for whom?" This is the most inferential phase in the playbook. Most entities here cannot be parsed mechanically from source code -- they MUST be inferred from documentation, naming conventions, interaction patterns, and domain knowledge. Estimated automation: 20--30%. The remaining 70--80% requires LLM inference combined with human validation. Key characteristics of Phase 5 extraction: Documentation is a critical input. User stories, API docs, product specs, and README files are often the primary source for actors, capabilities, and features. Every entity produced in this phase SHOULD be flagged for human review. Even when an LLM can plausibly infer a business intent, a domain expert MUST validate the result before it is considered authoritative. Prior phase outputs are prerequisites. Phase 5 builds on the CallableUnit, Component, Module, DomainEntity, Aggregate, and Schema instances produced in Phases 2--4. Without them, the bridge from code to intent cannot be established. 2. Step 1: Identify Actors Actor is an abstract class representing any entity that can initiate actions. The extraction agent MUST NOT instantiate Actor directly; instead, use its concrete subtypes HumanActor and SystemActor. HumanActor Set actor_type to one of: end_user -- regular end user of the system administrator -- system administrator with elevated privileges operator -- operations personnel managing system runtime developer -- software developer or engineer auditor -- compliance or security auditor Set name, description, and email where known. Sources: authentication/authorization code (role definitions, user role enums), user-facing documentation, API consumer descriptions. - HumanActor: name: CustomerUser description: End user who browses products and places orders category: human actor_type: end_user has_identities: - CustomerIdentity SystemActor Set actor_type to one of: internal_service -- internal service within the system external_system -- external third-party system scheduled_process -- scheduled or cron-based process ai_agent -- artificial intelligence agent or bot message_trigger -- message or event-triggered automation Set name, description, and service_account where known. Sources: scheduled jobs (cron, Quartz, CICS START), message consumers (Kafka listeners, RabbitMQ handlers), external API clients, service-to-service authentication configs. - SystemActor: name: PaymentGateway description: External payment processing system (Stripe) category: system actor_type: external_system service_account: stripe-webhook-svc - SystemActor: name: NightlyReportGenerator description: Scheduled process that generates daily sales reports category: system actor_type: scheduled_process service_account: report-gen-cron Linking Actors to Identities The extraction agent SHOULD link Actor.has_identities to Identity instances. Identity extraction is detailed in Phase 6 (Cross-Cutting Concerns); in Phase 5, the agent SHOULD create placeholder references that Phase 6 will resolve. 3. Step 2: Extract Operations Create an Operation for each named, invocable business action exposed via an interface. An Operation bridges the gap between a user-visible action and the code that implements it. Required attributes Attribute Description name Operation name (e.g., PlaceOrder, AuthenticateUser) description What the operation does in business terms accepts_input_schema Reference to the input Schema produces_output_schema Reference to the output Schema Key relationships Operation.implemented_by_callables -- MUST link to one or more CallableUnit instances from Phase 2. This is the essential bridge from business intent to code. Operation.exposed_by_component -- SHOULD link to the Component that exposes this operation. Operation.executes_operation_actions -- links to the Action instances (Queries and Commands) the operation performs. Operation.offered_on_screens -- links to Screen instances where the operation appears in a UI. Sources: API endpoint handlers (REST controllers, gRPC service methods), service facade methods, CICS transaction handlers, GraphQL resolvers. - Operation: name: PlaceOrder description: Accepts a cart and creates a confirmed order errors: - InsufficientInventoryError - PaymentDeclinedError exposed_by_component: OrderService accepts_input_schema: PlaceOrderRequest produces_output_schema: OrderConfirmation implemented_by_callables: - OrderController.placeOrder - OrderService.processOrder executes_operation_actions: - CreateOrderCommand 4. Step 3: Classify Actions as Queries or Commands Action is an abstract class with two concrete subtypes: Query (read-only) and Command (state-changing). The extraction agent MUST classify every business action into one of these subtypes. Common attributes (inherited from Action) Attribute Description category query, command, or mutation performed_by_actor The Actor who performs this action targets_resources Resource instances affected validated_by_action_rules Rule instances that validate this action emits_events_from_action Event instances emitted by this action executes_in_transaction Transaction context for this action Query A read-only action that retrieves data without side effects. Attribute Description filters Query filter expressions projections Fields to return - Query: name: SearchProducts description: Search product catalog by keyword and category category: query performed_by_actor: CustomerUser filters: - "keyword LIKE '%term%'" - "category = :category" projections: - id - name - price - thumbnail_url targets_resources: - ProductCatalog Command An action that changes system state. Attribute Description command_type create, update, delete, execute, archive, restore idempotency_key Key for idempotent execution - Command: name: CreateOrder description: Creates a new order from the customer's cart category: command command_type: create performed_by_actor: CustomerUser idempotency_key: cart_id targets_resources: - OrderAggregate validated_by_action_rules: - InventoryAvailabilityRule - MinimumOrderAmountRule emits_events_from_action: - OrderCreated Classification heuristic Signal Classification HTTP GET, GraphQL query, SQL SELECT Query HTTP POST/PUT/DELETE, SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE Command Method name starts with get, find, list, search, fetch Query Method name starts with create, update, delete, process, submit Command Returns data without persistence writes Query Triggers events, writes to a data store, or changes entity state Command CICS RECEIVE MAP followed by SEND MAP only Query CICS WRITE / REWRITE / DELETE on VSAM/DB2 Command When a method both reads and writes (e.g., transferFunds), classify it as a Command with category set to mutation. 5. Step 4: Extract Rules Create a Rule for each validation constraint, business policy, guard clause, or derivation logic. Required attributes Attribute Description name Descriptive rule name category validation, business, derivation, constraint, trigger condition The rule predicate (the "if" part) action What happens when the rule fires (the "then" part) priority Evaluation order (lower = higher priority) is_active Whether the rule is currently active Key relationships Rule.validates_actions -- which Action instances this rule validates Rule.validates_attributes -- which Attribute instances this rule constrains Rule.governs_domain_entities -- which DomainEntity instances this rule governs Rule.guards_transitions -- which Transition instances this rule guards (for state machines) Rule.enforces_aggregate_invariants -- which Aggregate instances this rule protects Rule categories explained Category Purpose Typical source validation Data integrity checks @NotNull, @Size, @Pattern, input validators business Business logic constraints Policy checks, eligibility rules, discount logic derivation Computed/derived values total = sum(lineItems), tax = subtotal * rate constraint Domain invariants Balance >= 0, stock >= 0, unique email trigger Event-driven automation "When order ships, send email", "When inventory low, alert" Sources: validation annotations (@NotNull, @Size, @Valid), if/throw patterns, guard clauses, policy service methods, COBOL paragraph-level condition checks (IF/EVALUATE), database constraints. - Rule: name: MinimumOrderAmountRule category: business condition: "order.total >= 10.00" action: "Allow order to proceed" priority: 1 is_active: true validates_actions: - CreateOrder governs_domain_entities: - Order - Rule: name: EmailFormatValidation category: validation condition: "email matches RFC 5322 pattern" action: "Reject with INVALID_EMAIL error" priority: 1 is_active: true validates_attributes: - User.email 6. Step 5: Extract Events Event is the base class for notifications that something occurred. The extraction agent MUST use its concrete subtypes: DomainEvent and IntegrationEvent. Common attributes (inherited from Event) Attribute Description name Event name, past tense by convention (e.g., OrderPlaced) category domain_event, integration_event, system_event, audit_event correlation_id For tracing related events event_structured_by_schema Schema defining the event payload emitted_by_component Component that produces the event DomainEvent A significant occurrence within a bounded context, produced by an Aggregate. Set produced_by_aggregate to reference the originating Aggregate. Set category to domain_event. - DomainEvent: name: OrderPlaced description: Emitted when a customer successfully places an order category: domain_event produced_by_aggregate: OrderAggregate event_structured_by_schema: OrderPlacedPayload emitted_by_component: OrderService IntegrationEvent A cross-service communication event that bridges bounded contexts or external systems. Set targeted_at_services to reference the Service instances that consume the event. Set category to integration_event. - IntegrationEvent: name: OrderShippedNotification description: Published to notify billing and notification services category: integration_event targeted_at_services: - BillingService - NotificationService event_structured_by_schema: OrderShippedPayload Subscription Create a Subscription for each event consumer registration. Attribute Description name Subscription name filter Filter expression for event selection delivery_mode Push or pull delivery subscribes_to_event_types Event instances subscribed to subscribed_by_actor Actor that owns the subscription subscribes_to_interface EventInterface for delivery - Subscription: name: BillingOrderShippedSubscription filter: "event.type = 'OrderShippedNotification'" delivery_mode: push subscribes_to_event_types: - OrderShippedNotification subscribed_by_actor: BillingService Message Create a Message when the integration involves explicit message payloads (e.g., message queues, topic-based messaging). - Message: name: OrderShippedMessage message_type: event message_structured_by_schema: OrderShippedPayload Sources: event publishing code (EventBus.publish(), Kafka ProducerRecord, RabbitMQ basicPublish), event handler annotations (@EventHandler, @KafkaListener), CICS START commands, domain event classes, message broker configurations. 7. Step 6: Extract Workflows Create a Workflow for each multi-step business process that coordinates multiple actions toward a business goal. Workflow attributes Attribute Description name Workflow name workflow_type synchronous, asynchronous, saga, choreography, orchestration steps Ordered list of Step instances triggered_by_workflow_events Event instances that start the workflow Step attributes Attribute Description name Step name order Execution order (integer) condition Condition for execution timeout_seconds Step timeout in seconds executes_actions_in_step Action instances executed during this step followed_by_steps Next Step instances in the sequence compensated_by_step Compensating Step for saga rollback Transaction Create a Transaction for each transaction boundary encountered. Attribute Description name Transaction name transaction_type local, distributed, saga, two_phase_commit isolation_level Transaction isolation level (e.g., read_committed) timeout_seconds Transaction timeout in seconds executes_actions Action instances within this transaction Sources: saga implementations, orchestration engines (Temporal, Camunda, Step Functions), multi-step handler methods, COBOL paragraph sequences with EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT, Spring @Transactional boundaries, database transaction blocks. - Workflow: name: OrderFulfillmentSaga workflow_type: saga triggered_by_workflow_events: - OrderPlaced steps: - Step: name: ReserveInventory order: 1 timeout_seconds: 5 executes_actions_in_step: - ReserveInventoryCommand compensated_by_step: ReleaseInventory followed_by_steps: - AuthorizePayment - Step: name: AuthorizePayment order: 2 timeout_seconds: 10 executes_actions_in_step: - AuthorizePaymentCommand compensated_by_step: CancelAuthorization followed_by_steps: - CreateShipment - Step: name: CreateShipment order: 3 timeout_seconds: 5 executes_actions_in_step: - CreateShipmentCommand compensated_by_step: CancelShipment followed_by_steps: - ConfirmOrder - Step: name: ConfirmOrder order: 4 executes_actions_in_step: - ConfirmOrderCommand - Transaction: name: OrderCreationTransaction transaction_type: local isolation_level: read_committed timeout_seconds: 30 executes_actions: - CreateOrder - DeductInventory Compensation steps for sagas For each forward step in a saga workflow, the extraction agent SHOULD create a corresponding compensation step and link it via compensated_by_step. Compensation steps are themselves Step instances: - Step: name: ReleaseInventory order: 1 executes_actions_in_step: - ReleaseInventoryCommand 8. Step 7: Synthesize Capabilities and Features Capability and Feature represent the highest level of abstraction in SAO. They describe what the system can do and how users experience it. Capability A discrete business or technical ability the system provides. Attribute Description name Capability name description What this capability provides provided_by_modules Module instances that implement this capability requires_permissions Permission instances needed (from Phase 6) realizes_features Feature instances this capability realizes enables_features Feature instances this capability enables Feature A user-facing manifestation of one or more capabilities. Attribute Description name Feature name category core, optional, experimental, deprecated enabled_by_capabilities Capability instances that enable this feature realized_by_capabilities Capability instances that realize this feature controlled_by_configs Configuration instances (for feature flags) accessible_by_roles Role instances that can access this feature Sources: product documentation, feature flag configurations (LaunchDarkly, Unleash, @FeatureToggle), capability-oriented package structure, marketing materials, user stories. - Capability: name: OrderManagement description: Ability to create, track, modify, and cancel customer orders provided_by_modules: - OrderModule - InventoryModule requires_permissions: - orders.create - orders.read - orders.update - orders.cancel realizes_features: - OnlineOrdering enables_features: - OrderTracking - OrderHistory - Feature: name: OnlineOrdering description: Allows customers to place orders through the web storefront category: core enabled_by_capabilities: - OrderManagement - PaymentProcessing - InventoryManagement realized_by_capabilities: - OrderManagement controlled_by_configs: - OnlineOrderingFeatureFlag accessible_by_roles: - Customer - Administrator - Feature: name: BetaRecommendationEngine description: AI-powered product recommendations on product pages category: experimental enabled_by_capabilities: - RecommendationEngine controlled_by_configs: - RecommendationEngineToggle accessible_by_roles: - BetaCustomer 9. Phase 5 Checklist Before proceeding to Phase 6, verify the following: [ ] Actors identified. Both HumanActor and SystemActor instances created with correct actor_type values. Every actor has a name and description. [ ] Operations extracted. Each named business action has an Operation instance. Every Operation MUST link to at least one CallableUnit via implemented_by_callables. [ ] Actions classified. Every business action is classified as a Query or Command with correct category and (for commands) command_type. [ ] Rules extracted. Validation constraints, business policies, and guard clauses captured as Rule instances with category, condition, and action set. [ ] Events identified. Significant domain occurrences captured as DomainEvent instances; cross-service events captured as IntegrationEvent instances. Each event has a category and links to its producing Aggregate or target services. [ ] Subscriptions created. Event consumers registered as Subscription instances linking events to actors. [ ] Workflows extracted. Multi-step business processes captured as Workflow instances with ordered Step sequences. Saga workflows include compensation steps. [ ] Transactions defined. Transaction boundaries captured as Transaction instances with transaction_type and isolation_level. [ ] Capabilities and Features synthesized. System abilities captured as Capability instances; user-facing features captured as Feature instances with appropriate category. [ ] Human review flagged. All entities produced in this phase are marked for domain expert validation.
entries.title: Phase 5: Business Intent

entries.description: Input: All prior phase outputs + configs + deployment manifests + CI/CD files + test files + documentation Output: Classes across SAO Sections 2-3 (Identity/Auth), 8 (Deployment), 9 (Observability), 10 (Compliance), 11 (Testing), 12 (UI),…
entries.text: Phase 6: Cross-Cutting Concerns Input: All prior phase outputs + configs + deployment manifests + CI/CD files + test files + documentation Output: Classes across SAO Sections 2-3 (Identity/Auth), 8 (Deployment), 9 (Observability), 10 (Compliance), 11 (Testing), 12 (UI), 13-14 (Build/CI/CD), 15-17 (Advanced), 30 (Knowledge) 1. Overview Cross-cutting concerns span every layer of a software system. Security, identity, testing, deployment, observability, compliance, UI structure, CI/CD, concurrency, and knowledge artifacts are not confined to a single architectural tier -- they attach everywhere. This phase can start as soon as Phase 2 completes and MAY run in parallel with Phases 3-5. It is organized into two independent groups: Group A: Security, Governance, Quality -- Identity, authorization, compliance, testing, UI, build/CI-CD, and knowledge artifacts. Group B: Runtime & Ops -- Deployment, observability, and concurrency. The two groups have no ordering dependency on each other and MAY be worked on simultaneously. Automation varies by subsection (40-80%): identity and CI/CD extraction are largely automatable from configuration files, while compliance and knowledge artifacts typically require human judgment. 2. Group A: Security, Governance, Quality 2.1 Identity and Multi-Tenancy Extract the identity model -- how users, services, and external actors are represented and authenticated. Classes: Identity, Credential, Tenant, Organization Class Key attributes Links Identity identity_type represents_actor -> Actor, has_roles -> Role, belongs_to_tenant -> Tenant, member_of_organizations -> Organization Credential credential_type, expires_at, is_active Inlined under Identity via credentials Tenant name organizations -> Organization, settings -> Configuration, contains_identities -> Identity Organization name parent / children -> Organization, has_identity_members -> Identity credential_type permissible values (enum CredentialType): password token certificate api_key biometric mfa oauth Sources: Auth configuration files, identity provider integration code (OIDC, SAML, LDAP), user model definitions, session management code. Extraction guidance: Scan for authentication middleware, login controllers, and identity provider SDKs. For each distinct identity type, create an Identity and link it to the corresponding Actor via represents_actor. Create Credential instances for each authentication mechanism. If the system is multi-tenant, create Tenant and Organization instances from tenant configuration or database schemas. identities: - name: UserIdentity identity_type: human_user represents_actor: EndUser credentials: - name: PasswordCredential credential_type: password is_active: true - name: OAuthCredential credential_type: oauth is_active: true belongs_to_tenant: DefaultTenant has_roles: [CustomerRole] 2.2 Authorization and Policy Extract the authorization model -- how permissions are granted, scoped, and enforced. Classes: Role, Permission, Policy, Scope, Constraint Class Key attributes Links Role name, is_system_role grants_permissions -> Permission, inherits_from_role -> Role, can_access_features -> Feature Permission name allows_actions -> Action, applies_to_resource_types -> ResourceType, limited_by_scope -> Scope Policy policy_type, priority evaluates_permissions -> Permission, enforced_by_system -> System, guards_routes -> Route Scope scope_type, resource_pattern limits_permissions -> Permission Constraint constraint_type, expression Inlined under Permission via constraints policy_type permissible values (enum PolicyType): rbac abac rebac pbac scope_type permissible values (enum ScopeType): global tenant organization resource field constraint_type permissible values (enum ConstraintType): temporal spatial attribute context rate_limit Sources: RBAC configuration files, @PreAuthorize / @Secured / @RolesAllowed annotations, policy engines (OPA, Casbin), IAM definitions (AWS IAM policies, Azure RBAC), middleware guard code. Extraction guidance: Identify all roles from configuration or code annotations. For each role, create a Role and link it to the permissions it grants. Create a Policy for each distinct authorization strategy. If roles inherit from other roles, set inherits_from_role. Scopes and constraints SHOULD be extracted from conditional access logic (e.g., tenant-scoped queries, time-based restrictions). roles: - name: Admin is_system_role: true grants_permissions: [ManageUsers, ManageOrders] inherits_from_role: Viewer permissions: - name: ManageUsers allows_actions: [CreateUser, UpdateUser, DeleteUser] applies_to_resource_types: [UserResource] limited_by_scope: TenantScope constraints: - name: BusinessHoursOnly constraint_type: temporal expression: "time.hour >= 9 && time.hour <= 17" policies: - name: TenantRBAC policy_type: rbac evaluates_permissions: [ManageUsers, ManageOrders] scopes: - name: TenantScope scope_type: tenant resource_pattern: "tenant/${tenant_id}/*" 2.3 Compliance and Governance Extract compliance obligations, controls, evidence, and risk assessments. Classes: ComplianceRequirement, Control, Evidence, RiskAssessment Class Key attributes Links ComplianceRequirement framework, effective_date controls -> Control (inlined), applies_to_systems -> System Control control_id, implementation, frequency evidence -> Evidence (inlined), owned_by_actor -> Actor, mitigates_risks -> RiskAssessment Evidence evidence_type, collected_at, artifact_uri verified_by_actor -> Actor RiskAssessment risk_level, threats, vulnerabilities, residual_risk mitigated_by_controls -> Control, assesses_system -> System framework permissible values (enum ComplianceFramework): gdpr hipaa soc2 pci_dss iso27001 sox ccpa fedramp Sources: Compliance documentation, audit records, security policies, data processing agreements, privacy impact assessments. Extraction guidance: Identify applicable compliance frameworks from documentation, README files, or legal notices. For each framework, create a ComplianceRequirement and list its Control instances. Controls SHOULD reference the Actor who owns them and any Evidence that proves effectiveness. RiskAssessment instances MAY be created from security review documents or threat models. compliance_requirements: - name: GDPR Compliance framework: gdpr effective_date: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" applies_to_systems: [OrderManagementSystem] controls: - name: DataEncryptionAtRest control_id: GDPR-ENC-001 implementation: "AES-256 encryption for all PII fields" owned_by_actor: SecurityTeam evidence: - name: EncryptionAuditLog evidence_type: automated_scan artifact_uri: "s3://audits/enc-report-2024-q2.pdf" 2.4 Testing Catalog test suites, individual test cases, assertions, and coverage metrics. Classes: TestSuite, TestCase, TestAssertion, TestCoverage Class Key attributes Links TestSuite suite_type (required), framework, source_location, total_cases, passing_cases, failing_cases contains_test_cases -> TestCase, tests_component -> Component, tests_module -> Module TestCase status, priority, is_automated assertions -> TestAssertion (inlined), belongs_to_suite -> TestSuite, tests_callable -> CallableUnit, tests_operation -> Operation TestAssertion assertion_type, expected_value, line_number Inlined under TestCase TestCoverage line_coverage_percent, branch_coverage_percent, function_coverage_percent, coverage_tool coverage_for_component -> Component, coverage_for_module -> Module suite_type permissible values (enum TestSuiteType): unit integration functional end_to_end performance security regression smoke contract status permissible values (enum TestCaseStatus): passing failing skipped flaky pending assertion_type permissible values (enum AssertionType): equality truthiness exception type_check containment mock_verification snapshot custom Sources: Test directories (test/, tests/, __tests__/, spec/), test runner configuration (Jest, pytest, JUnit, Go test), coverage reports (Istanbul, JaCoCo, coverage.py). Extraction guidance: Scan test directories and files (patterns like *_test.go, *Test.java, test_*.py, *.spec.ts). Create one TestSuite per logical grouping (typically per test file or class). For each test function, create a TestCase linked to the CallableUnit or Operation it tests. Coverage data SHOULD be extracted from coverage reports if available. test_suites: - name: UserServiceTests suite_type: unit framework: pytest source_location: tests/test_user_service.py total_cases: 12 passing_cases: 11 failing_cases: 1 tests_component: UserServiceComponent contains_test_cases: - name: test_create_user_success status: passing is_automated: true tests_operation: CreateUserOp assertions: - name: assert_user_created assertion_type: equality expected_value: "201" test_coverage: - name: UserServiceCoverage line_coverage_percent: 87.5 branch_coverage_percent: 72.0 coverage_tool: coverage.py coverage_for_component: UserServiceComponent 2.5 UI/Frontend Map frontend component hierarchies, routing structure, and state management. Classes: UIComponent, Route, StateStore Class Key attributes Links UIComponent component_type (required), framework, is_lazy_loaded, is_server_rendered, source_location has_parent_ui_component / has_child_ui_components -> UIComponent, renders_on_route -> Route, managed_by_state -> StateStore Route path_pattern (required), route_type, is_dynamic, is_authenticated route_renders_component -> UIComponent, has_parent_route / has_child_routes -> Route, route_guarded_by -> Policy StateStore management_type (required), framework, actions, selectors manages_ui_components -> UIComponent component_type permissible values (enum UIComponentType): page layout form widget modal navigation data_display composite higher_order provider route_type permissible values (enum RouteType): page_route api_route layout_route redirect catch_all guarded management_type permissible values (enum StateManagementType): local_state global_store context url_state server_state form_state Sources: Frontend component files (.tsx, .vue, .svelte), routing configuration (react-router, vue-router, Next.js app/ directory), state management setup (Redux store, Vuex/Pinia modules, Zustand stores). Extraction guidance: Walk the frontend source tree and create a UIComponent for each component file. Set has_parent_ui_component / has_child_ui_components from import analysis and JSX/template usage. Extract routes from routing configuration; for file-based routing (Next.js, Nuxt), derive path_pattern from directory structure. If a route requires authentication, set is_authenticated to true and link route_guarded_by to the relevant Policy. ui_components: - name: DashboardPage component_type: page framework: react source_location: src/pages/Dashboard.tsx renders_on_route: [DashboardRoute] managed_by_state: [AppStore] child_ui_components: [OrdersWidget, UserStatsWidget] routes: - name: DashboardRoute path_pattern: /dashboard route_type: page_route is_authenticated: true route_guarded_by: [TenantRBAC] state_stores: - name: AppStore management_type: global_store framework: zustand actions: [fetchOrders, updateUser] selectors: [selectCurrentUser, selectOrderList] 2.6 Build, CI/CD, and Dependencies Document build pipelines, their stages, produced artifacts, registries, and known vulnerabilities. Classes: BuildPipeline, PipelineStage, BuildArtifact, ArtifactRegistry, KnownVulnerability Class Key attributes Links BuildPipeline pipeline_type (required), platform, trigger, source_file stages -> PipelineStage (inlined), pipeline_deploys_to_environments -> Environment, pipeline_produces_artifacts -> BuildArtifact PipelineStage stage_type (required), order, condition, runner, is_manual Inlined under BuildPipeline BuildArtifact artifact_type (required), artifact_uri, size_bytes, checksum artifact_produced_by_pipeline -> BuildPipeline, artifact_stored_in_registry -> ArtifactRegistry ArtifactRegistry registry_type, base_url, is_private stores_artifacts -> BuildArtifact KnownVulnerability cve_id, severity (required), cvss_score, affected_versions, fixed_version Inlined under PackageDependency pipeline_type permissible values (enum PipelineType): build test deploy release integration delivery validation stage_type permissible values (enum PipelineStageType): checkout build test lint security_scan package publish deploy approval rollback notify artifact_type permissible values (enum ArtifactType): container_image binary archive package library documentation report load_module severity permissible values (enum VulnerabilitySeverity): critical high medium low none Sources: CI/CD configuration files (.github/workflows/*.yml, Jenkinsfile, .gitlab-ci.yml, azure-pipelines.yml, Makefile), package manifests, vulnerability scan reports (npm audit, snyk, trivy). Extraction guidance: Locate all CI/CD configuration files and create one BuildPipeline per pipeline definition. Parse stages in order and create PipelineStage instances with sequential order values. Identify produced artifacts and their registries. For known vulnerabilities, parse audit reports or lock file advisories and link KnownVulnerability instances to the affected PackageDependency (from Phase 1). build_pipelines: - name: MainCI pipeline_type: integration platform: github_actions source_file: .github/workflows/ci.yml trigger: [push, pull_request] trigger_branches: [main, "feature/**"] pipeline_deploys_to_environments: [Staging] stages: - name: Checkout stage_type: checkout order: 1 - name: Lint stage_type: lint order: 2 - name: UnitTests stage_type: test order: 3 - name: BuildImage stage_type: build order: 4 - name: PushToRegistry stage_type: publish order: 5 pipeline_produces_artifacts: [AppImage] build_artifacts: - name: AppImage artifact_type: container_image artifact_uri: "ghcr.io/acme/app:latest" artifact_stored_in_registry: GHCRRegistry artifact_registries: - name: GHCRRegistry registry_type: container base_url: "https://ghcr.io/acme" is_private: true 2.7 Knowledge Artifacts Index documentation, decision records, runbooks, and other knowledge artifacts. Class: KnowledgeArtifact Attribute Type Description artifact_type KnowledgeArtifactType Category of the artifact status KnowledgeArtifactStatus Lifecycle state uri URI Location of the artifact content string Inline content (optional) authored_by string (multivalued) Author names authored_at Timestamp Creation date Links: documents_system, documents_bounded_context, documents_module, documents_component, documents_aggregate, documents_domain_entity, documents_service, documents_integration, stored_in_container -> CodeContainer. artifact_type permissible values (enum KnowledgeArtifactType): adr readme design_doc runbook wiki_page api_doc onboarding_guide postmortem changelog comment diagram rfc sop status permissible values (enum KnowledgeArtifactStatus): draft published accepted superseded deprecated archived Sources: README files, docs/ directories, ADR directories (docs/adr/, docs/decisions/), wiki pages, inline code comments of architectural significance. Extraction guidance: Scan for documentation files (Markdown, AsciiDoc, reStructuredText) across the repository. Create a KnowledgeArtifact for each significant document and link it to the SAO entity it documents via the appropriate documents_* relationship. For ADRs, set status to accepted or superseded based on the ADR header. Supersession chains SHOULD use superseded_by / supersedes links. knowledge_artifacts: - name: ADR-001 Use PostgreSQL artifact_type: adr status: accepted uri: docs/adr/001-use-postgresql.md authored_by: ["Jane Doe"] documents_system: OrderManagementSystem - name: API Reference artifact_type: api_doc status: published uri: docs/api-reference.md documents_service: OrderService 3. Group B: Runtime & Ops 3.1 Deployment and Operations Capture the deployment topology -- environments, deployment units, configuration, infrastructure, and releases. Classes: Environment, Deployment, DeploymentUnit, Configuration, Infrastructure, Release Class Key attributes Links Environment environment_type hosts_deployments -> Deployment, env_configured_by -> Configuration, uses_infrastructure -> Infrastructure, deployed_by_pipelines -> BuildPipeline Deployment replicas deploys_service -> Service, deployed_in_environment -> Environment, deploys_unit -> DeploymentUnit, deployment_configured_by -> Configuration, deploys_release -> Release DeploymentUnit unit_type, artifact_uri, checksum deployed_in_deployments -> Deployment Configuration config_type, value, is_secret, source controls_features -> Feature, configures_environments -> Environment, configures_deployments -> Deployment Infrastructure infra_type, provider, region hosts_datastores -> DataStore, used_by_environments -> Environment, infrastructure_provisioned_by_iac -> IaCDefinition Release version, changelog artifacts -> DeploymentUnit, deployed_in_deployments_as_release -> Deployment environment_type permissible values (enum EnvironmentType): development testing staging production dr unit_type permissible values (enum DeploymentUnitType): container vm serverless_function binary package config_type permissible values (enum ConfigurationType): environment_variable config_file secret feature_flag remote_config infra_type permissible values (enum InfrastructureType): compute storage network load_balancer dns cdn firewall api_gateway service_mesh Sources: Dockerfiles, Kubernetes manifests, docker-compose.yml, serverless configs (serverless.yml, sam.yaml), Terraform/CloudFormation definitions, Helm charts, environment-specific config files. Extraction guidance: Create one Environment per deployment target. For each service deployed to an environment, create a Deployment linking the Service, Environment, and DeploymentUnit. Extract configuration from .env files, application.yml, Kubernetes ConfigMaps/Secrets -- set is_secret: true for sensitive values but MUST NOT include the actual secret value. Create Infrastructure instances from IaC definitions. Release instances SHOULD be created from release tags or changelogs. environments: - name: Production environment_type: production uses_infrastructure: [ProdK8sCluster, ProdPostgres] env_configured_by: [ProdDatabaseUrl] deployed_by_pipelines: [MainCI] deployments: - name: OrderServiceProd replicas: 3 deploys_service: OrderService deployed_in_environment: Production deploys_unit: OrderServiceContainer deploys_release: Release_v2_1_0 deployment_units: - name: OrderServiceContainer unit_type: container artifact_uri: "ghcr.io/acme/order-service:2.1.0" configurations: - name: ProdDatabaseUrl config_type: environment_variable source: kubernetes_secret is_secret: true - name: EnableNewCheckout config_type: feature_flag value: "true" is_secret: false infrastructure: - name: ProdK8sCluster infra_type: compute provider: aws region: us-east-1 3.2 Observability Document metrics, logs, traces, health checks, alerts, and incidents. Classes: Metric, Log, LogEntry, Trace, Span, HealthCheck, Alert, AlertRule, Incident Class Key attributes Links Metric metric_type, unit, labels metric_emitted_by_component -> Component, monitored_by_alert_rules -> AlertRule Log log_type contains_entries -> LogEntry, log_governed_by_retention -> RetentionPolicy LogEntry timestamp, level, message entry_in_log -> Log Trace trace_id contains_spans -> Span, starts_with_span -> Span Span span_id, operation_name, start_time, end_time, status belongs_to_trace -> Trace, child_of_span / parent_of_spans -> Span HealthCheck check_type, endpoint, interval_seconds, timeout_seconds -- Alert severity, triggered_at, acknowledged_at, resolved_at triggered_by_rule -> AlertRule, escalates_to_incident -> Incident AlertRule condition, threshold, duration_seconds, notification_channels monitors_metrics -> Metric, triggers_alerts -> Alert Incident severity, status, root_cause, postmortem_url escalated_from_alerts -> Alert, affects_services -> Service metric_type permissible values (enum MetricType): counter gauge histogram summary log_type permissible values (enum LogType): application access error security audit debug check_type permissible values (enum HealthCheckType): liveness readiness dependency startup Sources: Monitoring configuration (Prometheus rules, Datadog monitors, Grafana dashboards), health check endpoints (/health, /ready), alerting rules, logging configuration (log4j, Winston, slog), distributed tracing setup (OpenTelemetry, Jaeger). Extraction guidance: Scan for metric definitions in code (Prometheus registrations, StatsD calls). Create a Metric for each and link it to the emitting Component. Identify logging configuration to create Log instances -- the extraction agent SHOULD NOT create individual LogEntry instances during static extraction (those are runtime artifacts). Extract health check endpoints from framework configuration (Spring Boot Actuator, Kubernetes probes). Parse alerting rules to create AlertRule instances. Incident instances MAY be created from postmortem documents. metrics: - name: http_requests_total metric_type: counter unit: requests labels: [method, status_code, path] metric_emitted_by_component: APIGatewayComponent health_checks: - name: LivenessProbe check_type: liveness endpoint: /health/live interval_seconds: 10 timeout_seconds: 3 alert_rules: - name: HighErrorRate condition: "rate(http_requests_total{status_code=~'5..'}[5m]) > 0.05" threshold: 0.05 duration_seconds: 300 notification_channels: ["#alerts-critical", pagerduty] monitors_metrics: [http_requests_total] 3.3 Concurrency (if applicable) Document synchronization primitives and concurrency patterns. This subsection applies only to systems with explicit concurrency management. Skip it for purely request-response web applications that delegate concurrency to the framework. Classes: ConcurrencyPrimitive, ConcurrencyPattern Class Key attributes Links ConcurrencyPrimitive primitive_type (required), is_reentrant, timeout_ms, line_number used_by_callables -> CallableUnit, protects_data_elements -> DataElement ConcurrencyPattern pattern_type (required), max_concurrency, framework, shared_resources pattern_used_by_component -> Component primitive_type permissible values (enum ConcurrencyPrimitiveType): mutex semaphore read_write_lock spin_lock condition_variable barrier latch atomic pattern_type permissible values (enum ConcurrencyPatternType): thread_pool actor channel future_promise async_await fork_join producer_consumer reactor proactor csp Sources: Thread management code, async runtime configuration, channel usage, lock declarations, actor system setup (Akka, Erlang/OTP), thread pool configuration. Extraction guidance: Search for lock primitives (sync.Mutex, ReentrantLock, threading.Lock, std::mutex) and create ConcurrencyPrimitive instances. Identify higher-level patterns (thread pools, actor systems, async runtimes) and create ConcurrencyPattern instances. Link primitives to the CallableUnit that uses them and the DataElement they protect. concurrency_primitives: - name: OrderCacheLock primitive_type: read_write_lock is_reentrant: false used_by_callables: - getOrderFromCache - updateOrderCache protects_data_elements: - orderCacheMap concurrency_patterns: - name: RequestWorkerPool pattern_type: thread_pool max_concurrency: 50 framework: java.util.concurrent pattern_used_by_component: OrderProcessorComponent - name: EventProcessor pattern_type: async_await framework: tokio pattern_used_by_component: EventHandlerComponent 4. Phase 6 Checklist Before proceeding, verify that the following items have been addressed: [ ] Identity and authorization model extracted -- Identity, Credential, Role, Permission, Policy, Scope, and Constraint instances created [ ] Compliance requirements documented -- ComplianceRequirement, Control, Evidence, and RiskAssessment instances created (if applicable) [ ] Test suites cataloged -- TestSuite, TestCase, and TestCoverage instances created with links to the components and operations they test [ ] UI components mapped -- UIComponent, Route, and StateStore instances created (if frontend exists) [ ] CI/CD pipelines documented -- BuildPipeline, PipelineStage, BuildArtifact, and ArtifactRegistry instances created [ ] Knowledge artifacts indexed -- KnowledgeArtifact instances created for significant documentation [ ] Deployment topology captured -- Environment, Deployment, DeploymentUnit, Configuration, Infrastructure, and Release instances created [ ] Observability infrastructure documented -- Metric, HealthCheck, AlertRule, Log, and Trace instances created [ ] Concurrency patterns noted -- ConcurrencyPrimitive and ConcurrencyPattern instances created (if applicable) [ ] All enum values use exact permissible_values from legacy/sao/sao.yml [ ] Cross-references to entities from prior phases (e.g., Component, Service, Actor, Operation) are consistent

headings.title: Entities that MUST NOT be orphans

entries.text: Phase 7: Bridge Relationships and Graph Stitching Input: All outputs from Phases 1-6 (complete entity instances across all SAO layers) Output: Verified and completed cross-layer relationships; orphan report; symmetry verification results 1. Overview The SAO's power lies in its cross-layer bridges. They connect code to architecture, architecture to domain, and domain to business intent. Without them, each layer is an isolated catalog; with them, the SAO becomes a navigable graph where any question — "what code implements this business capability?" or "what business purpose does this function serve?" — is answerable by traversal. After independent extraction in Phases 1-6, bridges are often incomplete or inconsistent. Each phase focuses on its own layer and creates entities with forward references that may not yet have targets, or creates targets without backlinks. This is expected and by design: each phase is self-contained so it can be executed and validated independently. Phase 7 is a systematic verification and gap-filling pass. It does not create new entities. It examines the relationships between existing entities, identifies missing or asymmetric links, and completes them. The SAO documents 214 bidirectional relationship pairs; the most critical are the eight cross-layer bridges described in this document. This phase is not about discovery. If an entity is missing, the extraction agent SHOULD return to the appropriate earlier phase to create it. Phase 7 only stitches together what already exists. 2. The Eight Critical Bridges The SAO guide identifies eight cross-layer bridges that form the connective tissue of the ontology. Each bridge is a bidirectional relationship pair connecting entities in different conceptual layers. The extraction agent MUST verify all eight bridges and fill any gaps. Bridge 1: Module to StorageLocation Attribute Value Forward Module.mapped_from_directory --> StorageLocation Inverse StorageLocation.maps_to_module --> Module Layers Layer 4 (Architecture) <-> Layer 3 (Code Structure) What it connects. This bridge links the logical module structure (how architects think about the system) to the physical directory tree (how the file system organizes the code). It is typically the first bridge established, since Modules are created directly from StorageLocations in Phase 3. Verification. Every Module SHOULD have at least one mapped_from_directory reference to a StorageLocation. Every top-level StorageLocation (one that represents a cohesive package or directory tree) SHOULD have a maps_to_module reference back to a Module. Common gap. Modules created in Phase 3 sometimes lack backlinks to the StorageLocations identified in Phase 1. This happens when Phase 3 creates Modules from build manifests rather than from the directory walk, or when a Module spans multiple directories and only one is linked. The extraction agent MUST walk the Module list and verify each has a mapped_from_directory value. If a Module has no mapped directory, check Phase 1 outputs for the matching StorageLocation and add the link in both directions. Bridge 2: Component to EncapsulationUnit Attribute Value Forward Component.implemented_by_code --> EncapsulationUnit (list) Inverse EncapsulationUnit.implements_component --> Component Layers Layer 4 (Architecture) <-> Layer 3 (Code Structure) What it connects. This bridge links architectural components (logical groupings of functionality) to the code units that implement them. A single Component may be implemented by many EncapsulationUnits, but each EncapsulationUnit with an architectural role SHOULD link to exactly one Component. Verification. Every Component MUST have at least one implemented_by_code reference. Every EncapsulationUnit that plays a clear architectural role (controllers, services, repositories, domain models) SHOULD have an implements_component reference. Common gap. Utility and helper classes often remain unlinked. This is acceptable -- not every EncapsulationUnit has a meaningful architectural role. However, the extraction agent SHOULD verify that the unlinked units are genuinely utilities rather than overlooked implementation classes. A quick check: if an EncapsulationUnit is referenced by a CallableUnit that implements an Operation, it likely belongs to a Component. Bridge 3: DomainEntity to DataStructure Attribute Value Forward DomainEntity.mapped_from_structure --> DataStructure Inverse DataStructure.maps_to_domain_entity --> DomainEntity Layers Layer 5 (Domain) <-> Layer 3 (Code Structure) What it connects. This bridge links business-meaningful entities (the domain model) to their code-level representations (classes, structs, records). It is the primary bridge between "what the business cares about" and "what the code defines." Verification. Every DomainEntity MUST have a mapped_from_structure reference. Not every DataStructure needs a domain mapping -- DTOs, internal value holders, configuration objects, and framework scaffolding do not represent domain concepts. Common gap. DomainEntities created in Phase 4 are sometimes synthesized from documentation or domain knowledge without being linked back to their originating DataStructure. The extraction agent MUST verify that each DomainEntity traces to at least one code-level structure. If no matching DataStructure exists, return to Phase 2 to extract it. Bridge 4: Attribute to DataElement Attribute Value Forward Attribute.mapped_from_element --> DataElement Inverse DataElement.maps_to_attribute --> Attribute Layers Layer 5 (Domain) <-> Layer 3 (Code Structure) What it connects. This is the field-level counterpart to Bridge 3. It links individual domain attributes to their code-level data elements (fields, columns, properties). Verification. Every Attribute on a DomainEntity SHOULD have a mapped_from_element reference. Computed or derived attributes that have no direct code-level representation MAY omit this bridge. Common gap. Attributes are often created in Phase 4 by examining DomainEntities without tracing each field back to a specific DataElement. The extraction agent SHOULD walk each DomainEntity, compare its Attributes to the DataElements on the linked DataStructure (from Bridge 3), and establish the field-level mappings. Bridge 5: Operation to CallableUnit Attribute Value Forward Operation.implemented_by_callables --> CallableUnit (list) Inverse CallableUnit.implements_operation --> Operation Layers Layer 6 (Business Intent) <-> Layer 3 (Code Structure) What it connects. This bridge links business operations (what the system does from a user's perspective) to the code that implements them. A single Operation is typically implemented by multiple CallableUnits working together. Verification. Every Operation MUST have at least one implemented_by_callables reference. Not every CallableUnit implements an Operation -- internal methods, private helpers, and framework callbacks do not represent business operations. Common gap. Operations created in Phase 5 are often synthesized from use case analysis without tracing back to implementing code. The extraction agent MUST verify each Operation links to at least one CallableUnit. Start from the Operation, identify the entry-point CallableUnit (typically a controller method or API handler), and link it. Bridge 6: Capability to Module Attribute Value Forward Capability.provided_by_modules --> Module (list) Inverse Module.provides_capabilities --> Capability (list) Layers Layer 6 (Business Intent) <-> Layer 4 (Architecture) What it connects. This bridge links high-level business capabilities (what the system can do) to the architectural modules that provide them. It answers the question: "which part of the codebase is responsible for this business capability?" Verification. Every Capability SHOULD link to at least one Module via provided_by_modules. Every Module that has a clear business purpose SHOULD list its capabilities via provides_capabilities. Common gap. Capabilities synthesized in Phase 5 from business documentation are often left floating without links to the implementing modules. The extraction agent SHOULD examine each Capability, determine which Module(s) contribute to it, and establish the links in both directions. Bridge 7: Service to Module Attribute Value Forward Service.runs_module --> Module Inverse Module.runs_as_services --> Service (list) Layers Layer 4 (Architecture runtime) <-> Layer 4 (Architecture logical) What it connects. This bridge links runtime deployment units (services, processes, containers) to the logical module structure. While both entities live in Layer 4, they represent different perspectives: Module is the logical grouping of code, while Service is the runtime incarnation. Verification. Every Service SHOULD link to the Module it runs via runs_module. Every Module that has a deployment manifest (Dockerfile, Kubernetes deployment, serverless config) SHOULD link to its corresponding Service via runs_as_services. Common gap. Services identified from deployment manifests in Phase 3 are sometimes not linked to their Module because the naming conventions differ (e.g., the Kubernetes deployment is named order-svc but the module is named orders). The extraction agent SHOULD match services to modules by examining deployment configs, entry points, and build targets. Bridge 8: KnowledgeArtifact to Documented Entities Attribute Value Forward KnowledgeArtifact.documents_system, documents_bounded_context, documents_module, documents_component, documents_aggregate, documents_domain_entity, etc. Inverse System.system_documented_by_artifacts, Module.module_documented_by_artifacts, etc. Layers Cross-cutting <-> All layers What it connects. This bridge links documentation artifacts (READMEs, ADRs, wiki pages, API docs, runbooks) to the entities they describe. Unlike the other bridges, this one fans out across all layers. Verification. Every KnowledgeArtifact SHOULD link to at least one entity it documents via the appropriate documents_* attribute. Key entities -- System, BoundedContexts, critical Modules -- SHOULD have at least one *_documented_by_artifacts reference. Common gap. KnowledgeArtifacts created in Phase 6 are often cataloged without linking to the specific entities they describe. The extraction agent SHOULD read each KnowledgeArtifact's content (or summary) and match it to the most relevant entity. A README in a module directory documents that Module. An ADR about authentication documents the relevant Component and BoundedContext. 3. Graph Connectivity Checks After verifying all eight bridges, the extraction agent MUST perform three traversal checks to confirm the graph is fully connected. Top-down traversal Starting from the System instance, verify that every entity is reachable by following containment and bridge relationships downward: System └─ contains_bounded_contexts ──> BoundedContext (each one) └─ contains_modules ──> Module (each one) └─ contains_components ──> Component (each one) └─ implemented_by_code ──> EncapsulationUnit (each one) └─ contains_callable_units ──> CallableUnit (each one) Every BoundedContext MUST be reachable from the System. Every Module MUST be reachable from a BoundedContext. Every Component MUST be reachable from a Module. If any entity is unreachable, the containment hierarchy has a gap that MUST be fixed. Bottom-up traversal Starting from any CallableUnit, verify that you can trace upward to the System: CallableUnit └─ contained_in_unit ──> EncapsulationUnit └─ implements_component ──> Component └─ part_of_module ──> Module └─ belongs_to_bounded_context ──> BoundedContext └─ part_of_system ──> System Select a sample of CallableUnits (at minimum, every entry-point callable such as API handlers, event listeners, and scheduled tasks) and verify each can be traced to the System. Any break in the chain indicates a missing relationship. Cross-layer traversal Starting from a DomainEntity, verify that you can reach both the code layer (downward) and the architectural layer (upward): DomainEntity ├─ mapped_from_structure ──> DataStructure (down to code) │ └─ contained_in_unit ──> EncapsulationUnit └─ part_of_aggregate ──> Aggregate (up to architecture) └─ owned_by_bounded_context ──> BoundedContext └─ part_of_system ──> System This traversal confirms that the domain model is properly anchored to both code and architecture. Every DomainEntity MUST be reachable from both directions. 4. Orphan Detection An orphan is an entity with no incoming or outgoing cross-layer relationships. Orphans indicate extraction gaps -- entities that were created but never connected to the broader graph. Acceptable orphans Some entities MAY legitimately have no cross-layer bridges: EncapsulationUnits that are pure utilities, internal helpers, or framework-generated scaffolding CallableUnits that are private methods, getters/setters, or framework callbacks DataStructures that are DTOs, internal value holders, or configuration objects DataElements on non-domain structures These entities still MUST have intra-layer relationships (e.g., an EncapsulationUnit MUST still have contained_in_container linking it to a CodeContainer), but they do not need cross-layer bridges. Entities that MUST NOT be orphans The following entity types MUST have at least the specified cross-layer relationships: Entity type Required relationship(s) System contains_bounded_contexts BoundedContext contains_modules, part_of_system Module mapped_from_directory, belongs_to_bounded_context Component implemented_by_code, part_of_module Service runs_module DomainEntity mapped_from_structure, part_of_aggregate Aggregate root_entity, owned_by_bounded_context Operation implemented_by_callables Capability provided_by_modules KnowledgeArtifact At least one documents_* reference Systematic orphan check For each entity type in the table above, the extraction agent MUST: List all instances of that type For each instance, verify the required relationship(s) exist and point to valid targets Record any orphans in an orphan report For each orphan, either fill the missing relationship or document why the entity is intentionally unlinked The orphan report SHOULD be structured as a table: Entity type Entity name Missing relationship Resolution Module analytics mapped_from_directory Linked to StorageLocation src/analytics DomainEntity PaymentMethod mapped_from_structure Linked to DataStructure PaymentMethod in payments/models.py Capability ReportGeneration provided_by_modules Linked to Module reporting 5. Relationship Symmetry Verification Every bidirectional relationship pair in the SAO MUST be symmetric: if entity A references entity B via a forward relationship, then entity B MUST reference entity A via the corresponding inverse relationship. Asymmetric links are a data integrity problem that will cause traversal failures. Verification procedure For each of the eight critical bridges, the extraction agent MUST perform the following check: Forward scan. For each instance of the source entity type, read the forward relationship attribute. For every target entity referenced, verify that the target's inverse attribute includes the source entity. Inverse scan. For each instance of the target entity type, read the inverse relationship attribute. For every source entity referenced, verify that the source's forward attribute includes the target entity. Record asymmetries. Any case where A.forward references B but B.inverse does not reference A (or vice versa) is an asymmetry that MUST be fixed. Example verification for Bridge 2 (Component to EncapsulationUnit): For each Component c: For each EncapsulationUnit eu in c.implemented_by_code: ASSERT eu.implements_component == c If not: set eu.implements_component = c For each EncapsulationUnit eu where eu.implements_component is set: Let c = eu.implements_component ASSERT eu in c.implemented_by_code If not: append eu to c.implemented_by_code Common asymmetries and fixes Asymmetry Typical cause Fix Forward set, inverse missing Entity created in an earlier phase before the target existed Set the inverse on the target entity Inverse set, forward missing Target entity created with a backlink but source not updated Add the reference to the source entity's forward attribute Both set but pointing to different entities Copy-paste error or entity renamed after linking Determine the correct pairing and fix both sides Dangling reference Reference points to an entity ID that does not exist Either create the missing entity (return to the appropriate phase) or remove the dangling reference 6. Phase 7 Checklist Before proceeding to Phase 8, the extraction agent MUST confirm all of the following: [ ] Bridge 1 (Module <-> StorageLocation): All Modules have mapped_from_directory; all relevant StorageLocations have maps_to_module [ ] Bridge 2 (Component <-> EncapsulationUnit): All Components have implemented_by_code; all architecturally significant EncapsulationUnits have implements_component [ ] Bridge 3 (DomainEntity <-> DataStructure): All DomainEntities have mapped_from_structure [ ] Bridge 4 (Attribute <-> DataElement): All domain Attributes have mapped_from_element where a direct mapping exists [ ] Bridge 5 (Operation <-> CallableUnit): All Operations have implemented_by_callables [ ] Bridge 6 (Capability <-> Module): All Capabilities have provided_by_modules [ ] Bridge 7 (Service <-> Module): All Services have runs_module; all deployed Modules have runs_as_services [ ] Bridge 8 (KnowledgeArtifact <-> entities): All KnowledgeArtifacts link to at least one documented entity [ ] Top-down traversal passes: System -> BoundedContext -> Module -> Component -> EncapsulationUnit is fully connected [ ] Bottom-up traversal passes: sampled CallableUnits trace back to System [ ] Cross-layer traversal passes: DomainEntities reach both code and architecture [ ] Orphan report generated and reviewed; no entity in the MUST-connect list is orphaned [ ] Bidirectional symmetry verified for all eight bridges; no asymmetric links remain [ ] No dangling references: every entity ID referenced in a relationship resolves to an existing entity

entries.text: Phase 8: System Context (Layer 1) Input: All outputs from Phases 1--7 Output: Finalized System instance with complete top-level relationships 1. Overview Phase 8 is the capstone of the SAO extraction process. Where prior phases built individual layers from the bottom up -- code structure, architecture, domain model, business intent, cross-cutting concerns, and bridge stitching -- this phase zooms out to the highest level and asks: does the complete picture hold together? The System instance was created in Phase 3 with minimal attributes (name, description, version). At that point, only BoundedContext and Module instances existed to link to it. Now, with all seven prior phases complete, the System MUST be revisited and finalized with every top-level relationship populated. This phase serves two purposes: Assembly. Populate all remaining top-level attributes on the System instance. Sanity check. Verify that the full ontology tells a coherent, complete story when viewed from the root. Automation level: Low. This phase is primarily a review and assembly step. Attribute population can be scripted, but the coherence judgment requires human or LLM reasoning. 2. Finalize the System Instance The System class (defined in legacy/sao/sao.yml as is_a: NamedEntity with the Versionable mixin) has the following top-level relationship attributes. The extraction agent MUST verify that each is populated. Attribute checklist Attribute Range Populated in Action contains_bounded_contexts BoundedContext (multivalued) Phase 3 Verify all contexts are linked has_integrations Integration (multivalued) Phase 3 Verify all integrations are linked exposes_interfaces Interface (multivalued) Phase 3 Verify all top-level interfaces are linked enforces_policies Policy (multivalued) Phase 6 Verify all policies are linked must_comply_with ComplianceRequirement (multivalued) Phase 6 Verify all compliance requirements are linked assessed_by RiskAssessment (multivalued) Phase 6 Verify all risk assessments are linked system_documented_by_artifacts KnowledgeArtifact (multivalued) Phase 6 Link relevant documentation artifacts Note on Environments. The Environment class does not have a direct relationship to System in the current schema. Environments are linked to Deployment instances via Environment.hosts_deployments. The extraction agent SHOULD NOT attempt to add an has_environments attribute to System. Walk-through For each attribute, the extraction agent MUST: Collect all instances of the target class produced across Phases 1--7. Verify that every relevant instance appears in the System's attribute list. An instance is "relevant" if it belongs to this system (as opposed to being an external entity like ExternalSystem). Flag any instance that exists but is not linked. This is either a gap (fix it) or a deliberate exclusion (document why). Complete YAML example The following shows a finalized System instance for an e-commerce order platform: systems: - name: order-platform description: >- E-commerce order management platform handling order placement, payment processing, fulfillment tracking, and customer notifications. version: 2.4.1 contains_bounded_contexts: - name: ordering description: Handles order lifecycle from cart to confirmation contained_in_system: order-platform contains_modules: - order-api - order-domain - order-persistence contains_aggregates: - Order - Cart - name: payments description: Processes payments and manages refunds contained_in_system: order-platform contains_modules: - payment-gateway - payment-ledger contains_aggregates: - Payment - Refund - name: fulfillment description: Tracks shipment and delivery status contained_in_system: order-platform contains_modules: - fulfillment-service - shipping-adapter contains_aggregates: - Shipment has_integrations: - name: stripe-payment-integration description: Payment processing via Stripe API belongs_to_system: order-platform - name: warehouse-integration description: Fulfillment sync with warehouse management system belongs_to_system: order-platform - name: email-notification-integration description: Transactional emails via SendGrid belongs_to_system: order-platform exposes_interfaces: - name: storefront-ui description: Customer-facing web storefront exposed_by_system: order-platform - name: order-rest-api description: REST API for order operations exposed_by_system: order-platform - name: admin-dashboard description: Internal admin interface for order management exposed_by_system: order-platform enforces_policies: - name: rate-limiting-policy description: API rate limiting at 1000 req/min per client enforced_by_system: order-platform - name: data-retention-policy description: Order data retained for 7 years per regulatory requirements enforced_by_system: order-platform must_comply_with: - name: pci-dss description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard applies_to_systems: - order-platform - name: gdpr description: General Data Protection Regulation for EU customer data applies_to_systems: - order-platform assessed_by: - name: annual-security-assessment description: Annual penetration test and security audit assesses_system: order-platform system_documented_by_artifacts: - name: architecture-decision-records description: Collection of ADRs documenting key architectural decisions documents_system: order-platform - name: api-documentation description: OpenAPI specs and developer guides documents_system: order-platform - name: runbook description: Operational runbook for incident response documents_system: order-platform 3. System-Level Sanity Checks Once the System instance is fully populated, the extraction agent MUST perform the following verification checks. 3.1 Completeness Every BoundedContext produced in Phase 3 MUST appear in System.contains_bounded_contexts. To verify: Collect all BoundedContext instances from the extraction output. Compare against the list in System.contains_bounded_contexts. Any BoundedContext not linked to the System is orphaned -- either link it or justify its exclusion. The same check applies to Integration, Interface, Policy, ComplianceRequirement, RiskAssessment, and KnowledgeArtifact instances. 3.2 Consistency Cross-check counts and references for internal consistency: The number of Integration instances SHOULD roughly correspond to the number of distinct ExternalSystem instances. If there are significantly more integrations than external systems, some external systems may have multiple integration points (valid). If there are external systems with no integration, they may be incompletely modeled. The number of top-level Interface instances linked to the System SHOULD match the number of distinct user-facing or API-facing entry points discovered in Phase 3. Every BoundedContext SHOULD contain at least one Module. A context with no modules is likely a modeling gap. 3.3 Coverage Estimate what percentage of the codebase has been decomposed: By files: How many source files are mapped to a StorageLocation that is transitively reachable from the System? Aim for > 90%. By modules: How many top-level directories or build modules are represented as Module instances? Aim for 100%. By code units: How many EncapsulationUnit and CallableUnit instances exist relative to the number of classes/functions in the codebase? Coverage below 80% SHOULD trigger a review of Phases 1--2 to identify unmapped areas. 3.4 Coherence This is the most subjective check. Read the following in sequence: System.name and System.description The name and description of each BoundedContext The name and description of each Integration The name of each top-level Interface Ask: does this tell a coherent story? Can a newcomer read these names and descriptions and understand what the system does, how it is organized, and what it connects to? If not, revise descriptions until the narrative is clear. 4. Generating a System Summary As a final validation artifact, the extraction agent SHOULD generate a human-readable summary from the extracted ontology. This summary serves as both documentation and a smoke test -- if anything looks wrong in the summary, the underlying data likely has a gap. Summary template System: {System.name} (v{System.version}) {System.description} Architecture Bounded contexts: {count} {for each: name -- description} Modules: {total count across all contexts} Components: {total count across all modules} Domain Model Aggregates: {count} Domain entities: {count} Value objects: {count} Integration Landscape External systems: {count} Integrations: {count} {for each: name -- description} Actors Human actors: {count} {for each: name (actor_type)} System actors: {count} {for each: name} Interfaces User interfaces: {count} Programmatic interfaces: {count} Event interfaces: {count} Governance Policies: {count} Compliance requirements: {count} Documentation Knowledge artifacts: {count} Example output System: order-platform (v2.4.1) E-commerce order management platform handling order placement, payment processing, fulfillment tracking, and customer notifications. Architecture Bounded contexts: 3 ordering -- Handles order lifecycle from cart to confirmation payments -- Processes payments and manages refunds fulfillment -- Tracks shipment and delivery status Modules: 6 Components: 14 Domain Model Aggregates: 4 Domain entities: 12 Value objects: 8 Integration Landscape External systems: 3 Integrations: 3 stripe-payment-integration -- Payment processing via Stripe API warehouse-integration -- Fulfillment sync with warehouse management system email-notification-integration -- Transactional emails via SendGrid Actors Human actors: 3 CustomerUser (end_user) SupportAgent (operator) PlatformAdmin (administrator) System actors: 2 PaymentWebhookHandler WarehouseSync Interfaces User interfaces: 2 Programmatic interfaces: 1 Event interfaces: 0 Governance Policies: 2 Compliance requirements: 2 Documentation Knowledge artifacts: 3 The extraction agent SHOULD review this summary with a domain expert. If the summary accurately reflects the system as understood by stakeholders, the extraction is complete. 5. Phase 8 Checklist Before proceeding to Validation (doc 09), confirm every item: [ ] System instance is complete. All seven relationship attributes on System have been reviewed and populated (or explicitly marked as empty with justification). [ ] All BoundedContexts are linked. Every BoundedContext appears in System.contains_bounded_contexts. No orphaned contexts exist. [ ] All Integrations are linked. Every Integration appears in System.has_integrations. [ ] All top-level Interfaces are linked. Every system-level Interface appears in System.exposes_interfaces. [ ] Policies and compliance linked. All Policy instances appear in System.enforces_policies. All ComplianceRequirement instances appear in System.must_comply_with. [ ] Risk assessments linked. All RiskAssessment instances appear in System.assessed_by. [ ] Documentation linked. Relevant KnowledgeArtifact instances appear in System.system_documented_by_artifacts. [ ] System summary generated. A human-readable summary has been produced and reviewed for accuracy. [ ] Coherence verified. The system narrative (names, descriptions, relationships) tells a coherent story. Once all items are confirmed, the extraction is structurally complete. Proceed to Phase 9: Validation for schema-level validation, completeness scoring, and gap analysis.
