entries.text: Turtle authority migration What is authoritative now ontologies/sao/vocabulary/*.ttl are the editable RDFS vocabulary sources. They are no longer regenerated from LinkML. ontologies/sao/shapes/*.ttl are the editable initial validation profile. scripts/build_rdf.py reads their manifests, assembles dist/sao.ttl, dist/sao.shacl.ttl, and the optional dist/sao.owl.ttl supplement, and checks freshness. It imports RDFLib, not LinkML. RDF validation uses pySHACL and these Turtle sources. The first Turtle-authority step preserved the 2.1.0 vocabulary graph. The 3.0.0 candidate now deliberately changes relationship predicates and their validation. Class IRIs and the ontology namespace remain stable. Editing Turtle changes the next distribution without editing YAML. Initial SHACL coverage The initial shapes were bootstrapped once from the resolved SAO 2.1.0 LinkML model, using a small migration translator because the standard generator stopped on contained_in_unit.inverse referring to a class-local slot. No inverse declaration was corrected or silently reinterpreted. All 147 classes have named node shapes. The initial layer contains 1,866 property shapes after inheritance, including required fields, single-value cardinality, class ranges, scalar datatypes, enum membership, inherited datatype patterns, and seven any_of constraints. Shape and property-shape IRIs are separate from domain terms. The historical counts are recorded in the bootstrap report; they do not freeze future Turtle editing. Shapes are open: extra predicates are allowed. Vocabulary hierarchy is supplied during validation, so inherited base-class targets and sh:class constraints can recognize subclasses. We do not materialize OWL inferences. Validation uses SHACL Core and performs meta-validation of the shapes themselves. Required LinkML id fields remain literal properties alongside RDF subjects. That preserves the initial constraints while their future mapping is decided. The bootstrap is not a proof that the RDF validation profile equals LinkML instance validation. What is still pending Complete internal producer/query/data migration to the proposed 3.0.0 relationship contract. The seven audited groups have candidate resolutions and the supplement now carries 217 inverse pairs; SHACL validation still does not materialize OWL inferences. Decide the closed-world validation policy and treatment of abstract classes. Define how identifier fields map to RDF subjects and how JSON/YAML inlining and mixin conventions are preserved, retired, or represented in a serialization profile. Establish validation coverage with richer positive and negative graphs, including relationship references, enum lists, alternative ranges, and subclass overrides. Decide whether documentation and downstream JSON/type generation should be driven from RDF, retained as compatibility exports, or discontinued. Add consistency checks between descriptive enum annotations and class-specific SHACL allowed-value lists. Legacy YAML and its tooling remain available as a historical comparison baseline. CI still checks that baseline on its own; it does not require authored Turtle to equal a new LinkML export. Do not remove it until the above decisions and coverage justify doing so. Commands uv run python scripts/build_rdf.py uv run python scripts/build_rdf.py --check uv run python scripts/validate_rdf.py --ontology sao examples/sao/rdf/system.ttl uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests Historical tools under scripts/migration/sao/ require explicit output locations. bootstrap_shapes.py refuses to write into an already populated directory. These are migration tools, not authoring or build commands.

entries.description: Specification & Evidence Ontology Part of the CoreStory Ontologies repository. Run commands from the repository root. SpecSpec is an RDF vocabulary for requirements, scenarios, decisions, descriptive claims, and the evidence supporting…
entries.text: SpecSpec Specification & Evidence Ontology Part of the CoreStory Ontologies repository. Run commands from the repository root. SpecSpec is an RDF vocabulary for requirements, scenarios, decisions, descriptive claims, and the evidence supporting them. Its namespace is https://ontologies.corestory.ai/specspec/ (spec:). The goal is to read existing software, lift grounded knowledge into rich specifications, and use those specifications to guide replacement implementations while retaining the evidence chain. The ontology also represents supplied intent and proposed changes. Observed behavior, intended behavior, and verification outcomes remain distinct. This is a 0.1.0 modeling draft. It does not yet implement document importers, renderers, or a modernization engine. The namespace is a proposed identifier space; this checkout does not configure hosting or CDN publication. Authoritative sources Edit the modular Turtle files under ontologies/specspec/. The layout follows SAO: RDFS vocabulary, SHACL validation, and an optional OWL supplement are separate layers. LinkML is no longer required. Directory Contents ontologies/specspec/vocabulary/ Classes, predicates, descriptions, inheritance and enum annotations ontologies/specspec/shapes/ Class/property constraints and graph rules in SHACL and SHACL-SPARQL ontologies/specspec/axioms/ Optional OWL object/datatype property declarations ontologies/specspec/bridges/sao/ Optional vocabulary, shapes and OWL declarations connecting SpecSpec to SAO ontologies/specspec/manifests/ Explicit source lists used to assemble each distribution examples/specspec/modernization/ Synthetic Turtle instance graph and supporting source fixtures scripts/ RDF assembly, validation and fixture integrity checks tests/ Migration preservation and validation regression tests Vocabulary and shape modules cover common identity/provenance, specifications, decisions, evidence, representations and the graph envelope. Graph rules live in ontologies/specspec/shapes/rules.ttl. The assembled core products are dist/specspec.ttl, dist/specspec.shacl.ttl and dist/specspec.owl.ttl. They are build outputs; edit their sources and rebuild. The three corresponding specspec-sao.*ttl products contain only the optional bridge layer and are loaded alongside the core. Core SpecSpec has no SAO dependency, and the bridge does not copy or modify SAO definitions. Important distinctions A document can describe many knowledge items and software entities. Its identity is not the identity of any one of them. Claim.origin records observed, inferred, or supplied origin. It does not establish truth. Review status and optional confidence are separate fields. Descriptive claims state existing behavior. Requirements and acceptance criteria state obligations. An observation can motivate a requirement without automatically becoming one. Evidence points into an identified source state, not a moving branch. A supporting link records support offered, not proof. Verification results refer to a specific check and snapshot. A passing result is scoped to that check. Regeneration should retain supplied intent and record contradictions for review. The ontology represents these distinctions; it does not implement a regeneration policy. See model notes, format mappings, RDF migration details, and the modernization example. Build and validate Python 3.13+, uv, RDFLib, pySHACL and owlrl provide the shared ecosystem tooling. The lockfile pins the environment. uv sync --locked uv run python scripts/build_rdf.py uv run python scripts/build_rdf.py --check uv run python scripts/validate_rdf.py uv run python scripts/validate_axioms.py uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests Assembly checks each manifest against its source directory and verifies that distributions round-trip as equivalent RDF graphs. --check detects stale distributions regardless of Turtle formatting or triple order. Validation reads the editable sources, checks the shapes against SHACL's own shapes, then checks instance conformance and local fixture integrity. It does not prove claims or execute the sample programs. To validate your own Turtle graph: uv run python scripts/validate_rdf.py --ontology specspec path/to/graph.ttl The validator requires explicitly typed SpecSpec instance nodes. RDFS class hierarchies are supplied to SHACL; optional OWL declarations are not needed for validation. The profile includes SHACL-SPARQL, so a SHACL Core-only processor cannot run every check. To check bridge endpoint types against the co-located SAO vocabulary: uv run python scripts/validate_rdf.py --ontology specspec \ --sao-vocabulary dist/sao.ttl \ --bridge-data examples/specspec/modernization/sao-links.ttl This loads the core, bridge and supplied SAO vocabulary explicitly. It checks the link endpoints against their declared types; it does not apply SAO's full instance shapes to the example's small external identity/type manifest. There are no network imports. Core validation is independent of SAO; the ecosystem profile checks the full composition. CI also exercises the narrower bridge check against a synthetic vocabulary fixture. Scope and next decisions This conversion retains the existing 21 core classes, eight enums and three bridge classes. It changes representation and tooling, with documented RDF representation differences. The proposed model expansions remain separate work. The old SpecSpec document convention is a reference for stable IDs and evidence chains, not a required output format. Existing formats can be views of this graph. Initial mappings are illustrative, not certified adapters. KnowledgeArtifact and governance classes have not been removed from SAO or migrated wholesale. SpecificationArtifact remains a distinct draft term for document representations; its eventual relationship to SAO's KnowledgeArtifact needs agreement. Compliance-specific requirements, controls, and risk assessments need a separate modeling pass. Before stabilizing: review class boundaries, decide bridge coverage and release pinning, choose representation adapters, and define provenance/review policies. Specifications and sources have their own revisions; the ontology version describes the vocabulary. SAO and SpecSpec are intended for open-source release; hosting and release hardening remain separate work. Copyright © 2026 CoreStory, Inc. Licensed under Apache License 2.0.

entries.text: Existing formats as representations These are proposed mappings for adapter design, not claims of exact equivalence, conformance, or implemented import/export support. The graph vocabulary is independent of document headings and folder conventions. External profile versions should be pinned when adapters are implemented. Convention Native concept Initial SpecSpec representation Important limit OpenSpec Current behavior specs, requirements and scenarios Specification, Requirement, Scenario, ArtifactFragment Distinguish a stated requirement from evidence that current code satisfies it. OpenSpec Change proposal, design and spec deltas ChangeProposal, Decision, RequirementReplacement Task execution and complete native delta syntax are not modeled yet. arc42 Context, building-block, runtime and deployment views SpecificationArtifact and ArtifactFragment linked through the SAO bridge Software structures belong in SAO; a view can describe many entities. arc42 Quality requirements and architecture decisions Requirement, Scenario, Decision Full quality-scenario dimensions and template section ordering are not modeled yet. MADR Context, considered options, decision and consequences Decision, DecisionOption and rationale/consequence Claim nodes Preserve native drivers, tradeoffs and prose; there is no lossless adapter yet. Old SpecSpec Stable concept IDs, origin and code anchors SpecElement IDs, Claim.origin, SourceSnapshot and EvidenceAnchor Its mandatory abstraction ladder and proprietary Markdown layout are not core ontology requirements. PRD / user-authored use-case documents Goals, requirements and interactions Specification, Requirement, UseCase, Scenario PRD is a family of conventions; identify the specific template with a RepresentationProfile. Authoritative references used for this initial mapping: OpenSpec overview: specs and change artifacts. arc42 template overview: architecture documentation views and sections. MADR template: decision context, alternatives, outcome and consequences. No external template text or code is copied into this repository. These are semantic mappings written for this draft. The old SpecSpec checkout was consulted locally as background; its normative document instructions are not adopted as instructions for this ontology.

entries.description: Statements and software SAO describes software structure and behavior. SpecSpec describes statements, obligations, decisions, and evidence about software. A normative requirement and a descriptive statement that the software implements it…
entries.text: Model notes and boundaries Statements and software SAO describes software structure and behavior. SpecSpec describes statements, obligations, decisions, and evidence about software. A normative requirement and a descriptive statement that the software implements it are separate nodes. A requirement inherits Claim so it carries statement-level provenance, review, and support. It restricts statement_mode to normative. A general Claim may be descriptive, normative, or hypothetical. AcceptanceCriterion has the same normative restriction. UseCase expresses a goal and participants; Scenario contains ordered steps and claims describing conditions and outcomes. Their prose is contextual. Assertions needing separate provenance should be Claim nodes, not buried in a document description. Evidence and identity A SourceSnapshot identifies a captured source state using an immutable revision. EvidenceAnchor locates a region within it. A filename alone is insufficient grounding. Line coordinates are one-based and inclusive. A selector can locate a non-line-oriented region. A source anchor supports or contradicts a claim. Derived claims also reference their premise claims. This provides a traversable evidence chain, but neither a link nor an origin tag establishes truth. Runtime observations can be captured as snapshots just as code can. SpecActivity records responsible agents, inputs and optional tool/model versions. Claim links back to the producing activity. Authorship and review responsibility are distinct. The current model records a review disposition, not a full append-only review history. Document representations SpecificationArtifact identifies a document. ArtifactFragment maps a section to one or more knowledge nodes. RepresentationProfile identifies an external convention. A document is not given an SAO class merely because it mentions a software component. The initial draft preserves context, rationale and consequences through dedicated fields and claim relationships. It does not attempt lossless round trips through every external format. Native text should be retained when an adapter would otherwise discard meaning. Optional bridge ontologies/specspec/bridges/sao/ owns three initial link classes: SoftwareSubjectLink, RequirementImplementationLink and VerificationTestLink. Their subject and target properties have explicit class ranges in SHACL. Both endpoints are identified references; records do not need to be nested inside one another. The software-target ranges deliberately differ: a subject link may mention any SAO NamedEntity; an implementation link currently targets CallableUnit; a verification link targets TestCase. Further link classes should state their intended range rather than weakening all links to arbitrary URIs. These link nodes preserve the draft exchange design and its qualified relationships. Core SpecSpec class names avoid colliding with SAO’s existing NamedEntity, Evidence and KnowledgeArtifact. Core manifests do not include the bridge. Optional integration explicitly loads both vocabularies and the bridge, without network imports. Draft constraints and limits SHACL checks required properties, scalar cardinality, enum values, numeric bounds, normative statement mode, and typed references. SHACL-SPARQL checks canonical identity, source anchor coordinates, claim premise cycles, observed/inferred support, confidence basis, review responsibility, scenario positions, chosen decision membership, and baseline membership for proposed requirement removals/replacements. Every knowledge node uses its identifier as its RDF subject IRI. The existing spec:id URI literal is retained and must match that IRI. Scenario step order comes from ScenarioStep.position, starting at one; Turtle triple order is irrelevant. See RDF migration details for the representation differences from the earlier record format. The fixture manifest enables content-digest and line-bound checks for local example sources. General validation cannot determine from a revision string whether an external source is truly immutable or whether an assertion is faithful to it. Evidence adequacy, confidence calibration, claim scope, semantic contradictions and behavioral equivalence require tooling and human review beyond these checks. Stabilization questions include evidence-link qualification, review history, inference activities with multiple conclusions, versioned knowledge identities, transformation plans, governance-specific classes, and external graph validation. No current field implies universal behavioral equivalence or automatic acceptance. RDFS, SHACL and OWL layers ontologies/specspec/vocabulary/ defines the vocabulary in RDFS. Reused predicates have class-specific usage constraints in SHACL. A property with several intended domains or ranges uses schema:domainIncludes or schema:rangeIncludes annotations; multiple rdfs:domain statements would infer membership in every domain. An annotation does not enforce a constraint. SHACL is the validation contract. ontologies/specspec/axioms/ supplies optional OWL object/datatype property declarations. This draft has no declared inverses, transitivity or disjointness. The conversion does not invent them. Loading the OWL supplement does not replace SHACL validation or establish that claims are true.
entries.title: Model notes and boundaries

entries.description: SpecSpec now follows SAO's source layout: modular RDFS vocabulary, SHACL shapes and graph rules, optional OWL declarations, explicit assembly manifests, and assembled Turtle distributions under dist/. The ordinary build and validation…
entries.text: Turtle source migration SpecSpec now follows SAO's source layout: modular RDFS vocabulary, SHACL shapes and graph rules, optional OWL declarations, explicit assembly manifests, and assembled Turtle distributions under dist/. The ordinary build and validation environment contains no LinkML dependency. The previous schema and generated JSON Schema/documentation paths have been removed from the active tree. This is a representation migration of the 0.1.0 draft, not the proposed ontology redesign. All 21 core classes, eight enums, three optional bridge classes, class inheritance, descriptions, property IRIs, and 29 modernization example record identities are retained. The original 257 induced class/property contracts are recorded in the migration baseline and checked against the Turtle sources by the tests. The prior authoring tree was archived outside this checkout before conversion. Representation choices Each record's identifier becomes its RDF subject IRI. The existing spec:id literal is also retained, with datatype xsd:anyURI. A SHACL-SPARQL constraint checks that it matches the subject IRI. Identical RDF triples collapse naturally; duplicated record occurrences have no separate identity in RDF. Distinct nodes cannot reuse the same canonical identifier. References become IRI objects. Class inheritance uses rdfs:subClassOf; SHACL validates the expected class of each reference using the supplied vocabulary. Missing or mistyped targets fail validation. The former inlined graph envelope becomes an explicit SpecificationGraph node referencing the same records. RDF has no nested-record ownership or array insertion order. Scenario ordering uses the existing ScenarioStep.position, with unique consecutive positions starting at one. Concrete leaf class shapes are closed to catch unknown properties. The SpecElement and Claim superclass shapes remain open so their subclass targets can carry subclass properties. The bridge's shapes are also open for combined graphs. This intentionally differs from strict JSON object field closure on standalone superclass/bridge records; it is not a claim of byte-for-byte or validation-language equivalence. Enums retain their literal values and descriptions in vocabulary annotations. SHACL sh:in lists enforce membership. Custom RDFS enum datatype declarations alone do not enforce the allowed values. Required fields, scalar cardinality, datatypes, class ranges, bounds and normative statement mode are expressed in SHACL. Cross-field and graph constraints previously implemented in Python are SHACL-SPARQL constraints in ontologies/specspec/shapes/rules.ttl. These need a processor supporting SHACL-SPARQL in addition to SHACL Core. Source-file SHA-256, path containment and file line bounds remain Python fixture checks. SHACL alone cannot compare the graph with these local files. The fixtures are synthetic and no sample program is executed. Shared properties and reasoning One predicate can be used by several classes. Class-specific ranges remain attached to the appropriate SHACL property shapes. Vocabulary terms with multiple intended domains/ranges use schema:domainIncludes / schema:rangeIncludes annotations to avoid accidental intersection inference. These annotations are descriptive; SHACL supplies the constraints. The OWL supplement classifies properties as object or datatype properties. No inverse, transitive, disjointness or behavioral-equivalence axioms are introduced. The ontology version remains 0.1.0 because this remains the same unpublished modeling draft; release/version policy still needs agreement. Composition and validation The manifests enumerate local Turtle files; the builder merges their triples and checks coverage and graph-equivalent round trips. Each core layer has its own manifest. The bridge has three additional manifests and distributions containing only bridge definitions. It depends on the core and an explicitly supplied SAO vocabulary. Nothing is fetched through owl:imports. The validator reads source modules so it cannot silently validate stale distributions. scripts/build_rdf.py --check separately verifies that shipped distributions match those sources. It rejects graphs without explicitly typed SpecSpec instance nodes, avoiding an empty-target success. The tests check the captured class/property contracts, enum membership, class descriptions and inheritance, build equivalence, independent core, invalid typed references, provenance/review rules, decision and baseline membership, scenario order, identity, and fixture integrity. Bridge checks use a synthetic SAO vocabulary in CI; a real SAO vocabulary can be supplied separately. They validate endpoint types rather than the full SAO instance profile. Full model equivalence across all possible future RDF entailments is not asserted. The representation choices above make the differences explicit while retaining the current draft's modeled information and validation intent.

headings.title: What is an ontology, in plain language?
Follow one behavior: reject an overdraft

entries.text: Before the graph: tell the system’s story You do not need to know RDF to understand the idea. Start with a familiar problem: someone needs to change a system, but the code, requirements, and reasons for past decisions tell different parts of its story. An ontology gives those parts shared names and explicit relationships. It helps you say which software, which requirement, which claim, and which evidence you mean. It does not make the story true merely by organizing it. One system. Different questions. Imagine four people looking at the same change: Reader The question they need answered An agent What must this change preserve, and what evidence should I inspect? A product manager What behavior do we require, and what has not been verified? An engineer Where is that behavior implemented, and what does the source show? An executive What decision is proposed, and what uncertainty remains? The goal is not four unrelated summaries. It is different explanations that return to the same identities, statements, and evidence. These are questions the model can help you organize—not a claim that this repository generates four product experiences. What is an ontology, in plain language? Think of a shared map legend. A team agrees what counts as a road, a station, or a boundary, and how those things can connect. The legend does not survey the land; it gives people a consistent way to describe it. For software, the named things might be a system, a callable, a requirement, or a decision. A relationship says something specific: a claim cites a source anchor; an anchor belongs to a captured source state. A graph is those things and their connections. It need not look like a complicated network diagram. A table showing “this claim cites this source” already conveys the relationship. Why two ontologies? SAO—the Systems Abstraction Ontology—describes the software. Its vocabulary includes systems, modules, callables, domain concepts, and operating context. SpecSpec—the Specification & Evidence Ontology—describes statements about it. Its vocabulary includes requirements, claims, decisions, source evidence, and verification results. The distinction protects meaning: A method is not a requirement. A statement about behavior is not the behavior itself. A source citation is not proof that the statement is correct. A proposed decision is not an accepted decision. An optional bridge connects particular knowledge items to particular software entities. The models remain distinct, and SpecSpec can be used without SAO. Follow one behavior: reject an overdraft The repository includes a synthetic example, not a customer case or an executed modernization. A COBOL excerpt and a proposed Java replacement both contain an amount-versus-balance guard. The graph keeps the following records separate: Part of the story What the example records Observation The legacy excerpt displays a rejection when the requested amount exceeds the balance. The claim is marked observed and unreviewed. Requirement The replacement shall reject excessive withdrawals without reducing the balance. This is supplied intent, not an obligation automatically discovered in code. Decision Use a Java guard; the decision remains proposed. Implementation assertion An explicit link relates the requirement to the Java callable, with a separate descriptive claim as its basis. Evidence That Java claim cites an anchor at Account.java:5–8, within a captured source snapshot. Verification The behavioral comparison is not_run. It is not a pass. Now ask the same questions from different seats. Product can inspect the required behavior. Engineering can inspect the guard. An agent can identify an unverified obligation. An executive can see that a decision is proposed and the comparison remains unrun. The answer’s level of detail can change. Its evidence and status must not. A shorter executive explanation must not turn not_run into “verified.” Read the worked example when you want the full source context, or follow the modeling patterns to see the exact relationships. What the technical layers do You can learn these names when you need them: Name Plain-language job Turtle A text syntax for writing the graph. RDFS vocabulary Names the classes, properties, and class relationships. SHACL validation Checks whether supplied data meets the declared constraints. Optional OWL supplements Add declared reasoning relationships for consumers that choose to use them. Validation can catch a missing field or an invalid relationship endpoint. It cannot establish that a source really supports a claim, that a change is safe, or that two programs behave identically. Those need separate evidence and review. Your first useful step Choose one behavior, not the whole estate. Write down what you observe, what you require, what decision is proposed, and what remains unchecked. Identify the source state behind each observation. Then choose a next step: Understand the vocabulary: read the SAO overview and SpecSpec model notes. Inspect the example: follow the modeling patterns, without installing anything. Run a real check: use getting started to validate the bundled graph with Nix or uv. SAO 3.0.0 is a candidate, and SpecSpec 0.1.0 is a draft. The repository supplies models, validation tooling, and examples—not an automatic modernization service. See the catalog and model boundaries before depending on a particular version.
entries.title: Before the graph: tell the system’s story

entries.text: A source-grounded modernization example All sources, agents, and results here are synthetic fixtures, not production evidence. The COBOL and Java files are illustrative excerpts, not complete executable modernization targets. Follow these distinct identities in graph.ttl: legacy-behavior describes the old guard and cites an immutable source snapshot and line anchor. no-overdraft records supplied intent to preserve it. The descriptive observation does not automatically become an obligation. modernization-decision records a proposed implementation choice and its rationale. modern-behavior describes the Java guard with a separate anchor and snapshot. comparison-result records not_run. Matching a guard does not establish whole-program equivalence. spec-document represents multiple knowledge items; it is not the software callable itself. The normative acceptance criterion is deliberately separated from the observed Java behavior. The example does not infer successful modernization from either one. sources.json maps snapshots to local fixture files so validation can check their SHA-256 digests and anchor bounds. sao-links.ttl contains an optional typed implementation link plus an external identity/type manifest. That manifest is not a complete SAO graph; bridge validation checks link types against the supplied manifest and core graph, not the existence or correctness of a production software graph. The Turtle graph preserves the original 29 record identities and adds an explicit SpecificationGraph envelope linking the collections. Records are IRI nodes; relationships are RDF references. ScenarioStep.position supplies sequence order. From the repository root, run uv run python scripts/validate_rdf.py to check SHACL conformance, fixture digests and anchor bounds. The Python check reads only the local files listed in sources.json; the example.org identifiers are not fetched.

The current SAO 3.0.0 candidate is authored in Turtle under ontologies/sao/; SpecSpec is authored under ontologies/specspec/. The legacy model is intentionally not relabeled as the newer RDF contract.
